# What the integration hub implements of the EHDS Regulation

The European Health Data Space is [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32025R0327).
This page says, article by article, what the integration hub implements of it:
the page, the route or the file that does it, the test that shows it, and
where it falls short, with the issue that tracks the gap. Article numbers are
the adopted ones; older material in the repository may cite the [2022 proposal](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52022PC0197),
and [the numbering reference](/docs/ehds/article-numbering) maps one to the
other.

The hub is a demonstrator on synthetic data. It plays the roles of the
Regulation (a data holder, a data user, an access body, a trust centre, a
person) with fictional organisations; it is not an access body and holds no
real person's data.

Checked against the code on 2026-10-27 ([#694](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/694)). Status:

- **Implemented**: the duty is carried out end to end and a test shows it.
- **Partial**: part of it is there; the gap column says what is missing.
- **Not yet**: nothing does it; the issue says when.

([Art. 7](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_7)(3)) is `DELETE /api/patient/research`; erasure ([Art. 17](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_17)) exists for
accounts the Klarbefund app created; rectification ([Art. 16](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_16)) is limited to the
person's health interests; restriction, objection and automated decisions
([Art. 18](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_18), [21](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_21), [22](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_22)) are not implemented. The EHDS opt-out of [Art. 71](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_71) is the
objection to secondary use.

## Keeping this page true

The page is checked against the code, not written from the plan. When a
change moves an article, change its row in the same pull request, with the
test that shows it. The checks behind the rows:

- [`./scripts/run-ehds-tests.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-tests.sh): the graph, the catalogue, OMOP, the opt-out.
- [`./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Local`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-api-tests.sh): the Bruno collection, one folder per
  role of the Regulation.
- `cd ui && npm test` and `npm run test:e2e`: the routes, the pages and the
  journeys named above.

docs.markdown:
# EHDS article numbering: proposal vs adopted

Most EHDS article references in this repository are the numbers from the 2022
proposal, [COM(2022) 197 final](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52022PC0197). The Regulation was renumbered before adoption, and
the adopted numbers in [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng) are different, in places by more
than twenty.

This matters in one specific room. A regulator who knows the Regulation reads
"secure processing environment, Art. 50" and sees [Art. 50](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_50) of the adopted text,
which is _Applicability to health data holders_. The claim looks wrong even
though the substance is right.

**New material uses the adopted numbers.** Existing material has not been
rewritten: roughly 48 files carry proposal numbers, and a mass renumber before a
demo is the kind of change that quietly breaks something. Use this table when
reading them, and correct a file whenever you are editing it anyway.

## Chapter IV, secondary use

docs.title: Bonus programme: which data goes where
docs.summary: AlphaKasse's bonus programme from the catalogue to the yes or no: who takes part, every step, what the hub stores, what crosses to the insurer and what never does, the legal basis, and how to check it.
docs.markdown:
# Bonus programme: which data goes where AlphaKasse DE, a fictional statutory health insurer in a second data space ("insurance and wellbeing"), offers a bonus to members who stay active through the year and go to their yearly check-up. This page follows one member through the programme. It covers what the hub reads, what it stores, what crosses to the insurer, and what never does. The design decision is [ADR-080](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-080-a-bonus-programme-receives-a-yes-or-no-never-the-data.md); the plan is [#934](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/934). ## In short - **Today (steps 3, 4 and 6 of #934), no data about the member reaches AlphaKasse.** The hub reads AlphaKasse's catalogue, the member joins in the patient portal or in the Klarbefund app, sees their own result for the ended year, and "Send my answer" records the year and goal met inside the hub. It is delivered in step 8, or through the member's wallet. - **When it is delivered, AlphaKasse receives three things:** the programme, the year, and "goal met: yes" or "no". - **It never receives** steps, minutes of activity, heart rate, diagnoses, visit details, or any date finer than the year (ADR-080, decision 2). ## Who takes part | Party | Role | Where it runs | | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | The member (patient1 in the demo) | Decides: joins, sends, withdraws | Patient portal, `/patient/programmes`, or the Klarbefund app (Connect to EHDS) | | The hub (MVHD) | Reads the catalogue, keeps the consent, will compute the answer | `ehds.mabu.red` | | AlphaKasse DE (`did:web:alphakasse.de:insurer`) | Publishes the programme, will receive the yes or no | A catalogue served for it by the hub's mock DSP route, standing in for its own connector | | The catalogue crawler and enricher | Fetch the catalogue every 5 minutes and index the programme | Azure Container Apps jobs `mvhd-catalog-crawler`, `mvhd-catalog-enricher` | ## The process ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant AK as AlphaKasse DE (catalogue) participant CR as Catalogue crawler participant EN as Enricher participant G as Hub graph (Neo4j) participant M as Member (patient portal) participant H as Hub API AK->>AK: publishes "Active year bonus 2025" (DCAT-AP, rule 2025.1) CR->>AK: POST /catalog/request (empty query, crawler DID) AK-->>CR: catalogue: programme, rule, publisher CR->>EN: catalogue via NATS EN->>G: (:DataService:BonusProgramme) M->>H: GET /api/patient/programmes H-->>M: the programme, its rule, my consents M->>H: POST /consent (join) H->>G: (:ProgrammeConsent) open M->>H: GET /evaluation {programme, 2025} H->>G: 2025's exercise weeks and check-ups, summed H-->>M: goal met yes or no, and the breakdown (member only) M->>H: POST /transfer {programme, 2025} H->>G: (:ProgrammeTransfer) year, goal met M->>H: DELETE /consent (withdraw) H->>G: consent closed, withdrawal date set M->>H: POST /transfer again H-->>M: 403, nothing recorded Note over H,AK: Step 8: the yes or no goes to AlphaKasse over a DSP agreement,
or the member presents it from the EUDI Wallet. ``` 1. **AlphaKasse publishes the programme.** Its catalogue is DCAT-AP 3.0.1, not HealthDCAT-AP, because a bonus programme is not a health dataset ([`alphakasse-dcat-ap.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/content/catalogues/alphakasse-dcat-ap.json)). The programme is for 2025 and is claimed once that year is over ([ADR-087](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-087-the-hub-evaluates-a-bonus-year-once-it-has-ended.md), decision 1). It is a `dcat:DataService`. Its rule is a versioned `dct:Standard` (`owl:versionInfo` 2025.1), so the member and the insurer read the same rule (ADR-080, decision 3). The PR Gate validates the file against the DCAT-AP SHACL. 2. **The crawler fetches it.** Every 5 minutes it sends AlphaKasse's `dspCatalogUrl` an empty DSP catalogue request ([`EMPTY_QUERY_SPEC`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/a1c78c3e/services/catalog-crawler/src/dsp_client.py#L22)) with the crawler's DID. That request carries nothing about any person. 3. **The enricher indexes it** as `(:DataService:BonusProgramme)`, with the rule and the publisher ([`extract_services`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/a1c78c3e/services/catalog-enricher/src/mapping.py#L182)). Node labels come from a fixed list in the hub, never from the catalogue. 4. **The member sees it** on `/patient/programmes`, apart from research and from the opt-out. The card shows the rule, what AlphaKasse receives and what never leaves the record. In the Klarbefund app the same list is under Connect to EHDS, then Bonus programs, in the portal's words. The app calls `/api/patient/app/programmes` and its `consent` and `transfer` routes, the app-token twins of the portal's routes (ADR-049): the same queries and answers, the login's own record only, and a join from the phone is recorded with `source: "klarbefund"`. The app keeps the programme apart from its Consents screen, which notes a study consent, an ePA objection and a registry consent held by others (ADR-080, decision 6). 5. **The member joins.** The hub writes an open `(:ProgrammeConsent)` on the member's own record ([`JOIN_PROGRAMME_CYPHER`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/a1c78c3e/ui/src/lib/patient/programme-consent.ts#L32)). It is consent to this programme alone (GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)). It enrolls the member in no study, and it is separate from the Art. 71 opt-out. 6. **The hub works out the year, and the member sees it first.** Once 2025 has ended, the hub reads that year inside the member's record ([`programme-rule.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient/programme-rule.ts)): the weekly exercise means the tracker shared (LOINC 55411-3, minutes a day, times seven, summed over 52 weeks, a week without any counting as none) and the check-up (an Encounter coded SNOMED CT 185349003). The query returns three sums and nothing finer. The member sees goal met, yes or no, with the minutes a week, the weeks shared and the check-ups; that breakdown is for the member only. Before the year ends the screen says so, and nothing can be sent. 7. **The member asks the hub to send the year's answer.** The hub checks for an open consent ([`programmeTransferAllowed`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/a1c78c3e/ui/src/lib/patient/programme-consent.ts#L128)), that the rule covers the year (400 otherwise) and that it has ended (409 otherwise), works the year out again, and records a `(:ProgrammeTransfer)` with the programme, the year and goal met, status `evaluated` ([`RECORD_TRANSFER_CYPHER`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient/programme-consent.ts)). Nothing leaves the hub at this point. 8. **The member withdraws.** The consent gets its withdrawal date and stays on record with both dates (GDPR Art. 7(3)). 9. **After the withdrawal nothing is sent.** The same instruction is refused with 403, and nothing is recorded ([transfer route](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/a1c78c3e/ui/src/app/api/patient/programmes/transfer/route.ts#L59)). Every later delivery path, the DSP agreement and the wallet alike, has to pass the same gate. **The agreement AlphaKasse has to reach first (step 5).** AlphaKlinik offers the answer under the policy `mvhd-bonus-programme` ([`standard-policies.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/standard-policies.ts), [ADR-090](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-090-the-connector-admits-only-an-attested-bonus-payout-purpose.md)): use for the bonus payout only; no insurance decision, profiling, advertising or decision to the member's detriment; delete after the payout. The hub's connector decides one of its terms itself, `ehds:attestedPurpose`: AlphaKasse reaches the agreement only when its `DataProcessingPurposeCredential`, issued by the insurance and wellbeing authority, attests the purpose `bonus-payout`. A credential that attests "premium-setting" is refused with 400, "Policy in scope contract.negotiation not fulfilled". Step 8 delivers the yes or no over that agreement, or the member presents it from the EUDI Wallet. ## What is stored, and where | Record | Fields | Written when | Read by | | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `(:DataService:BonusProgramme)` | programme id, title, description, publisher, endpoint, themes, keywords, rule title, rule text, rule version, last seen | Each crawl | Patients and operators (`/api/patient/programmes`), the app (`/api/patient/app/programmes`) | | `(:ProgrammeConsent)` | consent id, patient id, programme id, joined at, withdrawn at, source | Join, withdraw | The member, and an operator who names the record | | `(:ProgrammeTransfer)` | transfer id, patient id, programme id, year, goal met, status `evaluated`, requested at | "Send my answer", only under an open consent | The member, and an operator who names the record | A patient reads and changes only their own record; naming another record is refused with 403 (`refuseForeignRecord`). `source` is `patient-portal`, `klarbefund` or `api-collection`. The API collection marks its own test consents so that the live clean-up removes them and nothing else ([`remove-api-collection-runs.cypher`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/neo4j/remove-api-collection-runs.cypher), section 3). ## What crosses between the hub and AlphaKasse | Direction | What | About a person? | | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | | Hub to AlphaKasse | The crawler's catalogue request: an empty query and the crawler's DID | No | | AlphaKasse to hub | The catalogue: programme, rule, publisher | No | | Hub to AlphaKasse, today | Nothing | n/a | | Hub to AlphaKasse, after step 8 | Programme, year, goal met yes or no, tied to the member reference AlphaKasse already holds | Yes, and nothing more | ## The legal basis - **Primary use the person directs.** "Primary use" includes reimbursement services ([EHDS Art. 2(2)(d)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#002.002)), and a person may have part of their data transmitted to a recipient in the social security or reimbursement sector ([Art. 7(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#007.003)). That fits a statutory insurer's bonus; for a private insurer only the GDPR consent applies, and the use case needs its own review (ADR-080, decision 1). - **Explicit consent** to the one programme ([GDPR Art. 9](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_9)(2)(a)), withdrawable at any time ([Art. 7](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_7)(3)). - **The line not crossed.** Secondary use may not be used to exclude people from insurance or change their premiums ([EHDS Art. 54](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_54)(b)). The bonus only rewards: a "no" changes nothing in the member's contract. Evaluating whether the programme works is secondary use and needs a permit from the access body (step 9). - **Data minimisation** ([GDPR Art. 5](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_5)(1)(c)): a yes or no per year, not the data behind it. AlphaKasse DE is fictional. Before a real insurer runs this, national bonus rules apply to it (in Germany § 65a SGB V), and the design needs a legal review. ## Check it yourself - **In the portal:** sign in as patient1, open My Health, then Bonus Programs. Join; "Your result for 2025" shows "Goal met: yes" with about 181 minutes a week from 52 weeks and one check-up. Send ("Recorded for 2025: goal met, yes"), withdraw ("Nothing is sent any more"). patient2 sees "Goal met: no": about 78 minutes a week from 48 weeks. - **In Klarbefund:** connect the app (Connect to EHDS), open Bonus programs, join, read the result, send, withdraw. Exercise minutes reach the record once "Send my device trends" is on. Without a phone, `cd clients/ios && Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh BonusProgrammesUITests` runs the same steps against the demo hub (`-MBDemoSeed`, `-MBShot programmes`), and `swift test --filter BonusProgrammes` pins how the app reads the answers, the 403 after a withdrawal among them. - **API collection:** `bruno/MVHDv2/01 Patient/22` to `27` list the programme, join, send (202, the year and goal met only), withdraw, send again (403), and read the member's result. `09 Access control/40` to `44` refuse the app routes without the app's token (401). - **Browser journeys:** J1092, J1094 and J1099 in [`54-bonus-programmes.spec.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/__tests__/e2e/journeys/54-bonus-programmes.spec.ts). They skip with a reason on a stack where the crawler has not run. - **The bonus policy at the connector (compose, JAD stack seeded):** `./scripts/seed-second-data-space.sh` then `./scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh`; PURPOSE-7.1 to 7.4 negotiate the offer with the bonus payout purpose (agreed), without a purpose (refused), with "premium-setting" (refused by `ehds:attestedPurpose`) and with the bonus payout purpose again (agreed). - **The catalogue against DCAT-AP:** `python3 scripts/healthdcat-ap/validate.py ui/src/content/catalogues/alphakasse-dcat-ap.json --dcat-ap`. - **The records in the graph:** ```cypher MATCH (p:Patient)-[:GAVE_PROGRAMME_CONSENT]->(c:ProgrammeConsent)-[:FOR_PROGRAMME]->(b:BonusProgramme) OPTIONAL MATCH (t:ProgrammeTransfer)-[:UNDER_CONSENT]->(c) RETURN b.title, c.joinedAt, c.withdrawnAt, c.source, collect(t {.year, .goalMet, .status}) ``` ## Done - Step 3: the crawled DCAT-AP programme on `/patient/programmes` (#1005). - Step 4: join, send and withdraw in the portal, and the transfer gate (#1014). - Klarbefund: the app's join, send and withdraw screen (`source: "klarbefund"`) (#1036). - Step 6: the hub works out goal met for an ended year inside the record, and the member sees it before sending; Klarbefund sends exercise minutes ([ADR-087](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-087-the-hub-evaluates-a-bonus-year-once-it-has-ended.md)). - Step 5: the bonus programme policy, its purpose decided by the hub's connector against the insurer's purpose credential ([ADR-090](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-090-the-connector-admits-only-an-attested-bonus-payout-purpose.md)). ## Open - The achievement attestation for the EUDI Wallet (ADR-080, decision 4, after #708). - Step 8: delivery to AlphaKasse's connector, which needs a `simpl-edc` with DCP. The member reference AlphaKasse ties the answer to is designed there.

docs.title: TEHDAS2: what the hub implements
docs.summary: The 21 TEHDAS2 guidelines and specifications against the hub, after a requirement-by-requirement check: what it implements, where it stops on purpose, and the issue that closes each gap.
docs.markdown:
# TEHDAS2: what the hub implements

TEHDAS2, the Joint Action that prepares the EHDS, has written 21 guidelines and
technical specifications for health data access bodies, data holders and data
users: 14 final ([results by user group](https://tehdas.eu/results-by-user-group/))
and 7 wave-3 drafts from the
[third public consultation](https://tehdas.eu/public-consultations/). This page
says, for each one, what the integration hub implements, where it stops, and
which issue closes the gap. Its
[final conference](https://tehdas.eu/event/tehdas2-final-conference/) is on
16 November 2026 in Brussels and online.

The decisions behind it are
[ADR-083](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-083-what-the-hub-takes-over-from-tehdas2.md)
(what the hub takes over) and
[ADR-086](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-086-tehdas2-ratings-after-the-requirement-check.md)
(the ratings after the requirement check). The work is epic
[#990](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/990).

## In short

- **Of the 21 documents, the hub implements 4, covers 15 in part and does not
  cover 2** (D8.2 significant findings, and the return of enriched data).
- The guidance is not law. Regulation (EU) 2025/327 and its implementing acts
  come first; TEHDAS2 applies where they leave the how open.
- Nine documents were checked requirement by requirement on 2026-11-09, every
  row linked to the code that shows it: reports for
  [D5.1 to D6.3](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/991#issuecomment-6745762566),
  [linkage and research outcomes](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/991#issuecomment-6745763337),
  [D7.1 to D8.1](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/991#issuecomment-6745821939)
  and [D6.4 DAAMS](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/992#issuecomment-6745694280).
- The wave-3 rows rest on the May 2026 drafts and are rated again once the
  final versions are published
  ([#997](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/997)).

## The final documents

| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [D4.1 Fees and penalties](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/d4.1-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-fees-and-penalties-for-non-compliance-related-to-the-ehds-regulation.pdf)                                                         | Implemented | Fees and fines on the access body's desk                                                                           | Amounts are fictional; fines are recorded, not collected                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [D5.1 Data description](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/guideline-for-data-holders-on-data-description.pdf)                                                                                                                                 | Implemented | HealthDCAT-AP Release 8, validated in CI against the official SHACL                                                | D5.1's stricter properties for sensitive data: geographical coverage, collection purpose, language, publisher type                                                           | [#1033](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/1033), [#697](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/697)                                                                            |
| [D5.2 Minimum categories and limitations](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/d5.2-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-minimum-categories-and-limitations-on-the-reuse-of-health-data.pdf)                                               | Partial     | Purposes and prohibitions as policy terms                                                                          | Art. 54 prohibitions are not checked on the application                                                                                                                      | [#717](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/717)                                                                                                                                                         |
| [D5.3 National metadata catalogue](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/technical-specification-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-the-national-metadata-catalogue.pdf)                                                                            | Partial     | Catalogue and federated discovery                                                                                  | Public access and EU harvesting, trusted holders in the catalogue, version history, the holder's yearly review                                                               | [#714](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/714), [#697](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/697)                                                                              |

| [D7.2 Minimisation, pseudonymisation, synthetic data](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/d7.2-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-data-minimisation-pseudonymisation-anonymisation-and-synthetic-data.pdf)                              | Partial     | Suppression of groups under five                                                                                   | Generalisation and synthetic data; a pseudonym per project                                                                                                                   | [#999](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/999), [#475](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/475)                                                                              |
| [D7.3 Common IT infrastructure](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/d7.3-technical-specification-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-the-implementation-of-the-common-it-infrastructure.pdf)                                                       | Partial     | Federated discovery, the query proxy                                                                               | No national contact point, no eDelivery; deferred until the Art. 75 implementing act                                                                                         | [#713](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/713)                                                                                                                                                         |
| [D7.4 SPE specification](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/d7.4-technical-specification-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-the-implementation-of-secure-processing-environments.pdf)                                                            | Partial     | Confidential containers: a sealed extract, a key released only to attested hardware, logs kept 12 months           | Strong identification and MFA, a workspace per person and permit, the export review, the remote desktop                                                                      | [#716](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/716), [#1030](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/1030), [#587](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/587) |
| [D8.1 Opt-out](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/d8.1-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-implementing-opt-out-from-the-secondary-use-of-health-data.pdf)                                                                              | Implemented | Opt-out without a reason, reversal, history, confirmation, the Art. 71(4) exception, the filter in the query proxy | The Art. 71(3) permit-date rule, other holders, the activity report's count                                                                                                  | [#696](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/696), [#1032](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/1032)                                                                            |
| [D8.2 Significant findings](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/d8.2-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-implementing-the-obligation-of-notifying-the-natural-person-on-a-significant-finding-from-the-secondary-use-of-health-data.pdf) | Not covered | Only a policy duty to report an incident                                                                           | The path from a finding to the person                                                                                                                                        | [#996](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/996)                                                                                                                                                         |

## The wave-3 drafts

| Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Status                               | Where in the hub                                                                                         | What is missing                                                                          | Issues                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Framework for collaboration](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-on-a-framework-for-collaboration.pdf)                                                                                     | Partial                              | Policies, participant onboarding                                                                         | Ethics review and IP protection are not modelled; not taken over now                     |                                                                                                                                                      |
| [Third-country access and transfer](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-international-and-third-country-access-and-transfer-of-electronic-health-data.pdf) | Partial                              | Transfers outside the EU/EEA refused by policy                                                           | No application path for applicants outside it; not taken over now                        |                                                                                                                                                      |
| [Data enrichment](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-for-data-enrichment.pdf)                                                                                                              | Not covered                          | Technical enrichment only (FHIR to OMOP, terminologies)                                                  | Returning enriched datasets to the access body                                           | [#998](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/998)                                                                            |
| [Navigating the catalogue](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-for-data-users-navigating-the-catalogue.pdf)                                                                                 | Partial                              | Catalogue, federated discovery, natural-language queries                                                 | No connection to HealthData@EU                                                           | [#713](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/713)                                                                            |
| [Linkage of datasets](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-linkage-of-health-datasets.pdf)                                                                  | Partial                              | Research pseudonyms in the trust centre                                                                  | The linking process itself (method, validation, quality report); a pseudonym per project | [#475](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/475), [#587](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/587) |
| [Citizen Information Point](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-for-health-data-access-bodies-on-informing-natural-persons-about-the-use-of-health-dataxxxcitizen-information-point-.pdf)   | Partial                              | The information page                                                                                     | It needs a sign-in, so a citizen cannot read it                                          | [#995](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/995)                                                                            |
| [Handling research outcomes](https://tehdas.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/draft-guideline-for-data-users-on-handling-research-outcomes.pdf)                                                                          | Implemented for Art. 61(4) reporting | Results reported under the permit, 18-month deadline, on the information page and in the activity report | The review before export; significant findings                                           | [#716](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/716), [#996](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/996) |

## Where the hub deviates on purpose

- **A query SPE.** D7.1 and D7.4 describe a workspace a user logs into, with a
  remote desktop. The hub's secure processing environment answers queries:
  the proxy asks the workspaces, and only aggregates leave. The confidential
  containers go beyond what D7.4 asks for the protection of the data.
- **Opted-out persons in extracts.** An extract for a workspace carries an
  opted-out person with a label rather than leaving them out; the query proxy
  filters them before any answer leaves.
- **A trusted data holder decides data requests itself.** D6.4 has the holder
  propose and the access body decide.

## Check it yourself

- The catalogue against HealthDCAT-AP Release 8, as the PR Gate runs it:
  `python3 scripts/healthdcat-ap/validate.py services/neo4j-proxy/__tests__/fixtures/healthdcat-ap-r8.jsonld`.
- The application, the decision and the permit: sign in as `researcher`, then
  as `regulator`, on `/applications`, `/compliance` and `/permits`.
- The opt-out: sign in as `patient1` and opt out on `/patient/research`; the query proxy
  leaves the person out of every answer.
- The roadmap of this work:
  [/docs/roadmap, epic #990](https://ma3u.github.io/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/docs/roadmap#e990).

docs.title: Klarbefund user guide
docs.summary: The app as a person uses it, screen by screen with screenshots: getting a report in, checking a value against the paper, trends, consents, connecting to the EHDS, exports and your data rights.
docs.markdown: # Klarbefund user guide Klarbefund turns a paper lab report into values you can read, check against the paper, and follow over time. Everything runs on the phone: the scan, the reading, the coding, the store and the exports. Nothing needs an account, and nothing leaves the device unless you send it. This guide walks through the app as a person uses it, task by task. The developer side (building, testing, the shared dictionary, the store layout) is the [developer guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-developer-guide). The work is tracked in [issue #186](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186). Every screenshot in this guide shows invented data. The laboratory, the practice, the patient and every number come from the app's own fictional development dataset, so a screenshot can be published without a real report ever being involved. How they are made is at the [end of this guide](#how-these-screenshots-are-made). | App name | Klarbefund, in English and German | | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Runs on | iPhone, iOS 26 or later | | Get it | [Public TestFlight beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/ssADSXX6), 200 places | | Languages | English and German, following the phone's language | | Source | [`clients/ios/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios) | | Privacy | [Privacy policy](https://ma3u.github.io/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/meinbefund/privacy.html) | | Not | a medical device: it explains what a measurement is and never judges a value ([below](#not-a-medical-device)) | ## Getting started 1. On the iPhone, open the [TestFlight link](https://testflight.apple.com/join/ssADSXX6). [TestFlight](https://developer.apple.com/testflight/) installs itself first if it is missing, then offers Klarbefund. 2. Open Klarbefund. There is no sign-up and no account: the app is ready for the first scan. 3. The first time you scan, iOS asks for the camera. The app uses it only for the pages of a report and for the QR code that connects it to your record; the photographs stay on the phone. **The lock.** By default the app asks for [Face ID](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/localauthentication), Touch ID or the passcode every time it comes to the front, so your results are not on show to whoever holds the unlocked phone. The switch is under **Analysis provider** in the **⋯** menu, section **Protection**. A phone without a passcode has nothing to ask for, and the lock then opens by itself ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)). ## Your reports The home screen lists every report, newest first: the title, the laboratory, practice or device it came from, the date it was taken and how many values were read. **1 to review** marks a report with a value you have not yet checked against the paper. The coloured badge is the report's **provenance**, and it matters more than it looks. **Lab-issued, final** means the values came out of a PDF that carried the laboratory's own text, so nothing was guessed. **Scanned, preliminary** means the values were read from a photograph, of a paper sheet or of a device's screen, and a photograph can be misread. A value stays preliminary until you have checked it against the original. The top of the list has what belongs to looking at your reports: **Trends**, **My EHDS record** with the state of your connection, and **Possible duplicates** when two reports look like the same one. The **+** button starts a scan, an import, or **Earlier measurements** entered by hand. The **⋯** button holds settings and your rights over your data, in three groups: _About you_ (profile, reference values), _Privacy and sharing_ (consents, analysis provider, privacy and safety) and _Your data_ (export, delete, and under _Research and support_ the OMOP export and the diagnostics). ## Getting a report in There are three ways, and the document decides what its values are worth. - **Scan report** opens the camera for a paper report. The app finds the page edges, reads the table on the device, and keeps the pages as a PDF next to the values. Multi-page reports are fine. - **Import a PDF or photo** takes a file your laboratory or portal gave you. If the PDF carries the laboratory's own text layer, the values are marked final; a PDF that is only a picture goes through the recogniser like a scan. - **Import from Photos** takes photographs already on the phone, up to twelve at a time. The app reads more than laboratory sheets. A **24-hour blood pressure measurement**, a **resting or exercise ECG**, a **Holter report**, a **spirometry**, a **lactate test**, a **CGM glucose profile**, a **DXA scan** and a **gut microbiome analysis** each have their own reader, so the values a practice prints on those sheets arrive with the right codes and units. A **body-composition scale** photographed in a gym is recognised as what it is: a dashboard, not a report. The app reads the metric, its current value and the date the scale shows, and where the scale plots a history it measures the points on the chart and marks those values as estimates. The scale's own verdicts ("Normal", "Low") are ignored; they are the manufacturer's bands, not a guideline's. Before anything is saved, the app shows what it read and asks you to confirm the laboratory date it found on the sheet. A report that looks like one you already have is pointed out; **Possible duplicates**, at the top of the list, appears whenever two stored reports look like the same one. ## Checking a report, value by value The top of a report is what the app read from the sheet's header: the laboratory, the date the sample was taken, the date the report was issued, the report number, and a link to the original pages. Then every measurement, and under each one the four things that make it checkable: - **the LOINC code** it was matched to, so the value means the same thing in every system it is exported to. The unit picks the code, never the name: lipoprotein(a) in mg/dL and in nmol/L are different measurements with different codes. A quantity LOINC does not code says so plainly instead of showing a near-enough code, and an organism from a stool report shows its [NCBI Taxonomy](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy) id instead, because LOINC names tests and not organisms; - **the reference range your laboratory printed**, exactly as printed, never normalised; - **the page and line** it was read from, so any number can be checked against the paper in front of you; - **the published band**, where a guideline or a named study states one ([ADR-039](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-039-published-reference-ranges.md)), with the words and a symbol beside the colour: "in the optimal band", "outside the optimal band", "outside the guideline range". This is a comparison to a number somebody published. It is not a finding. **Checking against the paper.** Tap a value to correct its name, number or unit; the correction is kept beside what the recogniser read, so the paper trail stays. **Mark all values as checked** turns the report's values from preliminary into checked once you have compared them. A report with values still to check carries **to review** in the list. Below the recognised values come two lists the app never hides: the lines that looked like measurements but matched nothing in the dictionary, and the lines that could not be read at all. A row that vanished silently would be indistinguishable from a row that was never printed, so no row vanishes. **Report missing values** in the report's menu sends the developers the labels of such rows, never the values, so the dictionary can grow. The share button offers the exports described further down. The menu lets you read the report again with the current version of the reader, scan the paper again, edit its name and laboratory, export its diagnostics, or delete it. ## The original pages Every report keeps its pages, as one PDF, encrypted like the values. **Original scan** shows them back, so the source is always one tap away from the reading. ## Trends **Trends** draws one chart per measurement across every report, ordered by what is furthest from its range. The filters narrow it to what matters: only analytes measured more than once, or only those outside a band. Each chart says what it is showing. Every kind of evidence has its own shape: a circle came from a laboratory's own file, a diamond was read from a photograph and is preliminary, and a triangle was entered by you or taken from a device. A legend under every chart that mixes them names each shape in words, so nothing depends on colour or on tapping a point. The green band is the published optimal band where one exists; for everything else the band drawn is the range your own laboratory printed, in its own colour and named as such. Under the chart every point is listed with its date, where it came from and which report it belongs to, and tapping a point opens that report. A sentence under each chart says **what the measurement is**: a definition of the test, in English or German. It is never a reading of your own value. At the bottom, **Show trends from [Apple Health](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit)** reads your resting heart rate, heart rate variability, steps and weight, after asking once for permission. They appear in their own section, **From your devices**, as grey dashed lines of weekly means on the same months as your reports, with a thin blue line on each report's day so the two can be read against each other. They are never drawn as a lab value: no range, no comparison, no colour that means anything, and they go into no export. The app reads them while the screen is open, writes nothing to Health and keeps no copy. ## Reference values **Reference values** is the table behind the bands. One card per measurement, a line per unit, two columns: **Guideline**, the threshold a guideline body states for adults, and **Optimal**, the lowest-risk band the same source names. Every card names its source and links to it; where a source partitions by risk tier or by age, the card says so and leaves the choice of tier to a clinician. A measurement with no citable source is simply absent. That is the difference from the longevity tables this screen was modelled on, which quote numbers nobody can check. The category menu narrows the list to one panel, and setting your sex in the profile adds the ranges that differ by sex. ## Profile and earlier measurements The **profile** holds sex, date of birth and height, used only to pick the published ranges that apply to you, and the body measurements: waist, weight and visceral fat. Each measurement keeps its own date and says where it came from. A value read from a scale's photograph is labelled as such; one you type is labelled as entered by you. **Earlier measurements**, in the **+** menu, is for catching up: one date per line, with whatever you measured that day. Saving stores each date as its own report, marked as entered by you, and works out the BMI and waist-to-height ratio from the height in the profile. They join the trends and the exports through the same path as a laboratory's values. ## Asking what a value is You can ask the app to explain a set of values. By default the model on the iPhone answers, so the question never reaches a network at all. If you would rather use a service, you pick the values, see them listed with their codes, and confirm before anything is sent. Only those values and your question travel. Your name, date of birth and insurance number are never sent, because the app does not hold them; they may be printed on the scanned page, which stays on the phone. Whichever provider is in use is named on the screen before you send. **Analysis provider** in the menu chooses where an answer comes from: on this iPhone, the Klarbefund service in the EU (by default [Azure OpenAI in the EU data zone](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/deployment-types#data-zone-standard)), or your own Azure OpenAI resource or Anthropic key. With your own service the phone talks to it directly, and neither the key nor the values reach the provider of this app ([ADR-034](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-034-claude-workload-identity-federation.md), [ADR-035](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-035-inference-provider-residency-and-quota.md)). The same screen holds the **Protection** switch for the Face ID lock. ## Consents **Consents**, in the menu, keeps your own record of three decisions that are easy to confuse and must never be one switch: - **Study participation**, your consent to a study, held by the study centre; - **Electronic patient record (ePA)**, an [_objection_](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__342.html), because the ePA exists unless you object to your health insurer; - **Registry and research use**, your consent for a registry or research database to use your values. Each has its own state, date, holder and button, and changing one never changes another. Withdrawing keeps the earlier grant in the history, so you can still show when you gave it. The app tells nobody: to give or withdraw one, contact whoever holds it. Two places use the record. **Export for research** asks once before exporting when no registry consent is recorded, and **Share for my doctor** reminds you, when you recorded an objection to the ePA, that there is no ePA to upload to while it stands. ## Connect to EHDS **My EHDS record**, at the top of the list, says whether the app is connected and sending, and opens **Connect to EHDS**, which connects the app to your record in the [European Health Data Space](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng) demo hub, so it can read it and, if you decide so, add to it. There are three ways in, and no password is typed into a web page on the phone: - **Create an EHDS account** makes an account with its own, empty record on the demo hub and connects the phone to it. You get a username and password to sign in on the website too. [Apple confirms](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity) to the hub that the request comes from the genuine app on a real device, which is why a simulator cannot do this ([ADR-054](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-054-klarbefund-creates-a-sandbox-account-with-app-attest.md)). - **Sign in with an EHDS account** you already have. - **Connect by QR code** ([OAuth device grant](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628), [ADR-049](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-049-klarbefund-connects-by-device-grant.md)), from the patient screen on a computer: 1. On the computer, open the patient screen (the app shows the address, to copy, share or open) and sign in as a patient. Choose **Show QR code**. 2. In the app, **Scan QR code**. On the computer, **Approve on this computer** opens [Keycloak](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#device-authorization-grant)'s consent page; check that the code shown there is the one the app shows, and approve. 3. The app says which account it connected to and asks **Is this your account?** A code someone else showed you would connect the phone to their account, so if the name is not yours, choose **Not me, disconnect**. Once connected, **Show my EHDS record** lists what the hub holds for you: measurements with their printed ranges and dates, reports, vaccinations and the medication plan ([ADR-059](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-059-the-record-holds-reports-vaccinations-and-the-medication-plan.md)). On the demo hub every record is synthetic, and the screen says so. The record is read when you open it, kept nowhere, and never mixed into your scanned reports. Two switches decide what goes the other way, and both are off until you turn them on: - **Send my reports to my EHDS record**: while it is on, every report you scan or read again goes to your own record, as preliminary values marked as read from a scan. Values without a LOINC code stay on the phone. - **Send my device trends to my EHDS record**: the weekly means from Apple Health that the Trends screen shows, never a single day or a single reading; each sync replaces the last ([ADR-057](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-057-klarbefund-sends-weekly-device-means.md)). Switching either off stops further sending; what was sent stays in the record until you delete the account. **Disconnect** is in the app and on the patient screen, where every connected phone is listed. On a phone holding the patient screen itself, **Open in Klarbefund** does the same as the QR code, and the iPhone's camera app opens Klarbefund from the code too. The code works once, for two minutes. ### Your EUDI wallet, if you want one An EUDI wallet is optional. Klarbefund and the hub work with a username and password alone. A wallet adds a second way to sign in on the website: d-you, the German EUDI Wallet, or any other certified one, proves who you are with your [PID](https://eu-digital-identity-wallet.github.io/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/latest/) (your digital identity card) instead of a password. d-you is [launched to the public in early January 2027](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/digital-wallet-2452384). Until then the hub is registered as a relying party in the SPRIND sandbox, so the steps below work with the d-you sandbox (test) wallet app, not yet with the public d-you ([ADR-065](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-065-the-eudi-wallet-sign-in-identifies-the-person.md), [ADR-066](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-066-the-hub-runs-its-own-eudi-verifier-behind-a-wallet-only-gate.md)). The hub never keeps your name or birth date. It keeps one secure hash of them on the account, which only says "this PID belongs to this account" ([ADR-067](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-067-a-pid-links-to-an-account-by-a-keyed-fingerprint.md)). One PID belongs to one account, so decide where you start. **You have Klarbefund first, and add the wallet later** 1. In the app, **Connect to EHDS › Create an EHDS account** gives you a username `kb-…` and a password. **Show password** or **Copy password** shows it again. 2. On a computer, open the website and choose **Sign in with Keycloak**, with that username and password. Not **Sign in with d-you**: the wallet can only open an account it is already connected to, and this one is not yet. 3. Open **Health Profile › Connect your EUDI wallet**, choose **Connect your EUDI wallet**, and scan the QR code with d-you. 4. d-you names the service and asks for three things: given names, family name and date of birth. Approve them with your Digital ID code. 5. The page says **d-you is connected**. From now on **Sign in with d-you** opens this account, and the app stays connected as before. **You have the wallet first, and add Klarbefund later** 1. On the website, choose **Sign in with d-you (QR)** and scan the code. Approve the same three things. 2. No account belongs to your PID yet, so the page offers **Create an account with this PID**. Only choose it if you have no Klarbefund account: if you have one, connect the wallet to it as above instead, because your PID cannot belong to two accounts. 3. The page shows a username `kb-…` and a password, once. Save both, then **I have saved them, sign me in**. 4. In the app, **Connect to EHDS › Sign in with an EHDS account** with that username and password. The app and the wallet now open the same record. **Disconnect wallet**, on the same page, removes the hash; the account, its record and the app's connection stay. Deleting the account removes the hash with it. ## Exports and your data rights Everything the app holds can leave it, in the form the recipient needs, and only when you say so. | Action | For | What you get | | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Share for my doctor | a practice, the ePA | a PDF summary with the original pages appended, plus a [FHIR R4](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/bundle.html) bundle | | Export for research (OMOP) | an analytics team | OMOP CDM v5.4 [`measurement.csv`](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#measurement), [`person.csv`](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#person), [`observation_period.csv`](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#observation_period) | | Export all my data | you, under GDPR [Art. 15](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_15) and [20](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_20) | every report, page, value, profile field and consent, in one archive | | Delete all my data | you, [GDPR Art. 17](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_17) | the store is wiped for good; the account the app made on the hub, with its record, values and consents, goes too; the app says so before it does it | | Export diagnostics | the developers | the recognised text and both recogniser passes, to fix a misread line | The FHIR bundle carries every value with its LOINC code, its [UCUM](https://ucum.org/ucum) unit, the range the laboratory printed (as numbers where they can be read, and always as the printed text in [`referenceRange.text`](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/observation-definitions.html#Observation.referenceRange.text)), and the page and line it was read from. A value read from a photograph is marked preliminary in the bundle too. The doctor export fits the ePA's [25 MB limit](https://www.kbv.de/praxis/tools-und-services/praxisnachrichten/2025/10-09/alles-nur-eine-frage-muessen-befundberichte-arztbriefe-etc-sofort-eingestellt-werden) with the pages attached. Everything goes through the system share sheet: to the ePA app, Files, AirDrop, or mail. There is deliberately no upload of its own, because there is no API into the ePA for an app like this, and the citizen is the integration point. ## Privacy and safety The photographs never leave the device. Values, pages and diagnostics are encrypted individually with [a key that is unavailable while the phone is locked](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/ksecattraccessiblewhenunlockedthisdeviceonly) and is never restored onto another device. The store is excluded from [iCloud Backup](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/urlresourcevalues/isexcludedfrombackup). When the app is not in front, its content is covered, so the app switcher shows nothing, and coming back asks for Face ID or the passcode. This was checked, not assumed: with the phone on a cable, copying a stored record, an export left in the temporary folder, or the system's own snapshot of the app all fail with a permission error, which is what [complete file protection](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsfileprotectioncomplete) looks like from outside. The full assessment, objective by objective, is the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment); what was tested and how is in [evidence](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence). ## Not a medical device Klarbefund explains what a measurement is. It does not diagnose, does not assess your risk and does not recommend treatment. No screen says normal or abnormal, scores anything, or advises. A value read from a photograph can be misread and is marked preliminary until you check it against the paper. Reference ranges are shown exactly as your laboratory printed them, and the published bands beside them are quotations with a source, not a verdict. Why the app is not a medical device under the [MDR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/745/oj/eng) and the [MDCG 2019-11](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/b45335c5-1679-4c71-a91c-fc7a4d37f12b_en) guidance is set out in the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment#regulation). Always consult a doctor before making any decision about your health. ## When something is read wrong A recogniser reads a photograph, and photographs get misread. Three things help, in this order: 1. **Compare with the paper.** The page and line under every value is there for this. Tap the value to correct it; the correction is kept beside the reading. 2. **Read again with this version**, in the report's menu, after an app update: the pages are kept, so a better reader can read them again. A re-read that finds fewer values than are stored is discarded, never saved over the better reading. 3. **Report missing values**, in the report's menu, sends the labels of the rows the app could not code, never your numbers, so the dictionary can learn the laboratory's spelling. **Export diagnostics** hands you an archive with the recognised text to attach to an [issue](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186); it leaves the phone only through the share sheet, when you send it. ## How these screenshots are made The images in this guide are shot from a simulator by [`clients/ios/Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh), launching the app straight into each screen with the fictional development dataset: ```bash cd clients/ios SEED=-MBDevData OUT=/tmp/shots \ SCREENS="list detail scan trends reference history profile consent settings privacy consents connect" \ Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh for f in /tmp/shots/*.png; do sips --resampleWidth 660 "$f" --out "../../docs/klarbefund/img/$(basename "$f")"; done ``` The dataset is built in code, in memory, and is compiled out of a release build. Every laboratory and practice in it is invented and every value made up, which is the only reason a screenshot may be committed at all: the rule in the [developer guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-developer-guide#two-rules-that-are-not-negotiable) is that no real health data enters the repository, not even as a picture, not even temporarily.
