docs.summary: Building, running and testing the app: the pipeline from camera to sealed store, the shared dictionary, the store layout, the dev dataset, the two test suites, diagnostics and TestFlight.
docs.markdown: # Klarbefund developer guide How to build, run, test and change the iPhone app in [`clients/ios/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios). The [user guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-user-guide) shows what a person sees; this guide shows what makes it so. The short command card is [`clients/ios/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/README.md); the work is tracked in [issue #186](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186). Every screenshot and every number in this guide comes from the app's own fictional development dataset. No real report is involved anywhere in the repository, and [the two rules at the end](#two-rules-that-are-not-negotiable) say why that is not negotiable. ## What you need | Tool | Version | Why | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | macOS with Xcode | [Xcode 26](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes) or later, iOS 26 SDK or later; CI builds with Xcode 26.6 on the [macOS 26 runner](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/macos/macos-26-arm64-Readme.md) | The app targets iOS 26; the Swift package declares macOS 26 for the tools | | Swift | 6.0, [strict concurrency](https://www.swift.org/documentation/concurrency/) | [`Package.swift`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Package.swift) and [`project.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/project.yml) both pin it | | [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) | `brew install xcodegen` | The `.xcodeproj` is generated from `project.yml` and never committed | | Node | as for `ui/` | Only to regenerate the dictionary from [`services/epa-ingest`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/epa-ingest) | | [PlantUML](https://www.plantuml.com/), [Graphviz](https://graphviz.org/) | `brew install plantuml` | Only to re-render the diagrams in this guide | | An iPhone | iOS 26 or later | Only for the camera, Face ID, [App Attest](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity) and [TestFlight](https://developer.apple.com/testflight/); everything else runs in the simulator | ## How it is put together ![Klarbefund as an ArchiMate layered view: the business layer with the person, the doctor and the research team and the six things a person does; the application layer with the four services, the app, the Shared package, the tools, the hub and the generator; the technology layer with the iPhone's frameworks, the Mac and Azure Container Apps](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/klarbefund-architecture.svg) Source: [`diagrams/klarbefund-architecture.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/diagrams/klarbefund-architecture.puml), rendered with [`scripts/render-plantuml.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/render-plantuml.sh) `docs/klarbefund/diagrams/*.puml`. The view follows [ArchiMate 3.2](https://pubs.opengroup.org/architecture/archimate32-doc/): the business layer (yellow) holds who does what, the application layer (blue) the services the software provides and the components that realise them, the technology layer (green) what it all runs on. An arrow from a lower band to an upper one means "serves"; a dotted arrow with a hollow head means "realises". Three things to read off it: - **[`Sources/Shared`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared)** is a Swift package that compiles for iOS and macOS. It holds the parser, the recogniser's post-processing, the generated analyte dictionary and reference ranges, the record model with its provenance, and the export formats ([FHIR R4](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/), [OMOP CDM](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html), the diagnostics bundle). Nothing in it touches the network, the Keychain or the store, which is why every number the app computes can be reproduced on a Mac with `swift test`. - **[`Sources/MeinBefund`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund)** is the app: SwiftUI views, [VisionKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/visionkit/vndocumentcameraviewcontroller) scanning, the sealed store, the exports' share sheet, the EHDS connection, the app lock, the analysis providers, and the debug-only demo data and self-test. - **[`Tools/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tools)** are four command-line programs over the Shared package: [`LabFile`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tools/LabFile) imports a PDF or image exactly as the app would, [`ScanReplay`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tools/ScanReplay) re-runs a diagnostics export through the current parser, [`AnalyteParity`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tools/AnalyteParity) proves the generated dictionary equals its TypeScript source, and [`IconGen`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tools/IconGen) draws the app icon. ``` clients/ios/ project.yml XcodeGen spec: the Shared framework and the MeinBefund app Package.swift SwiftPM: Shared, the four tools, SharedTests Sources/Shared/ parser, provenance model, formats; *.generated.swift are generated Sources/MeinBefund/ the app; en.lproj and de.lproj hold the strings Tools/{LabFile,ScanReplay,AnalyteParity,IconGen}/ Tests/SharedTests/ Swift Testing: what the app computes Tests/UITests/ XCUITest: what it shows, and what a tap does Scripts/ build, install, upload, screenshots, localisation, CodeQL appstore/ App Store Connect texts and the screenshot upload ``` ## Build and run ```bash cd clients/ios brew install xcodegen # once swift test # the Shared package, on the Mac swift run AnalyteParity # the generated table agrees with its source xcodegen generate && open MeinBefund.xcodeproj # then run the MeinBefund scheme in Xcode ``` From the command line into a simulator, note the **ad-hoc signature**: without it every Keychain call fails with [`-34018`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/errsecmissingentitlement) and the store cannot create its key. ```bash xcodebuild -project MeinBefund.xcodeproj -scheme MeinBefund \ -sdk iphonesimulator -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' \ CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=YES build ``` Onto a connected iPhone: [`Scripts/install-device.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/install-device.sh). The generated project carries no signing team, so a plain `xcodebuild` for a device fails; the script supplies one from `TEAM_ID` or from the keychain, and installs what it built. TestFlight: [`Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh); its header names the four things that must exist in the Apple Developer account first. The version is pinned in `project.yml`: `MARKETING_VERSION` matches the [App Store Connect](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-builds/upload-builds) record and `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` rises with every upload, because App Store Connect refuses a build number it has already seen, after the upload. ## Demo data and launch arguments Every launch argument below exists only in a Debug build. The checks are `#if DEBUG`, not a flag alone: a flag can be discovered, code that is not compiled cannot. | Argument | What it does | | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `-MBDemoSeed` | Two fictional reports, in memory only. Enough for a screenshot; what every UI test launches with. | | `-MBDevData` | Seven fictional reports across three years and four sources, built in code: a trend has shape, the unmatched list has rows, every report has pages. | | `-MBShot ` | Opens a screen directly once the reports are loaded: `list detail scan trends reference history profile consent settings privacy consents connect`. | | `-MBSelfTest` | Drives one synthetic report through the whole pipeline in the app target and logs 27 checks (see [The self-test](#the-self-test)). | | `-MBExportDiagnostics` | Builds the diagnostics archive into the app's temporary directory for [`Scripts/pull-diagnostics.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/pull-diagnostics.sh). | The dev dataset is **built, not stored**. A row states the label, the value, the unit and the range the laboratory printed, and [`Analytes.lookup`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/Analytes.generated.swift#L2775) codes it exactly as it codes a scan. No code in the dataset can be wrong, a row the dictionary cannot code lands in the unmatched list of its own accord, and the dataset follows the dictionary when the dictionary changes. The pages are drawn by [`SyntheticSheet`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/SyntheticSheet.swift), the same renderer the tests read. A demo launch never locks: the app lock reads the seed flag and stays open, so the UI tests and the screenshot script run where nobody can answer a passcode prompt. On a release build neither the flag nor the exception exists. Screenshots for the documentation and the App Store come from one script, which launches each screen by argument rather than by scripted taps, so a re-shoot after a layout change needs no new coordinates: ```bash SEED=-MBDevData OUT=/tmp/shots SCREENS="list detail trends" Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh # the App Store set, size-checked, into appstore/screenshots/en ``` ## From the camera to the store ![The scan pipeline as a sequence: the app's scanner hands the pages to LabImport, which decides the provenance, recognises or reads the text, reconciles the passes, infers the column roles, parses every row against the generated dictionary, reads the header, and hands the result to the review screen and then to the sealed store](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/klarbefund-scan-pipeline.svg) Source: [`diagrams/klarbefund-scan-pipeline.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/diagrams/klarbefund-scan-pipeline.puml). The order is fixed and each step has one owner ([ADR-033](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-033-lab-report-extraction-pipeline.md)): 1. **Provenance first.** [`LabImport`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/LabImport.swift) decides on the file, never its extension: a PDF carrying the laboratory's own text layer is `lab-issued-digital` and its Observations are `final`; anything that has to go through the recogniser is `ocr-transcribed` and `preliminary`. It is strict on purpose, because marking a transcription `final` is the failure that matters. 2. **Recognition.** [`VisionDocumentReader`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/VisionDocumentReader.swift) runs two [Vision](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/recognizing-text-in-images) passes, German and English, with language correction **off**: "correcting" `Lp(a)` or a decimal comma is actively harmful. [`DocumentReconciler`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/DocumentReconciler.swift) merges the passes and [`TableRoles`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/TableRoles.swift) infers which column holds the label, the value, the unit and the range, per table. 3. **Parsing.** [`LabLineParser`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/LabLineParser.swift) reads every row. When the ordinary parse finds nothing, the sheet readers take their turn: ambulatory blood pressure, resting and exercise ECG, Holter, cardiopulmonary exercise test, lactate, CGM glucose profile, DXA, and a body-composition scale's screen, which is a dashboard and not a report and is read for its headline value only. 4. **Coding.** [`Analytes.lookup(label, unit)`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/Analytes.generated.swift#L2775) picks the LOINC code. The unit decides, never the name alone. A quantity LOINC does not code (visceral fat as a mass, a water ratio) is carried with its unit, no code and a required reason; an organism from a stool report carries its [NCBI Taxonomy](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy) id, because LOINC names tests and not organisms. 5. **The header.** [`ReportMetadata`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/ReportMetadata.swift) and [`PrintedFields`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/PrintedFields.swift) read the laboratory, the lab date, the issue date and the report number from the sheet; the lab date is preferred over the receipt and issue dates and the person confirms it before saving. 6. **Conservation.** Every row that looks like a measurement ends up coded, unmatched or unread. A row in none of the three is indistinguishable from a row that was never printed, and that is exactly how an HbA1c row went missing once ([`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md#2026-09-19-the-measurement-that-justified-the-ocr-hybrid-was-taken-on-the-wrong-os), 2026-09-19). The self-test asserts it. 7. **Review and save.** [`ReviewViews`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund/ReviewViews.swift) shows what was read; [`ReportStore`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund/ReportStore.swift) seals it. `swift run LabFile ~/Downloads/befund.pdf` runs steps 1 to 6 on a Mac and prints the provenance, the header, and every row as coded, unmatched or unread; `--values` adds the numbers, `--rows` adds the recogniser's layout. It refuses a path inside this repository. ## The store and the lock Three sealed files per report under `Application Support/Reports`, each [AES-GCM](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptokit/aes/gcm) under the same Keychain key, [complete file protection](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsfileprotectioncomplete), [excluded from backup](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/urlresourcevalues/isexcludedfrombackup): ``` .sealed the record (LabReport) .scan.sealed the pages as one PDF .diag.sealed the scan's diagnostics (ScanDiagnostics) profile.sealed sex, date of birth, height (Profile) consents.sealed the three consent decisions (ConsentLedger) ``` The key is [`ThisDeviceOnly`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/ksecattraccessiblewhenunlockedthisdeviceonly) and unavailable while the phone is locked, so a container copy yields ciphertext and the system's own snapshot of the app fails with `EPERM`; [`SecurityPostureTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/SecurityPostureTests.swift) pins the build settings and the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment) records the measurement. Records written before a field existed still decode: every later field is optional or defaulted. The app lock ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)) is two types. [`AppLockPolicy`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/AppLockPolicy.swift) in Shared decides _whether_ a challenge is due and is pure, so [`AppLockPolicyTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/AppLockPolicyTests.swift) runs on a Mac; [`AppLock`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund/AppLock.swift) in the app asks [LocalAuthentication](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/localauthentication) _how_, Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode, and [`PrivacyCover`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund/PrivacyCover.swift) draws the cover the app switcher sees. The same ADR says why certificate pinning and jailbreak detection were declined. ## The dictionary is generated, never copied [`Sources/Shared/Analytes.generated.swift`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/Analytes.generated.swift), [`ReferenceRanges.generated.swift`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/ReferenceRanges.generated.swift) and [`PromptText.generated.swift`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/Shared/PromptText.generated.swift) are produced from [`services/epa-ingest`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/epa-ingest): ```bash cd services/epa-ingest && npm run generate:swift cd clients/ios && swift run AnalyteParity # 1760 codings, 96 units on 2026-11-07 ``` Do not hand-edit them. Add an analyte to [`analytes.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/epa-ingest/src/analytes.ts) or a range to [`reference-ranges.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/epa-ingest/src/reference-ranges.ts), regenerate, commit both. CI fails when a generated file is out of date with its source, because a stale copy is exactly the silent divergence the monorepo was chosen to prevent: an iPhone coding Lp(a) one way and the ingest service another, noticed when a value reaches a doctor. The reference-range generator refuses a range whose analyte the dictionary does not know or whose unit that analyte is not defined in. Only analytes with a citable published source get a band ([ADR-039](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-039-published-reference-ranges.md)); for every other analyte the Trends screen draws the range the person's own laboratory printed. ## Tests, and what each is for ```bash swift test # Swift Testing: what the app computes Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh # XCUITest: what it shows, and what a tap does swift test --filter AccuracyBenchmarkTests # the accuracy benchmark; KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT= writes its JSON swift test --filter SecurityPostureTests # the build settings the self-assessment relies on ``` **The unit suite** ([`Tests/SharedTests/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests), [Swift Testing](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/testing)) is the larger one and catches what can be reasoned about: a unit that picks the wrong code, a date read from the wrong line, an export column in the wrong place. [`FhirBundleParityTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/FhirBundleParityTests.swift) pins the bundle to the golden bundle `services/epa-ingest` writes, so both writers emit the same FHIR for the same sheet. **The UI suite** ([`Tests/UITests/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios/Tests/UITests), [XCUITest](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xctest/xcuiapplication)) exists because the unit suite caught none of the last several defects: a card clipped at the chart's edge, a selection that forgot itself on the next render, `LOINC Optional("2093-3")` on the one screen a person compares with their own paper. Every test launches with `-MBDemoSeed` and reaches its screen with `-MBShot`, so it breaks when what it checks changes and not when a button moves. Three things learned the hard way are in [`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md#2026-09-20--an-accessibilityidentifier-on-a-chart-renames-everything-inside-it): an `accessibilityIdentifier` on a container renames everything inside it; a `Button` whose label is `Color.clear` is not in the accessibility tree; [Swift Charts](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/charts)' selection answers a finger and not a synthesised tap, so real buttons sit over the marks. ### The self-test Everything after the camera runs in the app target and therefore not in `swift test`: the sealed store, the PDF of the pages, the export. `-MBSelfTest` drives one synthetic report through the whole chain and logs each of its 27 checks: recognition and coding, a citation per value, the lab date read from the header, the pages as a PDF, the three sealed files decrypting, the replay of the diagnostics record reproducing the extraction exactly, the archive building, and the doctor export fitting the ePA's 25 MB with the pages appended. ```bash xcrun simctl launch red.mabu.meinbefund -MBSelfTest xcrun simctl spawn log show --last 2m --predicate 'subsystem == "red.mabu.meinbefund"' --style compact ``` ### The accuracy benchmark [`AccuracyBenchmarkTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/AccuracyBenchmarkTests.swift) reads synthetic sheets of known content with Vision and, with `KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT` set, writes field-level accuracy as JSON; the published copy is [`docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json), and [`ExtractionAccuracyTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/ExtractionAccuracyTests.swift) tests the measure itself. The [evidence](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence) page quotes it and [run-on-mac](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac) reproduces every number. A real report is measured the same way, on the person's own Mac and never in the repository, with `ScanReplay --truth` against a hand-written `truth.json` beside the export: it prints which fields of which rows were wrong, never the values. ## Debugging a misread sheet The store yields ciphertext, so evidence leaves the phone through the app's own **Export diagnostics**, which asks for confirmation in words and hands a zip to the share sheet ([ADR-038](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-038-scan-retained-diagnostics-export.md)): ``` klarbefund-diagnostics-/ about.json build, device, dictionary size, counts log.txt this session's log lines: counts and codes only -<id8>/ report.json the stored record: values, metadata, page text diagnostics.json both Vision passes, the reconciled rows, the layout scan.pdf the pages as scanned ``` With the phone on USB and a Debug build installed, `Scripts/pull-diagnostics.sh` does the export and the unzip in one go, under `~/Downloads`. Unzip **outside this repository**, then: ```bash swift run ScanReplay ~/Downloads/klarbefund-diagnostics-<date> # every report, with the current parser swift run ScanReplay ~/Downloads/klarbefund-diagnostics-<date> --ocr # re-run Vision on scan.pdf swift run ScanReplay ~/Downloads/klarbefund-diagnostics-<date> --truth # accuracy against truth.json ``` The replay prints what the phone coded, what codes now, what is newly coded or lost, and every row with its reason. Add an analyte to [`analytes.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/epa-ingest/src/analytes.ts), regenerate, replay, and watch the real sheet's rows move from unmatched to coded without scanning it again. [`Scripts/check-localization.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/check-localization.sh) fails when a user-visible string has no German or when a German sentence was left in the English base; it uses [`xcodebuild -exportLocalizations`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/localization), the same extractor Xcode's editor uses, so it sees SwiftUI `Text` literals and `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` values that no grep of the sources would find. The camera permission prompt once shipped in German to every English phone, which is why the script exists. ## Static analysis and CI ```bash Scripts/codeql-swift.sh # CodeQL on the app and Shared, about 15 minutes ``` [CodeQL](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli) needs a real build to see Swift, so on GitHub it runs only when `clients/ios/` changes ([`.github/workflows/codeql-swift.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql-swift.yml)), on a macOS runner. The `codeql-swift` pre-push hook runs the same suite when a push changes the Swift sources; it exits 1 on any finding not listed, with its reason, in [`Scripts/codeql-accepted.txt`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/codeql-accepted.txt). Swift needs a macOS runner, which has lower concurrency than Linux, so the iOS job is path-filtered to `clients/ios/**` and never gates the web or service suites; conversely, the `ui/**` and `services/**` workflows exclude `clients/ios/**`. The security posture of the app, its threat model and what an independent test would add are in the [threat model](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund), the [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) and the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment). ## Two rules that are not negotiable 1. **No health data in `clients/ios/`, ever.** No lab reports, no scans, no exported HealthKit archives, no screenshots containing real values, not even temporarily, not even gitignored. Test fixtures are synthetic, the way [`services/epa-ingest/__tests__/fixtures/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/epa-ingest/__tests__/fixtures) already is. The tools refuse a path inside the repository for the same reason. 2. **No real organisation in demo content.** [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) forbids it outside the `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_TK` flag. The study this app is built for is real; the demo centre, the laboratory and the practice in the dev dataset are fictional. ## Where the decisions are | ADR | Decides | | docs.title: Operational guideline: hosting the hub and Klarbefund under the EHDS and the BSI standards
docs.summary: How to host the hub and Klarbefund for real: which EHDS role (Regulation (EU) 2025/327) operates which part, what BSI C5, IT-Grundschutz, TR-02102 and TR-03161 ask of each part, the clocks for incidents, retention, and the go-live checklist by role.
docs.markdown:
# Operational guideline: hosting the hub and Klarbefund under the EHDS and the BSI standards

What is in this repository is a demonstrator: one Azure resource group, one
operator, fictional participants, synthetic patients, and a stack that stops
at night to stay inside a personal credit. This guideline is written for the
day someone hosts it for real: a health data access body, an operating
company working for one, a health insurer, a hospital group, or a vendor who
takes the white-label app. It says which role in [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng)
(the EHDS) operates which part, what the BSI standards require of each part,
and what has to change from the demo before any real health data touches it.

Article numbers are those of the adopted Regulation. Older files in this
repository still carry the numbers of the 2022 proposal; the mapping is in
[`docs/ehds-article-numbering.md`](/docs/ehds/article-numbering). The
evidence behind every "the demo already does" below is in the
[security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report), the two threat
models ([hub](/docs/security/threat-model-hub), [app](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund)), the
[C5 gap analysis](/docs/security/bsi-c5-gap-analysis) and the Klarbefund
[self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment). This document is a
guideline by the project, not legal advice and not a certification.

## 1. The roles in the EHDS, and who operates what

The Regulation names the roles; it does not say who runs the servers below
the access body. The hub's seven Keycloak roles are the technical shadow of
the legal roles, and the table says which legal actor stands behind each
technical one when the system leaves the demo.

| EHDS role (Reg. 2025/327)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | What the Regulation expects of it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Hub role / component                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Who operates it in a real deployment                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Natural person** (the patient), [Art. 3](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_3) to [10](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_10), opt-out [Art. 71](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_71)                     | Access to their own electronic health data, insertion, rectification, restriction, information on who accessed; the right to opt out of secondary use.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `PATIENT`; `/patient/*`; Klarbefund on the phone; EUDI wallet sign-in ([ADR-028](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-028-patient-qr-login-eudi-wallet.md))                                                                                                        | Themselves, through the access service of the digital health authority or an EHR system; the app is theirs, the operator never sees its content.                                                                                                                                              |
| **Health professional**, [Art. 11](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_11)                                                                                                                                                                           | Access to the priority categories of the persons under their care, logged and visible to the person.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Not a role in the demo (primary-use access to the record goes through the ePA, not the hub)                                                                                                                                               | The EHR system's operator; the hub only receives what the person exports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Health data holder**, [Art. 2(2)(t)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#002.002), duties [Art. 60](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_60), dataset description [Art. 77](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_77) | Make the [Art. 51](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_51) categories available on a permit, describe datasets, communicate with the access body, apply the quality label ([Art. 78](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_78)).                                                                                                                                                                | `DATA_HOLDER`; `/data/share`, `/data/transfer`; the connector (control plane, data plane, IdentityHub)                                                                                                                                    | The holder itself (a hospital, an insurer, a registry); the operating company may host its connector under an [Art. 28 GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_28) processing contract.                                                                                   |
| **Health data user**, [Art. 61](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_61), applications [Art. 67](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_67), permit [Art. 68](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_68)                | Process only inside the secure processing environment, only for the permit's purpose ([Art. 53](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_53)), never for the prohibited purposes ([Art. 54](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_54)), publish results, report breaches.                                                                                                                            | `DATA_USER`; `/data/discover`, `/negotiate`, `/analytics`, `/query`                                                                                                                                                                       | The researcher's institution; it never operates infrastructure, it is a tenant of the SPE.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Health data access body (HDAB)**, [Art. 55](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_55), tasks [Art. 57](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_57), enforcement [Art. 63](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_63)    | Decide on applications, issue permits, provide the SPE ([Art. 73](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_73)), keep the public register and the information duties ([Art. 58](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_58), [59](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_59)), enforce, be controller of the SPE ([Art. 74](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_74)). | `HDAB_AUTHORITY`; `/compliance`, `/admin/policies`, the permit register, `HDABApproval` nodes                                                                                                                                             | The designated public body; it owns the decisions and the controllership even where it buys the operation.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Trusted health data holder**, [Art. 72](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_72)                                                                                                                                                                    | A holder allowed to run the simplified procedure for its own data, with the same SPE and logging duties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | A `DATA_HOLDER` with HDAB-delegated rights (not modelled separately in the demo)                                                                                                                                                          | The holder, under the access body's supervision.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Secure processing environment operator**, [Art. 73](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.001)                                                                                                                                                       | Access only for authorised natural persons, no download of personal data, every access and output logged, outputs checked for personal data before release, security audited.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `TRUST_CENTER_OPERATOR`; `/analytics`, `/query`, `SPESession`, the OMOP aggregates; [ADR-037](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-037-secure-processing-environment-confidential-computing.md), [ADR-052](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-052-confidential-spe-on-azure-revisited.md) | The access body or its operating company; on a certified cloud (C5 attestation) with confidential computing where the data warrants it.                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Digital health authority**, [Art. 19](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_19); national contact points, [Art. 23](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_23) and [75](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_75)     | Primary use: the access service, MyHealth@EU; secondary use: HealthData@EU and the cross-border permits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | The second access body and the cross-border permit in the seed; the federated catalogue ([ADR-020](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-020-cross-participant-dataset-discovery.md))                                                                               | The member state's designated authorities; the hub is a participant, never the national contact point itself.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **EHR system manufacturer**, Chapter III; **wellness app** label, [Art. 47](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_47)                                                                                                                                  | Conformity of the EHR system's European interoperability and logging components; a wellness app may claim interoperability with an EHR system ([Art. 48](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_48)) and then carries the label.                                                                                                                                                                                   | Klarbefund as a wellness-type app that exports to the ePA; FHIR R4 in the EEHRxF profiles                                                                                                                                                 | The vendor who ships the app; for the white-label case, the insurer as the entity placing it on the market.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Platform operator** (not an EHDS role; the operating company of [`docs/ehds-operating-company.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ehds-operating-company.md))                                                                                                                                    | Runs identity, catalogue, connectors, SPE and monitoring for the actors above; a processor under [GDPR Art. 28](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_28) for each of them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `EDC_ADMIN`; `/admin/*`, the Azure resource group, Keycloak, Vault, Key Vault, the pipelines                                                                                                                                              | A contracted operator with an ISO 27001 ISMS on the basis of [IT-Grundschutz](https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/IT-Grundschutz/IT-Grundschutz-Kompendium/it-grundschutz-kompendium_node.html) and a C5-attested cloud underneath. |
| **Supervisory authorities**: data protection (GDPR), market surveillance (Chapter III), BSI / national CSIRT ([NIS2](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2555/oj/eng))                                                                                              | Receive breach notifications, audit, enforce.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The audit trail ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)), the activity report, the permit register                                                                                                        | Not operators; the operator must be able to answer them within the clocks in section 7.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### The operating model as a process

The diagram is a BPMN-style process with one swimlane per role: boxes are
tasks, diamonds are decisions, the loop at the end is the output control,
the green dots are start and end. Article numbers are the adopted ones. The
lanes of the holder, the user and the person are their own; the access
body's lane is where every decision sits; the operating company's and the
SPE operator's lanes hold the technical work that this repository
implements.

![EHDS operating model: one swimlane per role, from the holder's onboarding through application, permit, opt-out, extraction, the secure processing environment and output control to the published results](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/ehds-operating-model.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/ehds-operating-model.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/ehds-operating-model.puml), rendered with `scripts/render-plantuml.sh`.

Three responsibilities that the diagram makes visible and a contract must
repeat: the access body decides and the operator executes; the person's
opt-out reaches the holder's extraction through the operator's policy
evaluation, not through goodwill; and no output leaves the SPE on the
operator's say-so, only on the access body's.

Two things follow. **Controllership is never the operator's.** The access
body is controller for the SPE and the permit data (Art. 74); the holder is
controller of its source data; the operator processes on instruction. Every
hosting contract repeats this. **Role grants are decisions, not tickets.**
Who becomes `HDAB_AUTHORITY` or `TRUST_CENTER_OPERATOR` is decided by the
access body in writing; the operator executes the grant in Keycloak and the
grant is logged ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)). The demo assigns roles in a seed file; a real
deployment removes the seed and keeps the grant history.

## 2. Hosting architecture: from the demo to an operable platform

The demo runs everything in one [Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/overview) environment,
`rg-mvhd-dev` ([ADR-012](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-012-azure-container-apps.md)), stopped off hours ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md), [ADR-058](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-058-azure-triggers-the-off-hours-schedule.md)). The shape
below keeps the components and changes how they are placed.

### The solution in layers

![The solution as an ArchiMate layered view: the business layer with the six EHDS roles and the processes each performs, the application layer with the six services and the components that realise them, the technology layer with the Azure platform, the databases, the vaults and the iPhone](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/ehds-solution-layers.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/ehds-solution-layers.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/ehds-solution-layers.puml),
[ArchiMate 3.2](https://pubs.opengroup.org/architecture/archimate32-doc/) notation. The business layer is section 1 of this guideline:
each role performs its own processes, and the two-sided procedure of Chapter
IV (apply, decide, process) runs left to right. The application layer names
what the hub provides to those processes and which component realises it;
the technology layer is the platform of the table below, as the demo runs it
today. An arrow from a lower band to an upper one reads "serves".

| Zone              | Components                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Demo today                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Required for real data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Edge              | TLS termination, WAF, rate limits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | ACA ingress with managed certificates; headers set by [`next.config`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/next.config.js#L76-L105) ([F8](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings))                                                           | A web application firewall in front of every public hostname; TLS per [BSI TR-02102-2](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TG02102/BSI-TR-02102-2.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=11#page=7) (TLS 1.2 minimum, 1.3 preferred; the TR still lists CBC suites with Encrypt-then-MAC, leaving them out is this project's hardening); HSTS preloaded; rate limits per route and per identity; bot and DDoS protection from the cloud.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Identity          | Keycloak, IdentityHub, IssuerService, the EUDI wallet backend                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Keycloak `start-dev` behind a Caddy guard ([F10](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings)); realm from [`keycloak-realm.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/keycloak-realm.json)                                                     | Keycloak in [production mode](https://www.keycloak.org/server/configuration-production) with its own database on the Flexible Server, admin console reachable only from the operator's network, MFA for every privileged role (C5 [IDM-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=78) and [IDM-09](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=80)), the realm under version control and drift-checked ([`docs/knowledge/runbooks/keycloak-realm-drift.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/keycloak-realm-drift.md)).                                                                                                        |
| Application       | The hub (Next.js), the neo4j-proxy, the explanation service, the crawlers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Public ingress for the hub and Keycloak; internal ingress for the rest                                                                                                                                                | Only the hub and Keycloak public; everything else on internal ingress or private endpoints; every image signed and pinned by digest; the bills of materials in [`docs/sbom/`](/docs/security/sbom) regenerated on every dependency change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Connectors        | Control plane, data planes, IdentityHub, Vault per participant                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | One connector set per fictional participant ([ADR-024](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-024-full-edc-provisioning-per-participant.md))                                                                                                     | One connector per legal holder, operated by the holder or by the operator under contract; DSP endpoints mutually authenticated; the participant's keys in its own Vault namespace ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)), never shared.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Data              | Neo4j, the PostgreSQL Flexible Server, [Azure Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-introduction)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Managed Postgres ([ADR-041](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-041-managed-postgres-on-azure-containerised-locally.md)); Neo4j on Azure Files ([ADR-017](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-017-persistent-storage-aca.md)); no backups                             | Encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (C5 [CRY-03](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=82)); zone-redundant Postgres with [point-in-time restore](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/concepts-backup-restore); Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph with backups tested quarterly (C5 [OPS-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=63) to [OPS-09](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=65)); no synthetic data and no real data in the same instance. |
| Secure processing | `/analytics`, `/query`, the OMOP aggregates, `SPESession`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Aggregates in the same Neo4j; confidential computing assessed ([ADR-037](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-037-secure-processing-environment-confidential-computing.md), [ADR-052](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-052-confidential-spe-on-azure-revisited.md)) | A separate environment per [Art. 73](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.001): isolated network, no outbound internet, no download path, output checked by the access body before release, [confidential VMs or enclaves](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/overview) where the permit's data warrant it; audited at least annually.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Secrets           | Key Vault, Vault                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Every operator secret a Key Vault reference ([ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md)); Vault state on Postgres ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md))       | Keep; add rotation on a schedule (C5 [CRY-04](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=83)), HSM-backed keys for signing credentials, and a documented break-glass procedure with two-person approval.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Observability     | The [OpenTelemetry collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/), [Grafana](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/), [Loki](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/), [Tempo](https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/), [Prometheus](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/) ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)) | One observability app; logs in Azure Monitor                                                                                                                                                                          | Logs shipped to a SIEM the operator's SOC watches; immutability for the audit trail (C5 [OPS-14](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=68)); retention per section 6; alerting on the events in section 7.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Availability      | The whole stack                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Stops at 18:13 UTC, starts at 05:17 UTC on weekdays                                                                                                                                                                   | 24x7 with the targets of the service contract; the off-hours schedule is a demo cost measure and is removed (it is one `az` call, [`scripts/azure/offhours.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/offhours.sh), and [ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md) is superseded by the hosting decision).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The demo's one resource group becomes at least three subscriptions or
resource groups with separate identities: identity and edge, the platform,
and the secure processing environment. The SPE's identity never has rights
in the others. This is the separation C5 asks for in [OPS-24](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=74) (separation of
datasets in the cloud infrastructure) and [COS-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=86) (segregation of data
traffic in jointly used network environments), and IT-Grundschutz
[NET.1.1](https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/IT-Grundschutz/IT-Grundschutz-Kompendium/IT-Grundschutz-Bausteine/Bausteine_Download_Edition_node.html) in practice.
