## 4. Identity and access

- **One identity provider, operated by the platform operator, with the
  realm in version control.** Keycloak holds the roles; the hub trusts only
  the roles in the token ([`ui/src/lib/auth.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/auth.ts)). Every API route needs a
  session ([ADR-044](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-044-every-api-route-needs-a-session.md)); the one exception per route is written as an ADR, never
  as a configuration flag.
- **Organisations prove who they are with verifiable credentials** issued
  against an authoritative register ([DCP v1.0](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/), [`did:web`](https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-web/)). The IssuerService
  is the operator's; the holder's keys stay in the holder's Vault
  namespace. The demo's seed issues credentials to fictional organisations;
  a real deployment issues them only after the onboarding steps in the
  [operating-company document](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ehds-operating-company.md#2-coordination-with-data-holders-and-the-onboarding-process), step 3.
- **Natural persons sign in through the EUDI wallet or the national eID**,
  at assurance "high" for their own record. "High" is this project's
  target: [Art. 16](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_16) asks for electronic identification means
  recognised under eIDAS; [TR-03107](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/Technische-Richtlinien/TR-nach-Thema-sortiert/tr03107/TR-03107_node.html) describes the levels. Username and password remain for staff, with MFA,
  and never for patients.
- **Privileged roles** (`EDC_ADMIN`, `HDAB_AUTHORITY`,
  `TRUST_CENTER_OPERATOR`) require MFA, a named person, a documented grant by
  the access body, and a review every quarter. Service accounts (the
  catalogue crawler's token, [ADR-020](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-020-cross-participant-dataset-discovery.md); the app's sandbox account, [ADR-054](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-054-klarbefund-creates-a-sandbox-account-with-app-attest.md)) are
  listed with owner, scope and rotation date.
- **The Keycloak admin console is not on the internet** ([finding F10](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings), the
  Caddy guard in [`scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh)); administration
  goes through a private network or a bastion with session recording.
- **Sessions** are short for privileged roles, bound to the client, and
  revoked on role change. `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` and every other operator secret
  is a Key Vault reference ([ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md)), rotated on a schedule.
- **Who sees a patient's identity is decided by role, never by a
  parameter** ([`ui/src/lib/patient-identity.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient-identity.ts#L33)): holders and the platform
  operator for primary use, the patient for their own record only
  ([`refuseForeignRecord`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient/own-record.ts#L19)), everyone else a pseudonym. The NLQ proxy refuses
  identity-revealing queries. This stays as it is and is tested on every
  build.

## 5. Data protection

- **Controllership and contracts.** The access body is controller for the
  secure processing environment ([Art. 74](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_74)) and processor-instructs the
  operator; the holder is controller of its source data; the data user is
  controller of what it is permitted to process, inside the SPE only. Each
  pair signs an [Art. 28 GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_28) contract; the [operating-company document](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ehds-operating-company.md) gives
  the model.
- **A [data protection impact assessment](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_35)** before go-live, for the platform
  as a whole and for the SPE separately. The two threat models are the
  technical input; the DPIA adds the legal basis per data category ([Art. 51](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_51))
  and the residual risks.
- **Data minimisation and purpose limitation** ([Art. 66](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_66)): the access body
  decides for each permit whether anonymised data answer the question, and
  only then pseudonymised data. The hub's OMOP aggregates and the k-anonymity
  of the cohort views are the anonymised path; the FHIR extraction is the
  pseudonymised one and runs only inside the SPE.
- **Pseudonymisation keys** are held by the access body or a trusted third
  party, never by the data user and never by the operator of the SPE.
- **The opt-out** ([Art. 71](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_71)) is a register the access body keeps; the
  holder's connector checks it before extraction. The demo has consent
  records in the app and on the patient page; a real deployment wires the
  national opt-out register into the ODRL policy evaluation.
- **Patient rights for primary use** ([Art. 3](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_3) to [10](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_10)): access, insertion,
  rectification, restriction, and the list of who accessed. The patient
  page's access log and the audit trail ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)) are the implementation;
  the operator must answer a request within the GDPR month ([Art. 12(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#012.003)).
- **Residency.** Every processor is in the EU or EEA; the explanation
  service's model provider is chosen by region and quota ([ADR-035](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-035-inference-provider-residency-and-quota.md)), and the
  on-device model is the default so that no health value leaves the phone
  unless the person sends it.
- **The app** holds nothing the operator can read: values, pages and
  diagnostics are encrypted per record with a key kept in the Keychain on this
  device only ([`ReportStore.swift`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund/ReportStore.swift#L65-L72)), excluded from backups, behind Face ID or the passcode ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)). The
  white-label operator inherits this; it must not add telemetry that
  carries values.

## 6. Logging, retention and the audit trail

What must be logged, for how long, and who may read it. The project's
[audit retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md) holds the current
numbers; the duties come
from [Art. 57](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_57) (the access body keeps a record of applications and permits),
[Art. 73(1)(e)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.001) (identifiable logs of access to and activity in the SPE, at least one year),
[Art. 58](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_58) and [59](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_59)
(information to the public, activity report) and [GDPR accountability](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#005.002).

| Event                                                       | Logged by                          | Readable by                                            | Retention (project policy)                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Data access, transfer, contract (the `TransferEvent` chain) | The neo4j-proxy and the connectors | The access body, the holder for its data, auditors     | 12 months as the floor for access events and transfers; none set for contract negotiations |
| Permit decisions, revocations                               | The access body in the hub         | Public register for the decision, parties for the file | Not set by the policy                                                                      |
| SPE sessions: who, which dataset, which query, which output | The SPE                            | The access body; the data user for its own             | At least one year (Art. 73(1)(e))                                                          |
| Role grants and revocations, privileged sign-ins            | Keycloak, shipped to the SIEM      | The operator's security team, auditors                 | 2 years, longer if an incident references them                                             |
| HTTP access at the edge, authentication events              | The edge and Keycloak              | The operator's security team                           | 2 years                                                                                    |
| Patient's own record: every read, by whom                   | The hub                            | The patient, on their page                             | As long as the record                                                                      |
| App: diagnostics the person chooses to export               | The app, on the device only        | The person; the developers only if sent                | The person decides                                                                         |

Three rules the demo already keeps and a real deployment must keep:
the audit trail is written by the service that performed the action, not by
the client; it is append-only for everyone but the retention job
(C5 [OPS-14](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=68); the hub's hash chain shows a change, an immutable store would prevent it); and no log
line carries a health value or a name where a pseudonym does.

## 7. Incidents, clocks and who notifies whom

| Trigger                                                 | Clock                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Who notifies whom                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Personal data breach                                    | [GDPR Art. 33](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_33): 72 hours to the supervisory authority; [Art. 34](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_34): the persons without undue delay                       | The operator informs the controller (access body or holder) without undue delay; the controller notifies the authority.                                                                                                                  |
| Significant incident at a health entity or the operator | [NIS2 Art. 23](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2555/oj/eng#art_23) as transposed ([BSIG § 32](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bsig_2025/__32.html)): early warning in 24 hours, notification in 72 hours, final report in a month | The operator's CSIRT contact to the BSI; the affected holders in parallel.                                                                                                                                                               |
| Data used outside the permit                            | [Art. 63(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#063.003): the access body may revoke the permit and stop the processing without undue delay                                                                                  | The SPE operator reports to the access body at once; the access body decides and, if a GDPR breach is possible, informs the supervisory authority immediately ([Art. 63(2)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#063.002)). |
| SPE audit finds a shortcoming                           | [Art. 73(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.003): corrective action                                                                                                                                                  | The access body instructs the operator; the fix is evidenced in the next audit.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Serious incident of an EHR system                       | [Art. 44](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_44) (risks posed by EHR systems and serious incidents; a wellness app such as Klarbefund is not an EHR system)                                                              | The manufacturer to the market surveillance authority.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Vulnerability in a dependency, high or critical         | Project rule: fixed or time-boxed exception within the CI gate ([`docs/npm-audit-exceptions.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/npm-audit-exceptions.json))                                                                                                           | The operator's security team; the scan runs on every push ([`security-scan.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml)).                                                                                                            |

### Incident coordination between the parties

An escalation is a set of notifications with deadlines, so it is drawn as a
sequence: one lifeline per party, one message per notification, the legal
clocks in bold on the message, and the branches that run at the same time in
one parallel block.

Source: [`diagrams/ehds-incident-coordination.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/ehds-incident-coordination.puml),
rendered with [`scripts/render-plantuml.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/render-plantuml.sh). The clocks come from
[GDPR Art. 33](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_33) and [34](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_34),
[NIS2 Art. 23](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2555/oj/eng#art_23) as transposed
in the [BSIG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bsig_2025/__32.html), and [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng)
Art. [63(2)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#063.002), [63(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#063.003) and [73(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.003), the table above names each; and [64(2)(h)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#064.002), which the diagram shows: whether a data user reported its own infringement is weighed when the access body sets a fine.

The clocks are not the operator's to negotiate: the controller owns the
GDPR ones, the operator the NIS2 ones, the access body the EHDS ones. The
contact list in the incident procedure names a person for each, with a
deputy, and the tabletop exercise before go-live walks this diagram once.

The alerting that feeds this table, at minimum: a privileged sign-in from a
new location, an admin-console request reaching Keycloak at all, a query
in the SPE that would reveal identity, a failed App Attest verification in
volume, a connector whose credential verification fails, a backup job that
did not run, and every HTTP 5xx rate above the floor.

## 8. Operating the platform

- **Change management.** Every change is a pull request with the gates in
  [`docs/quality-gates.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md): type-check, lint, unit and journey tests, the
  [Bruno](https://www.usebruno.com/) collection against the hub, [Semgrep](https://semgrep.dev/docs/), [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/tag/v8.30.1), [hadolint](https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint), the [SBOM
  check](/docs/security/sbom), [CodeQL](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli) for TypeScript and Swift, [trivy](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/tag/v0.74.0) and [grype](https://github.com/anchore/grype/releases/tag/v0.118.0). Merges deploy
  through [`deploy-azure.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml) from `main` only; the production environment
  adds a release approval by the operator's change board and a signed image.
- **Vulnerability management.** The scans in [`scripts/security/scan-repo.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/scan-repo.sh)
  run on every push and nightly (in the demo they run locally; CI runs grype
  and trivy weekly and on dependency changes, [`security-scan.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml)); high and critical findings are fixed within
  the contract's window or time-boxed with a written exception. The
  [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) is repeated at
  every release and once a year by an independent tester.
- **Patching.** Base images rebuilt monthly and on advisories; Keycloak,
  Neo4j and Postgres on supported major versions ([ADR-030](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-030-neo4j-2025-lts-migration.md) for Neo4j, the
  [Postgres 16 to 17 runbook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/postgres-16-to-17-azure.md) for the pattern).
- **Backups and recovery.** Postgres with point-in-time restore across
  zones; Neo4j with daily backups and a restore test every quarter; Vault's
  state is on Postgres ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)) and the unseal keys in Key Vault with a
  documented recovery drill. Targets to agree in the contract: recovery
  point one hour, recovery time four hours for the hub, one working day for
  the SPE.
- **Availability.** 24x7; the demo's schedule is removed; health checks in
  every image ([finding F6](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings)) and probes in every app definition; two replicas
  for the hub and the proxy; the off-hours page becomes a maintenance page
  used only inside announced windows.
- **Key management.** Signing keys for credentials in an HSM; TLS
  certificates automated; every secret rotated at least yearly and on
  personnel change; the break-glass procedure with two-person approval and a
  log.
- **Supplier security** (C5 [SSO-01](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=97) to [SSO-05](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=101)): Keycloak, Neo4j, the EDC components,
  the cloud and the model provider assessed and listed with their
  attestations; the bills of materials in [`docs/sbom/`](/docs/security/sbom) are the inventory.
- **Exit.** Data export in [FHIR R4](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/) and [OMOP CDM](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html) is already the hub's
  interface; the contract names the format, the time and the deletion
  evidence at the end.

## 9. Klarbefund in a white-label deployment

The app changes owner but not architecture. The entity that places it on
the market:

- keeps the on-device default: values, pages and the explanation stay on the
  phone unless the person sends them ([self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment), [TR-03161-1](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2) O.Purp, O.Data);
- keeps the app lock and the encryption per record ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md), O.Auth,
  O.Cryp) and does not add analytics that see values;
- operates the sandbox-account service ([ADR-054](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-054-klarbefund-creates-a-sandbox-account-with-app-attest.md)) and, if offered, the
  explanation service ([ADR-034](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-034-claude-workload-identity-federation.md), [ADR-035](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-035-inference-provider-residency-and-quota.md)) in the EU under its own name and
  its own DPIA;
- publishes a privacy notice in the person's language and a vulnerability
  disclosure address;
- commissions the TR-03161 test and, if it claims interoperability with an
  EHR system ([Art. 48](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_48)), issues the label of [Art. 47](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_47); it does not claim DiGA status ([§ 139e SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__139e.html)) without
  the CE mark the DiGA route requires ([self-assessment, "Regulation"](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment#regulation));
- repeats the accuracy evidence on its own report formats before the pilot
  (the benchmark in [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence) is synthetic).

## 10. Before go-live: the checklist by role

| #   | Item                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Owner                              | Evidence                                                                                                           |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | Hosting contract with controllership per Art. 74 and Art. 28 GDPR terms per pair                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Access body, operator              | Signed contracts                                                                                                   |
| 2   | Cloud provider's C5 type 2 report reviewed; scope covers every service used                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Operator                           | Report, scope mapping                                                                                              |
| 3   | Operator's ISMS certified or on a dated plan; the building blocks of section 3 assigned                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Operator                           | Certificate or audit plan                                                                                          |
| 4   | DPIA for the platform and for the SPE                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Access body (controller)           | DPIA documents                                                                                                     |
| 5   | Network zones, private endpoints, WAF, TLS profile per [TR-02102-2](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TG02102/BSI-TR-02102-2.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=11) or [TR-03116-4](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/Technische-Richtlinien/TR-nach-Thema-sortiert/tr03116/TR-03116_node.html) | Operator                           | Architecture, scan from outside ([`check-hub-blackbox.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh) extended) |
| 6   | Keycloak in production mode, admin console private, MFA on privileged roles, realm in git                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Operator                           | Realm diff, [`guard-keycloak-console.sh --check`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh)                   |
| 7   | EUDI or eID sign-in for natural persons at assurance "high"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Operator, digital health authority | Conformance test of the wallet flow                                                                                |
| 8   | Encryption at rest with customer-managed keys; backups and a restore drill                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Operator                           | Key Vault configuration, drill record                                                                              |
| 9   | SPE isolated, no download path, output control procedure, annual audit scheduled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Access body, SPE operator          | Audit plan, procedure                                                                                              |
| 10  | Audit trail immutable, shipped to the SIEM, retention per section 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Operator                           | SIEM configuration, retention job                                                                                  |
| 11  | Incident procedure with the clocks of section 7 and named contacts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Operator, access body              | Procedure, contact list, a tabletop exercise                                                                       |
| 12  | Independent penetration test of the hub and the TR-03161 test of the app                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Operator, app owner                | Reports; findings closed or accepted in writing                                                                    |
| 13  | Off-hours schedule removed; replicas and probes in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Operator                           | App definitions                                                                                                    |
| 14  | Synthetic data removed from the production graph; seeds disabled; demo flag off                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Operator                           | `MATCH (p:Patient) RETURN count(p)` equals the holders' count; `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_TK` unset                         |
| 15  | Opt-out register wired into policy evaluation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Access body, operator              | Policy test with an opted-out record                                                                               |
| 16  | Vulnerability disclosure address published; supplier list with attestations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Operator                           | [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/SECURITY.md), supplier register                                                              |

## 11. What the demonstrator does not do

So that nobody reads more into it than is there:

- It is one tenant, one operator, one region, stopped at night.
- Its participants, access bodies and patients are fictional; its credentials
  are issued by its own issuer against no register.
- It has no SIEM, no WAF, no customer-managed keys, no backup of the graph,
  no MFA, and the secure processing environment is a set of views on the same
  database, not an isolated environment ([ADR-037](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-037-secure-processing-environment-confidential-computing.md) and [ADR-052](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-052-confidential-spe-on-azure-revisited.md) record what was
  assessed).
- It has had no independent penetration test and no TR-03161 test; the
  [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) is the project
  testing itself.
- Its EHDS article references are partly the [proposal's numbers](/docs/ehds/article-numbering); this
  document uses the adopted ones.

What it does have is the shape, the roles, the logging, the role-based
identity rules, the connectors and the exports that a real deployment
needs, with every decision written as an ADR and every claim tied to a test.
That is what makes it a reference and not a product.

## Sources

- [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng) on the European Health Data Space, OJ L, 5 March 2025.
- [Regulation (EU) 2016/679](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng) (GDPR), Art. [28](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_28), [33](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_33), [34](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_34), [35](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_35).
- [Directive (EU) 2022/2555](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2555/oj/eng) (NIS2) and its national transposition, the [BSIG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bsig_2025/__32.html).
- BSI, [Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5:2020](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5); [C5:2026](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Informationen-und-Empfehlungen/Empfehlungen-nach-Angriffszielen/Cloud-Computing/Kriterienkatalog-C5/C5_2025/C5_2025_node.html).
- BSI, [IT-Grundschutz-Kompendium](https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/IT-Grundschutz/IT-Grundschutz-Kompendium/it-grundschutz-kompendium_node.html), current edition; [BSI Standards 200-1 to 200-3](https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/IT-Grundschutz/BSI-Standards/bsi-standards_node.html).
- BSI [TR-02102-1](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TG02102/BSI-TR-02102-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=15) and [TR-02102-2](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TG02102/BSI-TR-02102-2.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=11), cryptographic mechanisms and TLS.
- BSI TR-03161, security requirements for digital health applications, parts [1](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2), [2](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-2.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2) and [3](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-3.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=4).
- BSI [TR-03116-4](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/Technische-Richtlinien/TR-nach-Thema-sortiert/tr03116/TR-03116_node.html), cryptographic requirements for federal projects, TLS.
