docs.title: The dashboards
docs.summary: The three Grafana dashboards of the live hub, with screenshots: EDC contracts and transfers, the EHDS audit trail, and the load and stress test; what each row shows, how to read it, and how to sign in.
docs.markdown:
# The dashboards

Three [Grafana](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/) dashboards show what the live hub does: the contracts and
transfers the connectors negotiate, the regulatory audit trail and its
integrity, and the platform under a load test. They run on the hub's own
Grafana at <https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red>, part of the observability stack
of [ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)
([OpenTelemetry](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/tag/v0.161.0) collector, [Prometheus](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/), [Loki](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/), [Tempo](https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/), Grafana, with Azure
Monitor and [Log Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-overview) for the containers and the connectors' logs).

| Dashboard                                                                                                                                               | Id                | Answers                                                                                                                | Default range, refresh |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| [EDC contracts and transfers](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-edc-dsp/edc-contracts-and-transfers?from=now-90d&to=now&timezone=browser&refresh=1m) | `mvhd-edc-dsp`    | What did the connectors negotiate and transfer, what was refused and why                                               | 24 hours, 1 minute     |
| [EHDS audit trail](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-ehds-audit/ehds-audit-trail?from=now-30d&to=now&timezone=browser&refresh=1m)                    | `mvhd-ehds-audit` | Is the evidence intact, what was recorded, what does an auditor copy                                                   | 24 hours, 1 minute     |
| [Load and stress test](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test)                                                             | `mvhd-load-test`  | What is [k6](https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/) doing, how fast does the hub answer, which container saturates first | 1 hour, 10 seconds     |

**Signing in.** Grafana asks for its own sign-in. The operator account's
password is the Key Vault secret `grafana-admin-password` in
`kv-mvhd-b53a0449`; the auditor's read-only account is
`keycloak-user-mvhd-auditor-password`. Nothing on these dashboards is a
patient's data: the audit trail keeps questions and queries as SHA-256 only,
and the load tests run against synthetic patients.

**When there is nothing to see.** The stack stops outside office hours
([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md)), so the panels
that read the proxy or the connectors are empty then; the ones that read
Azure Monitor keep their history. Widen the time range before concluding
that nothing happened; the **Newest record** panel says when the last thing
did.

**Where they come from.** The dashboards are JSON under
[`observability/grafana/dashboards-azure/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/observability/grafana/dashboards-azure)
(the Azure variants read Azure Monitor and Log Analytics) and
[`observability/grafana/dashboards/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/observability/grafana/dashboards)
(the compose stack reads Prometheus and Loki), generated by
[`observability/grafana/build-dashboards.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/observability/grafana/build-dashboards.py) and provisioned with the
observability app. A change to a dashboard is a change to its JSON, reviewed
like code.

## EDC contracts and transfers

![The EDC contracts and transfers dashboard over 90 days: 2,791 negotiations requested and 2,788 finalized, 2,787 transfers requested, 2,785 started, 794 refused for want of a data permit, one terminated; the negotiation states over time with one spike on 6 October, the load tests](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/edc-contracts-transfers.jpg)

Every [DSP](https://eclipse-dataspace-protocol-base.github.io/DataspaceProtocol/2025-1/) contract negotiation and data transfer, counted from the `dsp`
hash chain of the audit trail: the hub writes a record when it asks the
connector (requested) or refuses a transfer for want of a data permit, and
the connectors' callbacks write every later state (agreed, finalized,
started, completed, terminated). The dashboard is the operator's view of the
same records the auditor reads on the audit-trail dashboard.

| Row                                          | Panels                                                                                                 | How to read it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header                                       | What this shows; **Newest record**                                                                     | The newest record in the chain whatever the time range. "9 days ago" with empty panels means nothing was negotiated since: widen the range.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Contract negotiations (DSP)                  | Requested, Agreed, Finalized, Terminated or failed; **Negotiation states** over time                   | Requested and finalized should match over a quiet period; a gap is a negotiation that never came back from the connector, which the **Connector services** row explains. "Agreed" is a transient state and is normally 0.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Data transfers                               | Requested, Started, Completed, **Refused (no data permit)**, Terminated or failed; **Transfer states** | Refused is the gate working: [Art. 61(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#061.001), no access without a permit ([Art. 68](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_68)). The k6 contract journey asks for one on purpose, one time in four, so refusals carry a _Load test run_ tag and are expected ([#571](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/571)). |
| Refused, terminated and failed, with reasons | **Not completed** table                                                                                | Every record that is not a success, with the connector's reason, the parties and the run it belongs to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Connector services (EDC)                     | Errors by service, log lines by service, latest connector errors (Log Analytics)                       | ERROR and SEVERE lines per connector service, without the OpenTelemetry agent's own export errors. Zero is the normal case; the EDC services log at INFO only at start and on trouble, so a quiet hour is a healthy one.                                                                                                                                                                                         |

The numbers in the screenshot are the load tests of 5 and 6 October 2026:
about 2,800 negotiations and transfers in a few hours, every negotiation
finalized, and 794 transfers refused because the journey asked without a
permit. "Completed" stays at 0 because the data planes of the demo answer
with a started transfer and no completion callback; the transfer counts in
the [load-test results](/docs/operations/load-tests) are the started ones.

![The lower rows of the EDC dashboard: the Not completed table with the refused transfers of the stress run, each with its reason and parties; errors and log lines per connector service over 90 days from Log Analytics, with the spike of 15 September; the latest connector errors](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/edc-contracts-transfers-connectors.jpg)

The lower rows in the screenshot: every refused transfer of the stress run
with `did:web:pharmaco.de` as the party and the reason, and the connectors'
error lines over 90 days, where the one spike is the day the identity layer
was reseeded.

## EHDS audit trail

![The EHDS audit trail dashboard: both chains INTACT, 17,540 query records and 11,946 contract and transfer records over 30 days, 0 failed audit writes, 0 refused queries, 794 refused transfers; below, the newest records of the contract and transfer chain with hash, run, outcome, parties, time and sequence number](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/ehds-audit-trail.jpg)

The regulatory audit trail of [ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md):
every natural-language or federated query, every contract negotiation and
every transfer is a FHIR R4 [`AuditEvent`](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/auditevent.html), hash-chained to the one before it,
and a request whose record cannot be written is refused. The dashboard opens
with the auditor's guide, which an auditor can follow without the project:

![The auditor guide at the top of the dashboard: what the regulation asks, then seven steps from setting the audit period to writing down the chain heads, and the known limit of a chain that lives in the database it protects](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/ehds-audit-trail-guide.jpg)

| Row                               | Panels                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | How to read it                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Auditor guide                     | The regulation ([Art. 61(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#061.001), [68](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_68), [73(1)(e)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.001), [9](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_9); [GDPR Art. 5(2)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#005.002), [30](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_30)) and seven steps | The procedure of an audit, from the time picker to the report. Follow it in order.                                                                                                                                                    |
| Integrity of the evidence         | **Query chain**, Query records, **Contract & transfer chain**, Contract & transfer records, Audit writes failed, Refused queries, Refused transfers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Both chains must read **INTACT**: the proxy recomputes every hash from the first record on every refresh. **BROKEN** means a record was changed, removed or reordered: stop and escalate. Audit writes failed must be 0 or explained. |
| What was recorded                 | Contract and transfer records by kind; query records by kind                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | The volume over time, by record kind; a load test shows as a spike tagged with its run.                                                                                                                                               |
| Records, newest first             | Contract and transfer records; query records                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | One row per record: agreement, asset and permit, demo flag, hash, load-test run, outcome, parties, reason, time, who reported it, sequence number, what. Questions and Cypher appear as SHA-256 only.                                 |
| For the audit report: chain heads | Query chain head; contract & transfer chain head                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Copy both values, record count and hash, into the audit report. At the next audit the chain must still hold the same head at the same record number; if not, records were rewritten after the fact.                                   |

Two things an auditor should know, both on the dashboard itself: a record
marked **Demo** is demonstration traffic, not a real use; a record with a
**Load test run** was written by a k6 run against the hub with synthetic
traffic and is counted apart. And the known limit ([#418](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/418)): the chain lives in
Neo4j and proves order and integrity, but someone with write access to the
database could rebuild it from a point onward; comparing chain heads between
audits detects that, and a signed daily digest with a write-once copy is
what closes it. The raw records are FHIR `AuditEvent`s at
`/audit/chains/query/events` and `/audit/chains/dsp/events` on the proxy;
[`scripts/verify-audit-chain.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/verify-audit-chain.sh) recomputes the chain outside Grafana.

## Load and stress test

![The load and stress test dashboard on the stress run of 6 October 2026: virtual users climbing from 50 to 400, up to 107 requests a second, 0 % failed requests, 0 rate-limited, the worst check at 84.9 %, 15,091 iterations; the p95 by kind rising to 5.6 seconds for NLQ, 5.1 seconds for the API and 3.7 seconds for pages from the 200-user stage](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/load-stress-test.jpg)

What to watch while k6 runs against the hub ([#519](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/519)): the load the test
applies, the response time the client sees by kind and by endpoint, the
proxy's own view of the same run, and which container saturates first. The
dashboard is filtered by the run's **Test run** id ([`testid`](https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/using-k6/tags-and-groups/)), so two runs
never mix; the links in the [load-test results](/docs/operations/load-tests) open
each run on its own id and time range.

| Row                                  | Panels                                                                                                                                                                                     | How to read it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Load (k6): what the test is doing    | Virtual users, requests / s, **Failed requests**, Rate limited (429), Checks passed (worst check), Iterations; users and requests over time; responses by HTTP status                      | Failed is the share of requests with a status the step did not expect; the [SLO](https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/using-k6/thresholds/) is under 1 %. 429 is the rate limit, 5xx the hub failing, 0 a request that got no answer. The worst check names the SLO that broke first, "api under 1000 ms" for instance. |
| Response time, as the client sees it | **p95 by kind**: pages, API, NLQ, sign-in; p50, p95 and p99; p95 per endpoint; per endpoint table                                                                                          | The SLOs: pages under 2 s, API under 1 s, NLQ under 3 s. The endpoint table is sorted by p95; routes are named by their pattern, never by a URL with an id.                                                                                                                                                           |
| Server side: the proxy               | Requests / s by route, p95 by route, responses per minute by status, **audit records per transaction**, errors during the run                                                              | Measured in the proxy; the difference to the client-side p95 is the UI and the network. Audit records per transaction above 1 means the batch writer takes the load (hypothesis 2 of the runbook); at 1 every query waits for its own transaction.                                                                    |
| Azure: who saturates first           | CPU and memory as % of each app's limit, replicas, restarts, [Postgres](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/concepts-compute) burst credits (Azure Monitor) | Neo4j at 100 % CPU is the ceiling; Neo4j near 100 % memory ends in an out-of-memory kill (exit 137); replicas climbing is [the scale rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app); Postgres credits under about 10 throttle everything that shares the server.                             |

![The server-side row of the same run: requests a second by route on the proxy, the audit chain and the tasks and NLQ routes; p95 by route with two spikes to 5 seconds; the proxy's responses per minute, all 200 and 201; audit records per transaction between 1 and 7](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/load-stress-test-server.jpg)

![The Azure row of the same run: CPU as a share of each app's limit, with the UI at 99 % from the 400-user stage on, the proxy at 48 %, Neo4j at 35 %; memory with Neo4j at 74 %; three UI replicas; no restarts; Postgres burst credits at 39](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/load-stress-test-containers.jpg)

The screenshots are `20261006-2140-stress-aca`, the run that reached 400 users
with no failed request and moved the ceiling to the UI's CPU. How to read a
result hypothesis by hypothesis, and what each number meant for the sizing
decisions ([ADR-056](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-056-neo4j-grows-to-2-vcpu-and-4-gib.md),
[ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)), is the
[runbook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/load-and-stress-test.md).

## Keeping the screenshots current

The screenshots on this page were taken on 2026-10-16 from the live Grafana
in kiosk mode (`&kiosk` on the URL hides the chrome), at 1600 by 1200
pixels. A dashboard that changes gets a new screenshot the same way; the
files live in [`docs/operations/img/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/docs/operations/img) and the content generator copies them
to the hub.

docs.title: Load, stress and spike tests: results and dashboards
docs.summary: Every load, stress and spike run against the live hub and the compose stack, with the Grafana dashboard of each, what it found, what changed because of it, and the runs still to do.
docs.markdown:
# Load, stress and spike tests: results and dashboards

What the live hub at <https://ehds.mabu.red> does under load, measured with the
[k6](https://github.com/grafana/k6/releases/tag/v2.3.0) suite in [`load-tests/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/load-tests) and recorded on the platform's
Grafana. This page is the index: every run, what it found, what changed
because of it, and the runs still to do. The detailed reports are linked, and
every live run has its dashboard link.

The dashboards need a sign-in on <https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red> and show
data only while the stack is up (it stops off hours, [ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md)). Each link
opens the **Load and stress test** dashboard on the run's `testid` and time
range; the raw k6 summaries are on the laptop that ran them
(`load-tests/results/<testid>*`) and in the issues.

| Scenario    | What it does                                                | Last run live     | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `smoke`     | 1 user, 30 s, every endpoint once                           | 2026-10-05        | passes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `load`      | 50 users, 15 min, the persona mix                           | 2026-10-06, 21:15 | **passes every SLO**: p95 155 ms API, 43 ms pages, 217 ms NLQ, 0 failed                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `audited`   | 1 to 20 parallel NLQ queries through the audit chain        | 2026-10-05        | passes after [#534](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/534) and [#536](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/536) (per-user rate limit)                                                                                                                |
| `contracts` | up to 10 users negotiating and transferring through the EDC | 2026-11-11, 18:56 | **fails on latency** since it transfers: 465 requests, 0 failed, 61 of 61 agreed and transferred, API p95 1.58 s on `GET /api/transfers` and the catalogue ([report](/docs/developer/edc-sizing-under-load#transfers-under-load-the-evening-runs)); without transfers it passed at 12:32 (p95 775 ms) |
| `stress`    | 50, 100, 200, 400 users, abort on failed requests           | 2026-10-06, 21:40 | **400 users, 0 failed**; latency SLOs break from 200 users, ceiling: UI                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `spike`     | a sudden jump to many users and back                        | not yet           | next, after [`size-ui.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/size-ui.sh) ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md))                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `soak`      | a steady load for two hours                                 | not yet           | after `spike`; measures the Postgres burst credits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `signin`    | 5 to 50 sign-ins a minute against Keycloak                  | not yet live      | compose: 12 of 127 sign-ins over 3 s                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `proxy`     | the proxy alone, 5 to 25 users                              | not yet live      | needs a job inside the environment; compose passes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## The live runs, newest first

### 2026-11-11 evening: contracts with transfers

The scenario now waits for each agreement and transfers on it. Two runs on
Azure,
[`20261111-1847-contracts-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1847-contracts-aca&from=1794422760000&to=1794423300000)
on a cold stack and
[`20261111-1856-contracts-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1856-contracts-aca&from=1794423300000&to=1794423840000)
on a warm one: 0 failed requests, every negotiation agreed and every transfer
`STARTED` in the connector (115 in all, 37 more refused for want of a permit,
all on the DSP audit chain), and both over the API SLO (p95
1.37 s, 1.58 s). The transfer POST stays under 1 s; the slow calls are
`GET /api/transfers`, which reads the newest 200 transfer processes, and the
catalogue request. Details in
[EDC sizing under load](/docs/developer/edc-sizing-under-load#transfers-under-load-the-evening-runs).

### 2026-11-11: contracts at the ADR-089 sizes

The first `contracts` runs that negotiated for real, against the Java EDC
apps halved by [ADR-089](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-089-the-java-edc-apps-shrink-to-what-they-use.md).
[`20261111-1232-contracts-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1232-contracts-aca&from=1794400260000&to=1794400800000)
held every threshold: 559 requests, 0 failed, checks 99.28 %, p95 775 ms.
The two runs before it found two bugs in the scenario (the compose DSP address,
then an offer sent without its policy), and the first of them shows that no
October `contracts` run on Azure negotiated at all. The report, with each EDC
app's CPU and memory against its new size, is
[EDC sizing under load](/docs/developer/edc-sizing-under-load).

### 2026-10-06 evening: load and stress after the fixes of the day

Stack: Neo4j at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB ([ADR-056](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-056-neo4j-grows-to-2-vcpu-and-4-gib.md)), the graph views capped at the
newest 30 access events ([#580](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/580)), the onboarding agent's retry loop fixed ([#581](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/581)),
the task store on the Flexible Server ([#589](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/589)).

| Run                                                                                                                                                                       | Users             | Requests        | Failed     | p95 all / API / pages / NLQ       | Verdict                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`20261006-2115-load-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-2115-load-aca&from=1791321300000&to=1791322320000)     | 50 for 15 min     | 19,509 (21.5/s) | **0.00 %** | 146 ms / 155 ms / 43 ms / 217 ms  | every SLO held, checks 99.97 %                               |
| [`20261006-2140-stress-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-2140-stress-aca&from=1791322800000&to=1791324300000) | 50 to 400, 20 min | 81,518 (63.6/s) | **0.00 %** | 3.35 s / 3.53 s / 3.23 s / 4.93 s | latency SLOs crossed from 200 users on; every answer correct |

The ceiling was the UI: three replicas of half a core at 99 % CPU from the
400-user stage on, Neo4j at 0.82 of its 2 cores and 2.66 GB of 4 GiB, the
proxy at 0.06 cores. The errors in the logs were the UI calling the EDC
management API at the wrong address (about 8,900 404 lines in the stress run),
which [#648](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/648) pins on every deploy; the EDC pages did no real work in these runs,
so the next `load` after it moves the numbers.

What changed because of it: [ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md),
a whole core per UI replica, up to six replicas on an HTTP concurrency rule of
15, applied by [`scripts/azure/size-ui.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/size-ui.sh); a deploy now waits while a run is on
(`LOAD_TEST_RUNNING`), because a merge on 2026-10-06 redeployed the UI and the
proxy in the middle of a run.

### 2026-10-06 afternoon: the first stress run to 400 users

| Run                                                                                                                                                                       | Users         | Requests      | Failed           | p95 API / pages / NLQ        | Verdict                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`20261006-1728-stress-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-1728-stress-aca&from=1791307740000&to=1791309060000) | 50 to 400     | 84,624 (66/s) | **0.00 %**       | 3.19 s / 2.8 s / 4.35 s      | all stages reached; Neo4j did not restart after [ADR-056](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-056-neo4j-grows-to-2-vcpu-and-4-gib.md)                                                                                             |
| [`20261006-1455-load-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-1455-load-aca&from=1791298500000&to=1791299520000)     | 50 for 15 min | 10,000+       | 0.03 %           | pages and API under the SLOs | with [#580](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/580) and [#579](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/579) deployed; both audit chains intact after the run |
| [`20261006-1152-load-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-1152-load-aca&from=1791287580000&to=1791288600000)     | 50 for 15 min |               | 0                | 151 ms overall               | with [#576](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/576); ran beside the onboarding agent's retry loop ([#577](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/577))    |
| [`20261006-stress-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-stress-aca&from=1791274440000&to=1791275580000)           | 50 to 400     |               | 2.1 % at the end | `/api/graph` 64 s at the end | aborted at about 300 users: Neo4j killed for memory (exit 137)                                                                                                                                            |
| [`20261006-load-aca`](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261006-load-aca&from=1791273300000&to=1791274320000)               | 50 for 15 min |               | 0                |                              | the morning baseline inside the environment                                                                                                                                                               |

The morning stress run found Neo4j's ceiling by memory; the afternoon run,
after [`size-neo4j.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/size-neo4j.sh) (2 vCPU, 4 GiB, heap 1.5 GiB, page cache 1 GiB), reached
400 users with no failed request and moved the ceiling to the UI. A load run in
between (`20261006-1359-load-aca`) failed on latency because the onboarding
agent was retrying a stuck credential request thirty times a second in the
background ([#577](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/577)); the fix ([#581](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/581)) went out before the evening runs.

### 2026-10-05: the baseline

The first runs against the live hub, from a laptop in Berlin, with the
platform's side from Azure Monitor: [the Azure baseline](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/loadtest/2026-10-baseline.md).
50 users for 15 minutes passed with no failed request but an API p95 of
1.8 s, with `/api/graph` at 10 s; the audited queries hit the proxy's rate
limit (83.6 % 429 before [#534](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/534), 23.2 % after). Neo4j at 97 % of its 2 GiB was
the first ceiling. The same suite against [the compose stack](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/loadtest/2026-10-05-local.md)
on a laptop, for comparison: load passes every SLO at 50 users, stress breaks
between 100 and 200 users on the UI's CPU.

![Load and stress test dashboard, 50 users against ehds.mabu.red on 2026-10-05](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/2026-10-05-load-azure.png)

## Where the platform stands

The [production readiness assessment of October 2026](/docs/operations/production-readiness-2026-10)
reads these runs together with the security work and the ADRs against the
[Well-Architected](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/pillars) and [Cloud Adoption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/) frameworks, pillar by pillar: what is in
place, what is open, and what stands between the demonstrator and an
operable platform.

## What the dashboard shows

The **Load and stress test** dashboard ([`observability/grafana/dashboards-azure/load-stress-test.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/observability/grafana/dashboards-azure/load-stress-test.json))
has three rows, each filtered by the run's `testid`:

- **Load (k6): what the test is doing**: virtual users, requests per second,
  failed requests, p95 per group (pages, API, NLQ), the slowest endpoints.
- **Server side: the proxy**: requests and p95 by route, rate-limit refusals,
  the audit chain's records per transaction, the log lines of this run.
- **Containers**: CPU and memory of the UI, the proxy, Neo4j, Keycloak and the
  connectors, replicas, and the Flexible Server's burst credits.

The **EDC contracts and transfers** dashboard ([`mvhd-edc-dsp`](/docs/operations/dashboards#edc-contracts-and-transfers)) follows the
negotiations and transfers a `contracts` run drives through the connectors.
How to read a result, hypothesis by hypothesis, is in the
[runbook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/load-and-stress-test.md).

## The runs still to do

1. `stress` after [`scripts/azure/size-ui.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/size-ui.sh) ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)): where the 1 s API SLO
   first breaks with whole-core replicas; the per-stage p95 goes into the
   ADR's table.
2. `spike`, then `soak` for two hours: the Postgres burst credits (hypothesis
   4 of the runbook) and the cost per 1,000 requests from [Cost Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/overview-cost-management) over
   the soak window.
3. `signin` live: whether sign-in is a singleton (hypothesis 6).
4. `load` once more with the EDC pages doing real work ([#648](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/648) pins the
   connector's address on every deploy).

Each inside office hours, announced, one at a time; a deploy waits while a run
is on. The procedure is the [runbook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/load-and-stress-test.md);
the open items are tracked in [#571](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/571).

## Reproduce

```bash
scripts/azure/run-load-test.sh load            # inside Azure, as a Container Apps job
ABORT_ON=failures scripts/azure/run-load-test.sh stress
load-tests/run.sh load azure                   # from a laptop, metrics to a local Grafana
```

The sessions are forged for ten users per persona and handed to the job as a
secret; nothing real signs in. The suite, its scenarios and its thresholds are
documented in [`load-tests/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/load-tests/README.md).

docs.title: Production readiness assessment, October 2026
docs.summary: The Well-Architected and Cloud Adoption assessment as of 2026-10-16: what is in place per pillar, with the evidence, what is open, the scores, and what stands between the demonstrator and an operable platform.
docs.markdown:
# Production readiness assessment, October 2026

[Well-Architected Framework (WAF)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/pillars) and [Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/), applied
to the EHDS Integration Hub as it runs on [Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/overview) on 2026-10-16.
Each pillar states what is in place, with the evidence, and what is still
open. The scores are the project's own judgement on a ten-point scale; none
of this is an independent audit. The WAF has five pillars; sustainability is not one of them but
Microsoft's separate [sustainability guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/sustainability/) for workloads, assessed here beside them.

| Pillar                                                                                                          | Score    | In one line                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WAF: [Operational Excellence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/operational-excellence/) | 7/10     | Deploy on every merge, tracing and structured logs, sixteen runbooks; no alert rules, no on-call                                                                                                    |
| WAF: [Security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/security/)                             | 8/10     | Tested by the project with nine of ten findings closed; no independent test                                                                                                                         |
| WAF: [Reliability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/reliability/)                       | 6/10     | 400 users with no failed request, health checks everywhere, managed Postgres with restore; Neo4j one node, no backup                                                                                |
| WAF: [Performance Efficiency](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/performance-efficiency/) | 7/10     | Sized from measurements, 50 users inside every SLO; 200 users not yet                                                                                                                               |
| WAF: [Cost Optimization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/cost-optimization/)           | 7/10     | Everything stops off hours, cost per 1,000 requests measured; no cost allocation per tenant                                                                                                         |
| Sustainability (separate guidance, not a WAF pillar)                                                            | 6/10     | The stack runs a third of the week; no carbon-aware choice                                                                                                                                          |
| CAF: [Strategy & Plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/strategy/)              | 8/10     | The EHDS roles, the BSI standards and sixty decisions ([ADR-001](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-001-postgresql-neo4j-split.md) to [ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)) written down; no SLA |
| CAF: [Govern & Manage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/govern/)                | 6/10     | Retention policy, audit trail, incident clocks; no SOC, no named incident team                                                                                                                      |
| **Overall**                                                                                                     | **7/10** | **A measured demonstrator. Not an operable platform for real data; the gap is listed at the end.**                                                                                                  |

The platform assessed: the hub and its connectors on Azure Container Apps in
`rg-mvhd-dev`, West Europe, 21 apps and 9 jobs. PostgreSQL on a Flexible
Server ([ADR-041](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-041-managed-postgres-on-azure-containerised-locally.md)),
Neo4j Community at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB ([ADR-056](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-056-neo4j-grows-to-2-vcpu-and-4-gib.md)),
the UI on whole cores with up to six replicas ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)),
Vault with its state on the Flexible Server ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)),
stopped outside office hours ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md),
[ADR-058](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-058-azure-triggers-the-off-hours-schedule.md)). The
load numbers are the runs in [the results index](/docs/operations/load-tests); the security
state is the [security test report of 2026-10-15](/docs/security/security-test-report);
how the platform is meant to be run for real is the
[operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline).

## WAF pillar 1: Operational Excellence, 7/10

In place:

- A merge to main deploys to Azure ([`deploy-azure.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml)); the deploy waits
  while a load test runs and pins the connector addresses on every run. The
  PR gate, the test, security and [CodeQL](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli) workflows run on every pull request,
  the compliance suites after changes to main; [`demo-smoke.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/demo-smoke.yml) runs [Bruno](https://www.usebruno.com/), [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) and [ZAP](https://www.zaproxy.org/) against the
  live hub.
- [OpenTelemetry](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/tag/v0.161.0) collector, [Prometheus](https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/), [Loki](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/), [Tempo](https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/) and [Grafana](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/)
  ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md));
  the proxy is traced ([`src/tracing.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/tracing.ts)) and logs structured JSON with the
  caller and the run on every line ([`pino`](https://getpino.io/)); every audit record carries its
  run. Logs in Azure Monitor for 30 days.
- Vault keeps its state across restarts, locally in a file and on Azure in a
  database on the Flexible Server with an unseal sidecar ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)).
- Sixteen runbooks under [`docs/knowledge/runbooks/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks): deploy, seeding, realm
  drift, Postgres recovery, off hours, load and stress test, the audit chain,
  the Klarbefund connection.
- Every image carries a [`HEALTHCHECK`](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#healthcheck); the crawlers expose `/metrics` and are
  checked on it; the seed phases are resumable.
- The documentation is published from the repository and checked in
  pre-commit, so the docs cannot drift from the files.

Open:

- No alert rules. The load dashboard, the audit chain and the Postgres burst
  credits are read by a person; nobody is paged.
- No on-call model and no named operator; the operational guideline
  describes the roles, the project cannot fill them.
- No feature flags beyond the demo switches.

## WAF pillar 2: Security, 8/10

In place:

- The [security test report of 2026-10-15](/docs/security/security-test-report):
  CodeQL, [Semgrep](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep/releases/tag/v1.176.0), [grype](https://github.com/anchore/grype/releases/tag/v0.118.0), npm audit, [trivy](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/tag/v0.74.0), [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/tag/v8.30.1), [hadolint](https://github.com/hadolint/hadolint), [shellcheck](https://www.shellcheck.net/),
  the app's posture tests and 46 anonymous black-box checks of the live hub.
  Ten findings; nine closed, one reviewed and accepted (the published
  development key of the local compose stack; Azure takes its keys from
  Vault).
- The [threat model of the hub](/docs/security/threat-model-hub) and
  [of the app](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund), each mitigation
  naming the code or test that shows it; one [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/) bill of materials per
  deployable part ([SBOM](/docs/security/sbom)), checked against the lockfiles.
- Every API route needs a session ([ADR-044](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-044-every-api-route-needs-a-session.md));
  who sees a patient's identity is decided by role, never by a query
  parameter; the UI reads the graph directly and the proxy serves the data
  planes ([ADR-043](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-043-graph-access-direct-or-through-the-proxy.md)).
- Rate limits in the proxy, per user and per participant, measured under
  load; k-anonymity with a minimum cohort of five in the proxy's
  configuration.
- Operator secrets are Key Vault references ([ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md));
  the live `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was rotated; participant keys live in Vault.
- Keycloak: login events kept seven days, the UI client's scope limited to
  the seven EHDS roles, the admin console off the internet, every privileged
  role behind the console guard. The app locks with Face ID or the passcode
  ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)).
- Only the hub and Keycloak have public ingress; everything else is internal
  to the environment.
- The [audit retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md): ten years for
  access, transfer, contract and permit records, two years for sign-ins and
  edge logs, applied by `/api/admin/audit/retention`, which cannot destroy
  the only copy.

Open:

- No independent penetration test of the hub and no [TR-03161](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2) test of the app;
  the report's last section says what each would add.
- No mTLS between apps and no private endpoints; the guideline asks for both
  before real data.
- Neo4j has one database user; access is controlled in the hub and the proxy.
- Secret rotation is written down, not scheduled.
- The operator accounts and `edcadmin` are on generated passwords in Key Vault
  only once [`scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh) has run against the live realm.

## WAF pillar 3: Reliability, 6/10

In place:

- The stress run of 2026-10-06 reached 400 users with 0 failed requests out
  of 81,518, at 63.6 requests a second; nothing restarted. At 50 users every
  SLO holds.
- Every image has a health check and Container Apps [probes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/health-probes) come from it; the
  proxy drains on `SIGTERM`; every outbound call has a timeout; `/api/tasks`
  answers from its store when the connector fails and says so.
- PostgreSQL on the Flexible Server keeps seven days of [point-in-time](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/concepts-backup-restore)
  restore; the realm, the contracts and the task store live there. Vault's
  state is there too.
- The graph views are capped at the newest 30 access events, which removed
  the one request that could take the UI down.
- A deploy cannot land in the middle of a load run.

Open:

- Neo4j is one Community node on Azure Files with no backup. Its data is
  re-seedable synthetic data today; before any real data the guideline asks
  for Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph with backups tested quarterly.
- No circuit breaker; a slow connector is bounded by timeouts only.
- From 200 users the latency SLOs break on the UI's CPU. The UI's new size
  ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)) is applied by `scripts/azure/size-ui.sh` and not yet measured.
- The connectors' pages did no real work in the runs so far (the UI called
  the management API at the wrong address, pinned since); the next `load`
  run is the first with contracts and transfers under load.
- No chaos engineering; the stress runs are the nearest thing.

## WAF pillar 4: Performance Efficiency, 7/10

In place:

- Measured, not guessed: the ceiling moved from Neo4j's memory to the UI's
  CPU within one day of runs, and each size was decided from the measurement
  ([ADR-056](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-056-neo4j-grows-to-2-vcpu-and-4-gib.md) for Neo4j, [ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md) for the UI, with the
  [scalability per component](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md#scalability-per-component)).
- At 50 users: API p95 155 ms, pages 43 ms, NLQ 217 ms, 21.5 requests a
  second. `/api/graph` inside the SLO after the cap and the resize.
- Neo4j at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, heap 1.5 GiB, page cache 1 GiB; indexes for
  every FHIR query path in [`neo4j/init-schema.cypher`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/neo4j/init-schema.cypher) (more than 70, three
  vector indexes).
- The audit chain's batch writer takes the write load; audited queries are
  not a ceiling (434 ms p95 at about 16 a second).
- Next.js compresses its responses; the static demo is served by GitHub
  Pages.

Open:

- No response cache on the catalog or the overview; no compression in the
  proxy.
- 200 users inside the SLOs is the target of the next `stress` run, after
  `size-ui.sh`; the per-stage p95 goes into [ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)'s table.
- No CDN in front of the live hub.

## WAF pillar 5: Cost Optimization, 7/10

In place:

- Everything stops at 18:13 UTC and starts at 05:17 UTC on weekdays,
  triggered by Azure as a managed identity; about 65 office hours a week. The
  decision followed a month that billed €741 against an estimate of €426 for
  a stack running around the clock ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md)).
- Container Apps scale rules: the UI on an HTTP concurrency rule of 15, one
  to six replicas; everything to zero off hours.
- The cost of a request is known: at list price the apps that serve a request
  bill about $0.60 an hour, about **$0.01 per 1,000 requests at 50 users**
  ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md), from `20261006-2115-load-aca`); a 20-minute stress run at six UI
  replicas adds about $0.22.
- Cost guards watch the total ([`cost-guards.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/cost-guards.yml)).

Open:

- One resource group, one bill: no cost allocation per tenant or per role.
- The cost per 1,000 requests from [Cost Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/overview-cost-management) over a `soak` window is
  still to be taken.

## Sustainability, 6/10 (separate guidance, not a WAF pillar)

Assessed against Microsoft's [sustainable workload guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/sustainability/),
which sits beside the five WAF pillars rather than among them.

In place:

- The stack runs a third of the week ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md), [ADR-058](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-058-azure-triggers-the-off-hours-schedule.md)).
- Resource use is visible: the containers row of the load dashboard, Cost
  Management.
- The one wasteful request, the uncapped graph view, is gone.

Open:

- West Europe, no carbon signal in the schedule or the region choice.

## CAF

**Strategy and plan, 8/10.** The regulatory motivation is written per article
(Regulation (EU) [2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng) in its adopted numbering); the
[operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline) names which
EHDS role operates which part and what [BSI C5](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5), [IT-Grundschutz](https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/IT-Grundschutz/IT-Grundschutz-Kompendium/it-grundschutz-kompendium_node.html), [TR-02102](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TG02102/BSI-TR-02102-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=15) and
TR-03161 ask of each; sixty [ADRs](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/docs/ADRs), [ADR-001](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-001-postgresql-neo4j-split.md) to [ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md), recorded the decisions on 2026-10-16; the planning index
tracks the work. Open: a formal SLA for participants, which the guideline
puts into the operator's service contract.

**Ready, 7/10.** Azure from a merge; the local stack in one compose command;
the seed phases resumable; one Dockerfile per part with its bill of
materials. Open: the operator's own environment, which does not exist yet.

**Adopt, 7/10.** The hub's own [DSP 2025-1](https://eclipse-dataspace-protocol-base.github.io/DataspaceProtocol/2025-1/), [DCP](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/) and EHDS checks ([`run-ehds-dataspace-checks.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-dataspace-checks.sh), [`run-ehds-identity-checks.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh), [`run-ehds-tests.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-tests.sh))
run after changes to main, once a night since [ADR-074](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-074-e2e-and-compliance-suites-run-nightly-when-main-changed.md); they are not the
Eclipse [DSP TCK](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dsp-tck) or [DCP TCK](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dcp-tck), neither of which has been run yet; the Bruno collection asserts every route by persona
([ADR-031](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-031-checks-must-assert.md), [ADR-032](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-032-persona-organised-api-collection.md));
on 2026-10-15 the [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) counted 2,488 UI unit tests and 419 Swift tests. Open: chaos
engineering, and a rehearsal of the Neo4j 5 to 2025 migration
([ADR-030](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-030-neo4j-2025-lts-migration.md)).

**Govern and manage, 6/10.** The retention policy and the tamper-evident
audit trail exist ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)); the incident clocks of GDPR and NIS2 and who
holds each are in the guideline ([section 7](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#7-incidents-clocks-and-who-notifies-whom)); the EHDS roles have their
go-live checklist ([section 10](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#10-before-go-live-the-checklist-by-role)). Open: an SLA and its dashboard, an incident
response plan with a named team, change management beyond pull requests,
cost allocation per tenant, an independent test.

## What stands between the demonstrator and an operable platform

The gap is no longer in the code; it is in the operation, and the
[guideline's checklist](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#10-before-go-live-the-checklist-by-role)
lists it by EHDS role. The items the project itself can still do:

| #   | Item                                                                                                                                                  | Pillar                   | Tracked in                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `stress` after `size-ui.sh`, then `spike`, `soak` and `signin`; the per-stage p95 into [ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md) | Performance, Reliability | [#571](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/571)                                                                                                     |
| 2   | Alert rules on the load dashboard and the audit chain, and who is paged                                                                               | Operational Excellence   | open                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 3   | A Neo4j backup, or Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph, before any non-synthetic data                                                                 | Reliability              | [guideline, section 2](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#2-hosting-architecture-from-the-demo-to-an-operable-platform)                                                     |
| 4   | Compression and a short cache on the catalog and overview responses                                                                                   | Performance              | open                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 5   | Secret rotation on a schedule: the Keycloak clients, the account service, the catalog token                                                           | Security                 | [guideline, section 2](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#2-hosting-architecture-from-the-demo-to-an-operable-platform)                                                     |
| 6   | An independent penetration test of the hub and a TR-03161 test of the app                                                                             | Security                 | [#655](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/655)                                                                                                     |
| 7   | Operator accounts and `edcadmin` on generated passwords in Key Vault ([`scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh))   | Security                 | [#671](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/671) added the script; running it against the live realm is open                                           |
| 8   | An SLA with its dashboard, and the incident response plan with a named team                                                                           | Govern and manage        | guideline, sections [7](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#7-incidents-clocks-and-who-notifies-whom) and [8](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#8-operating-the-platform) |

docs.title: Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
docs.summary: How a change reaches the live hub: discussions and issues, branches and pull requests, every pre-commit and pre-push hook with its fix, the PR Gate and the other workflows, the deploys to Azure and GitHub Pages, releases, how to contribute from outside, and how to define an SDLC for a DevSecOps and AI project, with the tools for each stage.
docs.markdown:
# Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) - **Project:** Minimum Viable Health Dataspace v2 (EHDS reference implementation) - **Audience:** contributors, reviewers, and anyone who wants to know how a one-person, AI-assisted project keeps a regulated-domain codebase shippable. - **Last updated:** 2026-11-07 - **Maintainer:** Matthias ([`@ma3u`](https://github.com/ma3u)) How a change gets from an idea to the live hub: issues and discussions, branches and pull requests, the hooks on your machine, the checks on GitHub, the deploys, the releases, and how to contribute from outside. The plain-language version is [How We Build This Software](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/SDLC-explained.md); how the AI author fits in is [Deterministic Agentic AI Development with Claude Code](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/AGENTIC-DEVELOPMENT-WITH-CLAUDE-CODE.md). Two companion pages go deeper: [Integration tests through the APIs](/docs/developer/api-integration-tests) and [The stack and the development environment](/docs/developer/stack-and-environment). Section 12 is the recipe behind all of it: how to define an SDLC for a DevSecOps and AI project, stage by stage, with the tools.
Acronyms used in this document | Acronym | Expansion | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **CI/CD** | Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery: the automated build, test and deploy | | **PR** | Pull Request: a proposed change, checked and reviewed before it is merged | | **ADR** | Architecture Decision Record: a short note of a decision and its reasons | | **[OIDC](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html)** | OpenID Connect; here the federated login of GitHub Actions to Azure | | **[SBOM](https://cyclonedx.org/)** | Software Bill of Materials: the list of every third-party component | | **[CVE](https://www.cve.org/)** | Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures: the public catalogue of known flaws | | **[SARIF](https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/sarif-v2.1.0.html)** | Static Analysis Results Interchange Format: how scanners report to GitHub | | **[DSP](https://eclipse-dataspace-protocol-base.github.io/DataspaceProtocol/2025-1/) / [DCP](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/) / TCK** | Dataspace Protocol / Decentralised Claims Protocol / Technology Compatibility Kit | | **[ACA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/)** | Azure Container Apps, where the live hub runs |
--- ## 1. Philosophy: deterministic tooling around a non-deterministic author > **The author proposes; deterministic tooling disposes.** A senior engineer, a newcomer and an AI agent are all non-deterministic: ask the same question twice and you may get two answers. The output becomes trustworthy when the author is wrapped in gates that run the same way every time, for everyone: formatters, linters, type checks, tests, security scanners and a CI/CD pipeline. The project is a team of one plus an AI pair programmer. So it keeps every deterministic gate a large team would have and collapses the coordination ceremonies (mandatory human review, sprint rituals, release boards) that only pay off with more people. Section 11 says what is collapsed and why. This matters more here than in most projects. It is a reference implementation of the European Health Data Space, a regulated domain with health data, patient rights and audit duties. The gates buy trust (whole classes of mistakes are caught before they ship), auditability (every change is logged with author, time and reason), repeatability, cheap mistakes (a local hook costs seconds, a production incident hours) and safe AI assistance. --- ## 2. The lifecycle at a glance ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Idea"] --> Q{"Question or
open design?"} Q -- yes --> DI["GitHub Discussion"] DI --> I Q -- no --> I["GitHub Issue
open tasks + test steps"] I --> B{"Architectural
decision?"} B -- yes --> C["ADR
docs/ADRs/ADR-NNN"] B -- no --> D["Short-lived branch"] C --> D D --> E["Change
human + Claude Code"] E --> F["pre-commit hooks
(31, on your machine)"] F --> P["pre-push hooks
(4: Vitest, iOS analyte parity, CodeQL Swift, npm audit)"] P --> G["Pull request"] G --> H["PR Gate (required)
+ advisory workflows"] H -- "red: fix and push again" --> E H -- "green" --> M["Squash merge to main"] M --> K["Deploy: Azure Container Apps
+ GitHub Pages"] M --> R["Release when ui/package.json
version changes"] M --> S["Smoke and compliance runs on main"] ``` 1. **Idea.** An open question or a design to explore starts as a Discussion; a piece of work starts as an Issue (section 3). 2. **ADR** when the decision is expensive to reverse or cross-cutting. 3. **Branch** off `main`, short-lived. 4. **Change**, by a human, Claude Code or both. 5. **Hooks** on your machine: 31 at commit, 4 at push (section 5). 6. **Pull request.** The **PR Gate** is the one required check; the other workflows are advisory (section 6). 7. **Squash merge** once the PR Gate is green and every review thread is resolved. 8. **On `main`:** the live hub and the static demo redeploy, the smoke and compliance runs start, and a release is cut when the version changed (sections 7 and 8). --- ## 3. Discussions, issues and the planning folder ### Discussion or issue? [Discussions](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/discussions) are enabled, with the categories Announcements, General, Ideas, Polls, Q&A and Show and tell. | Open a **Discussion** when | Open an **Issue** when | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | you have a question ("how does the hub map X?"), want to compare options, or propose a direction that is not yet a task (Ideas; recent examples are [#776](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/discussions/776) on FHIR and OMOP tooling and [#701](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/discussions/701) on Simpl-Open) | there is something to do: a bug, a feature with a clear outcome, a gap with an acceptance criterion | | the answer may be "no" or "not now" | someone will close it with a commit or a PR | | several people should weigh in before anything is decided | the decision is made, or an ADR will make it | A discussion that reaches a decision becomes an issue (and an ADR when the decision is architectural), linked both ways. ### What an issue carries Use the templates in [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE) (bug report, feature request). Every issue that is being worked on carries: - **The open tasks** as a checklist, kept current. When a PR leaves work undone, the issue says what is left; nothing open lives only in a chat or a commit message. - **Manual test steps** with links (to the static docs, a page of the hub, a workflow run), so anyone can check the result without asking. - **The decisions**, each linked to its ADR. [Labels](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/labels) in use: `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, `infrastructure`, `azure`, `dependencies`, the priorities `P1` to `P3`, and the area labels `EHDS-compliance`, `dataspace-discovery`, `simpl`, `NLP`, `Agentic AI`, `production`, `load test`, `stress test`, `pentest`, `trivy`, `Cost`. New contributors look for `good first issue` and `help wanted`. ### The planning folder [`docs/planning/index.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/planning/index.md) lists work items as files that move `future/ → current/ → done/` and are never deleted. A file in `current/` is the long form of an issue (its phases, measurements, links); the issue stays the place for the checklist. Roadmap detail lives in `docs/planning/roadmap-phases-*.md`, and the issue and ADR tables in [`docs/planning-health-dataspace-v2.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/planning-health-dataspace-v2.md). [`/plan`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/commands/plan.md) in Claude Code grooms the folder.
