Branches, commits and pull requests - **Trunk-based.** `main` is always deployable. Work happens on short-lived branches named `type/short-slug` (`feat/…`, `fix/…`, `docs/…`, `chore/…`, `ci/…`), often with the issue number: `fix/708-ui-sticky-sessions`. - **[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)** with a scope: `feat(spe): workspaces start on demand (ADR-072)`. All of the last 40 commits on `main` follow it; no hook enforces it yet. - **Commits carry the author's name.** No AI co-author trailer is added; how the AI works in this project is documented in the companion document. - **A PR links its issue and its ADRs** and says how it was tested; the [PR template](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) asks for both. [`CODEOWNERS`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) names the maintainer, so a PR from anyone else gets a review request. - **Squash merge.** The PR title becomes the commit on `main`, so it follows the commit convention too. ### 4.1 Branch protection on `main` A repository ruleset on the default branch: | Rule | Effect | | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Require a pull request** | No direct pushes to `main`. Zero approvals required (see below). | | **Require conversation resolution** | Every review thread is resolved before merge, so review findings are answered rather than scrolled past. | | **Require status checks** | **PR Gate** must be green. It is the only required check. | | **Require linear history** | Squash or rebase only; merge commits are switched off. | | **Block force pushes, deletions** | `main` cannot be rewritten or deleted. | **Zero required approvals is deliberate.** With one maintainer, a required approval means a second account and a rubber stamp. Review is done by the AI reviewers and the gates; the mechanical protections (no direct push, no force push, no merge on red) are the part a solo maintainer cannot supply by discipline, so they are enforced. When a second regular contributor joins, this goes to one approval. **Admins can bypass only on a pull request.** A stuck check can be overridden on a PR, which is better than being unable to land a hotfix on a live demo; a direct push to `main` is refused for everyone. ### 4.2 Why exactly one required check Every other workflow is path-filtered, which is right for cost and wrong for branch protection: a required check that never starts stays pending, and the PR can never merge ([#303](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/303) collected 28 checks, [#305](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/305) none). So [`pr-gate.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml) has no path filter and is the one required check. Section 6.1 lists what it runs. --- ## 5. The hooks on your machine [`.pre-commit-config.yaml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml), run by the [pre-commit framework](https://pre-commit.com/). Install both stages once per clone (since [#847](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/847) a plain `pre-commit install` does the same, through [`default_install_hook_types`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L7)): ```bash pip install pre-commit pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push pre-commit run --all-files # optional: everything, once ``` Most hooks are scoped by file pattern, so a docs-only commit skips the TypeScript ones. Hooks that need a tool you have not installed ([gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/tag/v8.29.0), [Semgrep](https://semgrep.dev/docs/), [lychee](https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee), [actionlint](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint)) print a warning and pass; the PR Gate installs gitleaks and actionlint and runs them anyway. Every suite step may fail without stopping the job; the **Compliance Report** job then compares each result with its floor in [`scripts/compliance-baseline.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/compliance-baseline.json) and fails on a regression. It gates on a recorded baseline, not on green, so a suite that does not pass yet still cannot get worse. The suites are ours and drive our APIs; they are not the Eclipse TCKs ([DSP](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dsp-tck), [DCP](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dcp-tck)) and do not prove conformance ([#338](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/338)). Current numbers and how to run them are in [Integration tests through the APIs](/docs/developer/api-integration-tests). ### 6.4 GitHub Pages: the static demo [`pages.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/pages.yml) builds the public demo at [ma3u.github.io/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2](https://ma3u.github.io/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/): it renames [`ui/src/app/api/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/ui/src/app/api) out of the way, builds with `NEXT_PUBLIC_STATIC_EXPORT=true`, adds the test reports of the last [`nightly.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml) run and publishes, on every push to `main` and when a nightly run finishes. The nightly run seeds its own Neo4j and runs Vitest, [Playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.64.1), the [WCAG](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) audit and the security checks; a failure turns it red and opens an issue ([ADR-079](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-079-e2e-runs-on-pull-requests-and-fails-visibly.md)). Without API routes every page reads [`ui/public/mock/*.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/ui/public/mock), the fixtures in the repository, so a page that GETs an `/api/...` path needs a fixture there, and [`static-mock-coverage.test.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/__tests__/unit/lib/static-mock-coverage.test.ts) fails without one. [`scripts/refresh-mocks.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/refresh-mocks.sh) refreshes them by hand from a stack you are signed in to. ### 6.5 Deploy to Azure Every push to `main` runs [`deploy-azure.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml): 1. log in to Azure with **[OIDC](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-azure)** (no stored password: a federated credential trusts this repository's `main` branch); 2. build the UI and the Neo4j proxy images, push them to the registry `acrmvhdehds`; 3. wait while a load test runs (the `LOAD_TEST_RUNNING` variable), so a merge does not redeploy under [k6](https://grafana.com/docs/k6/latest/); 4. deploy both to Container Apps in `rg-mvhd-dev` as a new revision (ACA caches [`:latest`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L75), so a restart alone would not pick up the image); 5. verify the revisions, wait for the UI, and prove sign-in works end to end; 6. if the hub is live (not stopped off hours), run [Playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.64.1), the [WCAG](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) audit and the security checks against it. **OIDC works on `main` only.** The federated credential names `refs/heads/main`, so an Azure step on a pull request, a fork or another branch cannot log in. A job that needs Azure is gated to `main`, the schedule or a dispatch on `main`; letting PRs in means adding a federated credential in Azure, not editing the workflow. Off hours (Mon to Fri 07:00 to 20:00 Europe/Berlin is on) everything is stopped ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md)), so a deploy then updates the revision without being able to test it live. --- ## 7. Releases and versions [ADR-075](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-075-a-minor-release-every-month.md) sets the rhythm: - **The hub has one version**, the `version` in [`ui/package.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/package.json). - **A minor release on the first working day of each month**, starting with [v2.1.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/releases/tag/v2.1.0) on 2026-11-04. A **patch** release in between only for a fix a partner needs before the next month; a **major** release when something a partner integrates against breaks (an API route or the graph model). - **A release is a pull request**, `chore(release): vX.Y.Z`: the version in `ui/package.json` and the root of [`ui/package-lock.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/package-lock.json), and a one-line highlight in the developer guide's release list, in all five languages. - **On merge, [`release.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml) cuts the release:** it tags `vX.Y.Z`, writes the notes from `git log` since the previous tag, and publishes a GitHub Release. A dispatch with `force_version` re-runs it. A short hand-written summary may go above the generated list afterwards, as [v2.0.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/releases/tag/v2.0.0) has. - **`main` is still what runs live.** A release marks a point a reader can cite and a changelog of at most a month, not a deployment. - **Before ADR-075** there was no cadence: eleven tags from [v1.0.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/releases/tag/v1.0.0) (2026-03-30) to [v2.0.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/releases/tag/v2.0.0) (2026-09-29), then about 350 commits without a release; [v1.4.3](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/v1.4.3) is a tag without a release. - **The Neo4j proxy and the other services are not versioned separately** ([`services/neo4j-proxy/package.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/package.json#L3) says `0.1.0`); their images are tagged by commit. ### The iPhone app: TestFlight builds Klarbefund is versioned separately, in [`clients/ios/project.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/project.yml): [`MARKETING_VERSION`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/project.yml#L19) (now `1.0`) and the build number [`CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/project.yml#L22) (now `11`). Each [TestFlight](https://developer.apple.com/testflight/) upload is its own PR, `chore(ios): build N for TestFlight, with its What to Test`, which raises the build number and writes the tester notes in English and German in [`clients/ios/appstore/texts.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/appstore/texts.py). The upload is [`clients/ios/Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh), run on the Mac; [App Store Connect](https://developer.apple.com/app-store-connect/) refuses a build number it has seen. Testers join by the public TestFlight link ([ADR-050](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-050-klarbefund-beta-by-public-testflight-link.md)). The app has no App Store release yet. --- ## 9. Contributing from outside The repository is public under the [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/LICENSE). The short version is in [`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md), which GitHub links from the issue and PR forms. 1. **Start with a Discussion or an issue** (section 3), so the change is agreed before the work. Small fixes to docs and typos can go straight to a PR. 2. **Fork, branch from `main`**, install the hooks (section 5) and set up the stack you need ([The stack and the development environment](/docs/developer/stack-and-environment)). 3. **Keep the PR to one change.** Follow the conventions in [`.claude/rules/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/.claude/rules): code style, testing and API conventions. A new API route needs [`requireAuth()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/auth-guard.ts#L22), a request in the API collection, a mock fixture and an entry in [`openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/public/openapi.yaml); the hooks tell you which is missing. 4. **Fictional organisations only.** Demo data, docs, tests and screenshots name AlphaKlinik Berlin, PharmaCo Research AG, MedReg DE, Limburg Medical Centre and Institut de Recherche Santé, never a real hospital, company, insurer or authority. Real names appear only behind the `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_TK` build flag, and real third-party screenshots are never committed. No real patient data, ever: the patients are synthetic ([Synthea](https://synthetichealth.github.io/synthea/)). 5. **No secrets.** [gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/tag/v8.29.0) runs locally and in the PR Gate; the local defaults (`neo4j` / `healthdataspace`) are for development only. 6. **Open the PR.** The PR Gate must be green; Azure steps do not run for a fork (6.5), and the maintainer runs what needs the live hub. Answer every review thread; the maintainer squash-merges. You do not need to write code to contribute. Sharper issues, ADR proposals and reviews of the user-facing docs and journeys improve every later change, because they are the specifications the AI author reads. --- ## 10. [OIDC](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect), [artifact attestations](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/using-artifact-attestations/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds), [SLSA](https://slsa.dev/), [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please), [semantic-release](https://semantic-release.gitbook.io/) | OIDC on `main`, `release.yml`; attestations and SLSA not yet (sections 6.5 and 8) | | **Measure the process** | the framework you hold the SDLC against, and how often | [NIST SSDF (SP 800-218)](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final), [OWASP SAMM](https://owaspsamm.org/), [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://scorecard.dev/) | the [quality gates](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md) and the security reports | | **Govern the AI** | which AI the product contains and which AI writes the code; the risks of each | [EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [NIST AI RMF](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework), [ISO/IEC 42001](https://www.iso.org/standard/42001), [OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications](https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/) | the natural-language query refuses to read a patient's identity unless the UI allows it ([`api-conventions.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/api-conventions.md)); the AI author is covered by the companion document | ### 12.2 Spec-driven development in practice A spec is written before the code and lives in the repository, so a person and an agent read the same text. [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) names the steps: **specify** (what and why, with acceptance criteria), **plan** (how, within the project's constraints), **tasks** (small, checkable steps), **implement**. Whatever the tool, the spec is good when: - every acceptance criterion can be checked by a test or a manual step with a link; - it names what is out of scope; - it points to the ADRs it relies on and says when a new one is needed; - the agent's standing instructions ([`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md), [`AGENTS.md`](https://agents.md/), rules files) hold what is true for every change, so the spec holds only this one. This repository does not use Spec Kit. The same steps live in the issue (what, why, acceptance criteria, open tasks), the ADR (the decision), the planning file (the plan) and `CLAUDE.md` with `.claude/rules/` (the constraints). ### 12.3 Where each conversation belongs | It is… | Put it in | It ends as | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | | a question, an idea, a comparison | a Discussion | an answer, or an issue | | a decision that is hard to reverse | an ADR, proposed in a PR | accepted, rejected or superseded | | something to do | an issue with acceptance criteria and tasks | closed by a PR, with test steps | | the change itself | a pull request linking its issue and ADRs | a squash merge on green | | what happened after the merge | the workflow run, the release, the issue | evidence anyone can open | ### 12.4 Where to start In this order, each a day's work or less: 1. A ruleset on `main`: pull request required, one required check with no path filter, no force push. 2. pre-commit with formatting, type checks and a secret scan, and the same hooks re-run in that required check. 3. Discussions on, issue templates, labels for type and priority. 4. An ADR template and a first ADR: how you decide. 5. Standing instructions for the AI author ([`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) or [`AGENTS.md`](https://agents.md/)) and the rules it must follow. 6. [CodeQL](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/introduction-to-code-scanning/about-code-scanning-with-codeql), [Dependabot](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot) or [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/), and an [SBOM](https://cyclonedx.org/). 7. A spec template for features: acceptance criteria and out-of-scope. 8. A release workflow, then provenance (attestations, [SLSA](https://slsa.dev/)) for what you ship. --- ## References - [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): commands, layout, the top gotchas. - [`.pre-commit-config.yaml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml) and [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/.github/workflows). - [`.claude/rules/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/.claude/rules): code style, testing, API conventions. - [Integration tests through the APIs](/docs/developer/api-integration-tests) · [The stack and the development environment](/docs/developer/stack-and-environment) · [Quality Gates](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md) · [Gotchas](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md) - [ADR-008, testing strategy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-008-testing-strategy.md) · [ADR-026, token-efficient planning](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-026-token-efficient-planning-structure.md) · [ADR-031, checks must assert](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-031-checks-must-assert.md) · [ADR-032, the persona-organised API collection](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-032-persona-organised-api-collection.md) - [Planning index](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/planning/index.md) · [`docs/planning-health-dataspace-v2.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/planning-health-dataspace-v2.md)

docs.markdown:
# Integration tests through the APIs

The hub is tested from the outside, the way a partner would use it, by three
suites that call its HTTP APIs: the [Bruno](https://www.usebruno.com/) collection for the hub's own routes,
and two shell suites for the dataspace protocol and the identity layer. This
page says what each one covers, how to run it, and how current it is, with the
numbers measured on 2026-11-03.

## The three suites

| Suite                 | What it calls                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Run it with                                                                            | Runs in CI                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bruno collection      | the hub's `/api/*` routes, plus the EDC services and the Neo4j proxy                                                                                                                                            | [`./scripts/run-api-tests.sh <environment>`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-api-tests.sh)           | [`bruno-smoke.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/bruno-smoke.yml) (PRs), [`compliance.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/compliance.yml) (nightly), [`demo-smoke.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/demo-smoke.yml) (live) |
| EHDS dataspace checks | the EDC control plane's Management API and [DSP 2025-1](https://eclipse-dataspace-protocol-base.github.io/DataspaceProtocol/2025-1/) endpoints                                                                  | [`./scripts/run-ehds-dataspace-checks.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-dataspace-checks.sh) | `compliance.yml`, job "DSP 2025-1 TCK"                                                                                                                                                                      |
| EHDS identity checks  | [IdentityHub](https://github.com/eclipse-edc/IdentityHub/releases/tag/v1.0.0-RC5), IssuerService and the control plane ([DCP 1.0](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/)) | [`./scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh)   | `compliance.yml`, job "DCP v1.0 Compliance"                                                                                                                                                                 |

A fourth suite, [`scripts/run-ehds-tests.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-ehds-tests.sh), checks the health domain in the
graph ([FHIR](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/), [OMOP](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html), [HealthDCAT-AP](https://data.health.europa.eu/healthdcat-ap/releases/release-8/), the access chain of [Art. 53](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_53)) through Neo4j
rather than HTTP; `compliance.yml` runs it as "EHDS Health Domain".

None of the suites is the Eclipse TCK. They are ours, they drive the APIs with
`curl` or Bruno, and the DSP and DCP ones never act as a protocol peer, so they
are liveness and shape checks on our own stack, not proofs of conformance.
Adopting the real Eclipse [DSP](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dsp-tck) and [DCP](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dcp-tck) TCKs
is phase 1 of [#338](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/338).
The [SDLC](/docs/developer/sdlc#63-protocol-compliance) has the history of why.

## The Bruno collection

[`bruno/MVHDv2/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/bruno/MVHDv2) is organised by the persona that sends a request, one folder
per role of [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng), plus the two-sided procedures of
[Chapter IV](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#cpt_IV), the role boundaries, and the protocol and platform surfaces
([ADR-032](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-032-persona-organised-api-collection.md)). A partner
uses it to rehearse against the hub.

| Folder                    | Requests | Runs against                          |
| ------------------------- | -------: | ------------------------------------- |
| 00 Public                 |        8 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 01 Patient                |       22 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 02 Data Holder            |       16 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 03 Data User              |       14 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 04 Access Body            |       13 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 05 Dataspace Operator     |       30 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 06 Trust Centre           |        3 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 07 Journey - Data permit  |       16 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 08 Journey - Data request |        5 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 09 Access control         |       39 | Local, Azure-Dev                      |
| 10 Connecting partner     |       20 | Local only (EDC is internal on Azure) |
| 11 Platform               |        6 | Local only (the proxy is internal)    |
| 12 EUDI wallet            |        3 | Local with `BRUNO_EUDI=1`             |
| 13 Static export          |       32 | Static-mock only                      |
| **Total**                 |  **227** |                                       |

So a Local run sends 192 requests, an Azure-Dev run 166 and a Static-mock run 32.

### Running it

```bash
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Static-mock   # GitHub Pages fixtures, GET only, no secret needed
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Local         # the compose stack on :3003
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Azure-Dev     # the live hub, needs NEXTAUTH_SECRET
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Local "07 Journey - Data permit"   # one folder
```

The runner forges one [NextAuth](https://next-auth.js.org/) session per persona ([`ui/scripts/forge-bruno-session.mjs`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/scripts/forge-bruno-session.mjs))
from `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, so no `.bru` file ever holds a cookie. For `Local` it
reads the secret from the UI container when the variable is unset; for
`Azure-Dev` you export it yourself and it is never printed. Reports land in
`test-results/bruno/` (override with `BRUNO_REPORT_DIR`): a summary JSON the
compliance baseline reads, and HTML, JUnit and raw JSON under `raw/`.

### The rules a request follows

From [`.claude/rules/testing.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/testing.md)
and [ADR-031](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-031-checks-must-assert.md):

- It sits in the folder of the persona that sends it; a request two personas
  send goes in a journey folder and names the acting persona.
- It asserts the status **and** at least one property of the body. A request
  whose only check is `res.status: lt 500` cannot fail and is refused.
- A request whose subject cannot exist on a stack skips loudly, with a test
  named `SKIPPED: <reason>`. It never passes silently.
- No session cookie or other credential in a `.bru` file.

Three scripts enforce this in pre-commit and the PR Gate:

| Check                                                                      | What fails it                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`scripts/check-bruno-coverage.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/check-bruno-coverage.py) | a route with no request, a request whose route is gone, a request with no assert, a credential                                             |
| [`scripts/check-bruno-strength.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/check-bruno-strength.py) | a 2xx request softer than [`docs/bruno-soft-assertion-allowlist.txt`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/bruno-soft-assertion-allowlist.txt) allows (only container types) |
| [`scripts/check-workflow-paths.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/check-workflow-paths.py) | a workflow whose `paths` filter misses a script it runs, so a fix would not re-run it                                                      |

### Are they up to date?

Measured on 2026-11-03 against `main` at [`b0586238`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/commit/b0586238):

| Question                                                                               | Answer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Does every route have a request?                                                       | **Yes.** [`check-bruno-coverage.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/check-bruno-coverage.py): 109 implemented routes, 109 requested (100 %), 0 allowlisted without a request.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Can every request fail?                                                                | **Yes.** No request lacks an assert or a test.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Are the success paths strong?                                                          | **Partly.** [`check-bruno-strength.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/check-bruno-strength.py): of 127 live 2xx requests, 49 only check a container type; all 49 are on the allowlist, which is the ratchet.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Does the static demo answer?                                                           | **Yes.** [`run-api-tests.sh Static-mock`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/run-api-tests.sh): 32 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped of 32 (99 assertions) against GitHub Pages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Does the compose stack answer? (CI, `main`)                                            | **Almost.** [`compliance.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/compliance.yml) run [41586005794](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/actions/runs/41586005794): 191 passed, 1 failed of 192. The failure is `03 Data User/13 A dataset described in German` ("the title is there in English and in German"). The floor is 179/0, so the Compliance Report job fails.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Does the live hub answer? ([`demo-smoke.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/demo-smoke.yml)) | **Not until the fix of 2026-11-03.** Run [41586005885](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/actions/runs/41586005885): 30 passed, 136 failed of 166, 163 of them 401. The secret was right; Bruno's cookie jar replaced the session header with the ingress's `acaAffinity` cookie ([gotchas](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md), 2026-11-03). With [`--disable-cookies`](https://docs.usebruno.com/bru-cli/commandOptions) the same run scored 165 of 166; the one left is `03 Data User/07 Federated cohort statistics`, a 503 from the federated query. The floor is 153/0. |
| DSP checks (CI)                                                                        | 25 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped of 33, at the floor of 25/0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| DCP checks (CI)                                                                        | 27 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped of 27, at the floor of 27/0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| EHDS domain checks (CI)                                                                | 25 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped of 30, above the floor of 18/0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

So the collection is current with the code: every route is covered and the
coverage gate keeps it so. On 2026-11-03 both results on `main` were red; both
are fixed and tracked in
[#839](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/839). The
live run scores 166 of 166 since [#853](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/853), and its floor is 166/0 since [#856](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/856).

## The compliance baseline

Every suite's result is compared with a floor in
[`scripts/compliance-baseline.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/compliance-baseline.json)
by [`scripts/check-compliance-baseline.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/check-compliance-baseline.py). The job fails when `passed` drops
below the floor or `failed` rises above it, so a suite that does not pass yet
can still guard against getting worse. Raise a floor whenever a suite
improves; lowering one needs a reason in its `note`, and `review_by` makes a
floor expire so nobody can leave it low forever.

```bash
python3 scripts/check-compliance-baseline.py --results test-results
```

## The dataspace and identity checks

Both need the full [JAD](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspace-hub/jad) stack (see [the stack and environment](/docs/developer/stack-and-environment))
with seed phases 1 to 7 done.

```bash
./scripts/run-ehds-dataspace-checks.sh   # DSP: catalogue, negotiation, transfer, policy (33 checks)
./scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh    # DCP: DIDs, keys, credentials, scopes, trust lists (27 checks)
```

They read `EDC_MANAGEMENT_URL`, `EDC_IDENTITY_URL` and `EDC_ISSUER_URL`, and
default to the compose ports. The identity checks start and stop the
[`rogue-issuer`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docker-compose.jad.yml#L808) container (compose profile `trust-check`) to show that a
credential from an issuer on no trust list is refused. On Azure the same
suites run from an [ACA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/jobs) job ([`scripts/azure/08-compliance-runner.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/08-compliance-runner.sh),
[`compliance.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/compliance.yml) dispatched with `target: azure`), where the checks that need
to look inside a container skip.

docs.summary: A glossary of the stack (EDC-V, JAD, CFM, DSP, DCP, IdentityHub, IssuerService, Vault, the proxy, the catalogue services) and how it fits together; prerequisites, the two local stacks, seed phases, ports, environment variables, the iPhone app and the day-one gotchas.
docs.markdown:
# The stack and the development environment

What each part of the hub is called, what it does and how the parts fit
together, followed by how to run them on a laptop. The decisions behind each
part are in the ADRs linked from its row; the full gotcha log is
[`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md).

## Glossary

### Protocols

| Term                                                                                          | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Decision                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **[DSP 2025-1](https://eclipse-dataspace-protocol-base.github.io/DataspaceProtocol/2025-1/)** | The Eclipse Dataspace Protocol, version 2025-1: how two connectors exchange a catalogue ([DCAT](https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dcat-3/)), negotiate a contract on an [ODRL](https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/) offer and run a transfer. The control plane speaks it under `/api/dsp/<participant>/2025-1/`.                                                    | [ADR-007](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-007-did-web-dsp-negotiation.md)                   |
| **[DCP 1.0](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/)**    | The Decentralised Claims Protocol: how a participant proves who it is. Each one has a [`did:web`](https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-web/) DID and holds [verifiable credentials](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/) (a `MembershipCredential`, EHDS role credentials); a counterparty asks for a presentation instead of trusting a central login. | [ADR-009](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-009-issuerservice-credential-fix.md)              |
| **[ODRL](https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/) 2.2**                                             | The policy language of an offer: who may use a dataset, for what purpose, under which permit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | [ADR-013](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-013-simpl-open-alignment.md)                      |
| **[HealthDCAT-AP](https://data.health.europa.eu/healthdcat-ap/releases/release-8/)**          | The catalogue vocabulary for health datasets, Release 8 since [#700](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/700).                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [ADR-063](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-063-healthdcat-ap-release-8-and-its-namespace.md) |
| **[did:web](https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-web/)**                                      | A DID resolved over HTTPS. Two forms coexist, a stable one in the graph and the UI and a resolvable one in the EDC layer; [`api-conventions.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/api-conventions.md) explains which goes where.                                                                               | [ADR-007](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-007-did-web-dsp-negotiation.md)                   |

### The connector: EDC-V

| Term                                                                                  | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Decision                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **EDC-V**                                                                             | Eclipse Dataspace Components, virtual: one multi-tenant EDC runtime in which every participant is a _participant context_ rather than its own connector. The hub runs [EDC 1.0](https://github.com/eclipse-edc/Connector/releases/tag/v1.0.0-RC5) (`1.0.0-RC5`): the control plane, IdentityHub and IssuerService are its own launchers, built from [`runtimes/edc`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/runtimes/edc). EDC 0.18 from the JAD images was retired with [#927](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/927). | [ADR-024](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-024-full-edc-provisioning-per-participant.md), [ADR-078](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-078-edc-1-on-container-apps-without-cfm.md)  |
| **Control plane**                                                                     | The EDC runtime that holds assets, policies and contract definitions, negotiates contracts over DSP and starts transfers (`controlplane` in [`docker-compose.jad.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docker-compose.jad.yml#L277)). Management API on `:11003`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [ADR-002](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-002-edc-data-plane-architecture.md), [ADR-078](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-078-edc-1-on-container-apps-without-cfm.md)            |

### How they fit together

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI["UI (Next.js)<br/>:3000"] -->|Bolt| NEO[(Neo4j)]
    UI -->|HTTP| PROXY["neo4j-proxy<br/>:9090"]
    UI -->|Management API| CP["EDC 1.0 control plane"]
    UI -->|OIDC| KC["Keycloak"]
    PROXY --> NEO
    CP -->|DSP 2025-1| CP
    CP -->|Data Plane Signaling| SIG["siglet (data plane)"]
    PROXY -->|checks the access token| SIG
    CP -->|DCP 1.0| IH["IdentityHub"]
    UI -->|provisions participants| IH
    IS["IssuerService"] -->|credentials| IH
    IH --> VAULT[("Vault")]
    SIG --> VAULT
    CRAWL["catalog crawler"] -->|DSP catalogue| CP
    CRAWL --> NATS(("NATS"))
    NATS --> ENR["catalog enricher"]
    ENR --> NEO
    CP --> PG[("PostgreSQL")]
    IH --> PG
    KC --> PG
```

A participant is created once, by the hub itself ([`ui/src/lib/edc/provision.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/edc/provision.ts), behind
`POST /api/participants`; [ADR-078](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-078-edc-1-on-container-apps-without-cfm.md#decision)): a participant context on the
control plane, the same participant with its DID and keys in the IdentityHub,
its DSP profile, a holder on the IssuerService, and a MembershipCredential
issued over DCP. A failed step undoes the ones before it; seed phase 1 runs
the same sequence. From then on the control plane negotiates on its behalf
over DSP, proving who it is over DCP; once a contract holds, siglet issues the
access token and the neo4j-proxy serves the data against it. The UI reads the
graph directly for its pages and goes through the control plane for anything
that is an exchange. With `CFM_TENANT_URL` set, CFM 0.0.7 creates them
instead ([ADR-085](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-085-cfm-stays-as-eclipse-cfm-releases.md)).

### Two ways to run it

| Stack        | Start                                                                                                                                                                                        | What you get                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Minimal**  | `docker compose up -d neo4j`, load the schema and data, `cd ui && npm install && npm run dev`                                                                                                | the graph and every page that reads it, at http://localhost:3000; no Keycloak, so sign-in needs the static persona mode |
| **Full JAD** | `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.jad.yml up -d`, then [`./scripts/bootstrap-jad.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/bootstrap-jad.sh) and [`./jad/seed-all.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-all.sh) | every service in the glossary, the UI container on http://localhost:3003, sign-in through Keycloak                      |

Loading the graph for the minimal stack (both files, [`neo4j/init-schema.cypher`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/neo4j/init-schema.cypher) and [`neo4j/insert-synthetic-schema-data.cypher`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/neo4j/insert-synthetic-schema-data.cypher), are idempotent):

```bash
cat neo4j/init-schema.cypher | docker exec -i health-dataspace-neo4j \
  cypher-shell -u neo4j -p healthdataspace
cat neo4j/insert-synthetic-schema-data.cypher | docker exec -i health-dataspace-neo4j \
  cypher-shell -u neo4j -p healthdataspace
```

`docker compose up -d` without a service name also builds the UI as the
container `health-dataspace-ui` on `:3000` and `:3003`; start only `neo4j`
when you want `npm run dev` on `:3000`.

### The seed phases, in order

[`./jad/seed-all.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-all.sh) runs seven phases, and each needs the one before it, so a
failed phase invalidates every later one. Resume with `--from N`, run one with
`--only N`.

| Phase | Script                                                                      | Does                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|     1 | [`../scripts/seed-identity-layer.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/seed-identity-layer.sh) | the five participants on EDC 1.0: control plane contexts, IdentityHub, the issuer's identity, holders, a MembershipCredential each (0.18 ran `seed-health-tenants.sh` through CFM) |
|     2 | [`seed-ehds-credentials.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-ehds-credentials.sh)            | the EHDS credential types on the IssuerService                                                                                                                                     |
|     3 | [`seed-ehds-policies.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-ehds-policies.sh)                  | ODRL policies for every participant                                                                                                                                                |
|     4 | [`seed-data-assets.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-data-assets.sh)                      | data assets and contract definitions on EDC-V                                                                                                                                      |
|     5 | [`seed-contract-negotiation.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-contract-negotiation.sh)    | siglet as each participant's data plane, then PharmaCo to AlphaKlinik negotiations, one of them refused (TERMINATED)                                                               |
|     6 | [`seed-federated-catalog.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-federated-catalog.sh)          | MedReg to Limburg Medical Centre catalogue negotiation                                                                                                                             |
|     7 | [`seed-data-transfer.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-data-transfer.sh)                  | EDR tokens from siglet and the transfers the neo4j-proxy serves                                                                                                                    |

The runbook is [JAD stack seeding](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/jad-stack-seeding.md).

| `NEO4J_PROXY_URL`                                                                                                 | the proxy, `http://localhost:9090` by default ([`ui/src/lib/proxy.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/proxy.ts#L8))                                                                                 |
