| `KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_INTERNAL_URL`, `KEYCLOAK_ISSUER`, `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID`, `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET` | sign-in; never `wellKnown` (gotcha 5 in [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L71))                                                                                                           |
| `EDC_MANAGEMENT_URL`, `EDC_IDENTITY_URL`, `EDC_ISSUER_URL`, `EDC_TENANT_URL`, `EDC_PROVISION_URL`                 | the EDC services ([`docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docker-compose.yml#L78-L82)); the last two point at CFM's managers, which only the `cfm` profile starts                                |
| `CFM_TENANT_URL`, `CFM_CLIENT_SECRET`                                                                             | set, `/onboarding` provisions through CFM and `/api/participants` shows each one's CFM state ([ADR-085](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-085-cfm-stays-as-eclipse-cfm-releases.md)); unset, the hub itself |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_STATIC_EXPORT=true`                                                                                  | the GitHub Pages build: no API routes, fixtures from [`ui/public/mock/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/ui/public/mock)                                                                                        |

### The iPhone app

[`clients/ios/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios) is a Swift package and an [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) project; it does not need
the hub to build or to run its tests.

```bash
cd clients/ios
brew install xcodegen      # once
swift test                 # the parser and provenance model
xcodegen generate && open MeinBefund.xcodeproj
```

The simulator build needs an ad-hoc signature (`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-"`) or
every Keychain call fails. A device build and a TestFlight upload need an Apple
Developer team: [`Scripts/install-device.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/install-device.sh), [`Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh).
The [Klarbefund developer guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-developer-guide) has the
rest, and [`Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh) runs the on-screen tests.

### Gotchas worth knowing on day one

The full log, dated, is [`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md). The ones that cost
the most time:

- **Vault must keep its state.** If the IdentityHub logs `Private key ... not
found`, check that [`health-dataspace-vault-unseal`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docker-compose.jad.yml#L138) reported `ready`.
- **Seed phases are strictly ordered**; resume a failed run with [`--from`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/seed-all.sh#L71).
- **The static export has no API routes.** Every page that reads `/api/...`
  needs a fixture in [`ui/public/mock/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/ui/public/mock), and a test fails without one.
- **Pre-commit rewrites files** ([Prettier](https://prettier.io/), the docs facts). Stage them again
  and commit again; check that `HEAD` moved.
- **A 200 from Keycloak discovery proves nothing**: it is cached. Prove sign-in
  with [`scripts/azure/check-keycloak-health.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/check-keycloak-health.sh).
- **Container Apps cache [`:latest`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#L75)**; a deploy pushes a new revision rather
  than restarting.

docs.title: EDC sizing under load: the contracts run after ADR-089
docs.summary: Whether the EDC control plane, IdentityHub and IssuerService still negotiate under load at the ADR-089 sizes: the k6 contracts run of 2026-11-11 with its latencies, each app's CPU and memory against its new size, the two runs before it that measured nothing and why, and the Grafana links.
docs.markdown:
# EDC sizing under load: the contracts run after ADR-089

[ADR-089](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-089-the-java-edc-apps-shrink-to-what-they-use.md) halved
the three Java EDC apps on Azure on 2026-11-11: the control plane to 0.5 vCPU
and 1 GiB, the IdentityHub and the IssuerService to 0.25 vCPU and 0.5 GiB each,
with `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=50` so the heap ceiling stayed where it was. The ADR
left one question open: whether negotiation under load fits the new sizes. This
page is the answer, measured with the k6 `contracts` scenario the same day, and
the two runs before it that measured nothing, with why.

**Result:** it fits. Run `20261111-1232-contracts-aca` held every k6
threshold with 0 failed requests, and no EDC app came near its new size.

## What the scenario does

`contracts` in [`load-tests/config.js`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/load-tests/config.js) ramps from
1 to 2 users in a minute, to 10 users over two minutes, and down to 0 in 30
seconds: 3 minutes 30 seconds. Each user is PharmaCo Research AG (data user)
running the journey of the negotiate page,
`contractJourney()` in [`load-tests/platform.js`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/load-tests/platform.js):

1. `GET /api/negotiations` reads AlphaKlinik Berlin's catalogue through the
   control plane.
2. `POST /api/negotiations` asks for a contract on the first offer, sending the
   whole offer policy and the provider's DSP address.
3. `GET /api/transfers` lists PharmaCo's transfers.

A live negotiation has no agreement yet when the POST answers (the connectors
agree afterwards and report it to the audit chain themselves), so the run
starts no transfer; that is about three requests per iteration. The run is
started inside the Container Apps environment as the job `mvhd-load-test` by
[`scripts/azure/run-load-test.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/run-load-test.sh),
which holds deploys while it runs.

## The run that counts: `20261111-1232-contracts-aca`

12:32 to 12:38 UTC, image `mvhd-k6:aee62e65`, the EDC apps at the ADR-089
sizes.

| Measure                  | Value                                |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| Users                    | 1 to 10                              |
| Iterations               | 183 (0.86 per second)                |
| Requests                 | 559 (2.6 per second)                 |
| Failed requests          | **0** (0.00 %)                       |
| Checks                   | **99.28 %** (1,110 passed, 8 failed) |
| API latency avg / median | 361 ms / 310 ms                      |
| API latency p95 / p99    | **775 ms** / 1.06 s                  |
| Slowest request          | 1.24 s                               |
| Thresholds               | all held; the job reported succeeded |

The 8 failed checks are all "api under 1000 ms": 8 of 559 answers took longer
than a second, the slowest 1.24 s. Every answer was the one expected.

The control plane wrote no line at all from 12:30 UTC to the time of
writing (Log Analytics, `ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL`, read at 14:30 UTC). It
logs warnings and errors only, so that means no `Name does not resolve`, no
retry and no refused agreement; in the run before, 12:25 to 12:30, it wrote
340 SEVERE lines for its 170 refused agreements, so the log was flowing.

Every negotiation the run created reached `FINALIZED`: 350 records created
between 12:32 and 12:38 UTC on the consumer and provider sides together, none
terminated and none still requesting (management API,
`POST /v5/participants/<ctx>/contractnegotiations/request` over all seven
participant contexts, read at 14:20 UTC).

### The EDC apps against their new sizes

Azure Monitor, `UsageNanoCores` and `WorkingSetBytes`, the highest one-minute
value of the run window (12:31 to 12:40 UTC), one replica each:

| App                  | Size (ADR-089)  | CPU peak  | Share of CPU | Memory before / peak | Share of memory |
| -------------------- | --------------- | --------- | ------------ | -------------------- | --------------- |
| `mvhd-controlplane`  | 0.5 vCPU, 1 GiB | 0.33 vCPU | 66 %         | 364 / 368 MiB        | 36 %            |
| `mvhd-identityhub`   | 0.25, 0.5 GiB   | 0.09 vCPU | 36 %         | 224 / 231 MiB        | 45 %            |
| `mvhd-issuerservice` | 0.25, 0.5 GiB   | 0.00 vCPU | 0 %          | 178 / 178 MiB        | 35 %            |
| `mvhd-siglet` (Rust) | 0.25, 0.5 GiB   | 0.00 vCPU | 0 %          | 89 / 89 MiB          | 17 %            |

The load reached the connectors from 12:35 to 12:38 UTC. The control plane's
CPU rose minute by minute (0.06, 0.16, 0.28, 0.33 vCPU) with 10 users, so it is
the app with the least headroom: two thirds of its half core at the peak. Its
memory hardly moved, 4 MiB over the run. The IssuerService did nothing, as
expected: a negotiation presents credentials the IdentityHub already holds and
issues none. Each app kept its one replica, created hours before the run,
with 0 restarts.

The rest of the stack in the same window, for scale: the UI peaked at 0.28
vCPU of 0.5, Neo4j at 0.21 vCPU of 2, the proxy at 0.07 of 0.25, Keycloak at
0.07 of 1.

The JVM heap ceiling is half the container (`EDC_JVM_HEAP_OPTS`): 512 MiB for
the control plane and 256 MiB for the other two, the same as before the change.

## The two runs that measured nothing

Both ran against the same sizes and both are invalid. They are kept here
because each found a bug in the load test, not in the hub.

| Run                           | k6 said                                                                | What really happened                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Fixed by                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `20261111-0807-contracts-aca` | 406 requests, 0 failed, checks 83.49 %, p95 2.7 s; thresholds crossed  | The scenario sent `http://controlplane:8082/api/dsp`, the compose name, as the provider's address. On Azure the app is `mvhd-controlplane`, so all 132 negotiations failed with `Name does not resolve` and kept retrying through the NATS consumer, and real negotiations queued behind them. | [#1076](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/1076): the runners pass `DSP_ADDRESS` from the stack they run against; the stuck negotiations were terminated through the management API |
| `20261111-1223-contracts-aca` | 520 requests, 0 failed, checks 95.86 %, p95 1.16 s; thresholds crossed | The address was right, but the scenario sent only the offer's id, not its policy. The consumer compares the agreement with the policy it asked for, so all 170 negotiations ended in `TERMINATED` with "Policy in the contract agreement is not equal to the one in the contract offer".       | this branch: `firstOffer()` keeps the whole offer and the POST sends `policy`, as the negotiate page does                                                                                                    |

The first one also means no `contracts` run on Azure had negotiated for real
since the scenario came in (#579, 2026-10-06): the October numbers in the
[load test index](/docs/operations/load-tests) measured requests to a name that does
not resolve. The full account is the 2026-11-11 entry in
[`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md).

The latencies of the three runs are not comparable: in the first the control
plane was busy retrying, in the second every negotiation ended early.

## Transfers under load: the evening runs

The scenario now waits for each agreement and transfers on it (see
[What follows](#what-follows)). Two `contracts` runs measured that on Azure
the same evening, at the ADR-089 sizes. The stack had been stopped at 18:13
UTC (ADR-053); it was started at 18:36, up at 18:46, held with
`live-demo-hold-until` and stopped again at 19:08.

| Measure                     | `20261111-1847-contracts-aca` (cold) | `20261111-1856-contracts-aca` (warm) |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| Started after the stack     | 3 minutes                            | 11 minutes                           |
| Iterations / requests       | 54 / 429                             | 61 / 465                             |
| Failed requests             | **0**                                | **0**                                |
| Negotiations agreed         | 54 of 54                             | 61 of 61                             |
| Time to agreement p50 / p95 | 6.7 s / 14.8 s                       | 6.2 s / 19.6 s                       |
| Transfers started (`201`)   | 54, all `STARTED` in the connector   | 61, all `STARTED` in the connector   |
| Refused transfers (`403`)   | 17                                   | 20                                   |
| Polls (`kind:poll`), share  | 186, 43 %                            | 191, 41 %                            |
| API p95 (`kind:api`)        | **1.37 s**, over the 1 s SLO         | **1.58 s**, over the 1 s SLO         |
| Control plane CPU peak      | 0.31 vCPU of 0.5                     | 0.36 vCPU of 0.5                     |
| IdentityHub CPU peak        | 0.20 vCPU of 0.25                    | 0.12 vCPU of 0.25                    |
| Control plane errors        | none                                 | none                                 |
| k6 result                   | failed: `checks`, API p95            | failed: `checks`, API p95            |

Every answer was the one expected, and every negotiation and transfer
reached the connectors (the hub's `GET /api/negotiations` and
`GET /api/transfers` for PharmaCo, filtered to each run's minutes) and the
audit trail. The **EDC contracts and transfers** dashboard, which reads the
DSP chain, counts for the two runs' windows 54 and 61 negotiations agreed and
finalized, 54 and 61 transfers started, 17 and 20 refused for want of a
data permit, and none terminated or failed. None is completed either: an
`HttpData-PULL` transfer stays `STARTED` while its data address is valid, and
the scenario does not fetch the data.

Both runs fail on latency only, and the second, warm one is no faster, so it
is not a cold start. Latency per endpoint (Prometheus through Grafana,
`k6_http_req_duration_seconds` by `name` over each run's six minutes; the
counts are Prometheus's estimate, a few above k6's own) shows where:

| Endpoint                            | Requests, cold / warm | p50, cold / warm | p95, cold / warm |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- |
| `GET /api/transfers`                | 55 / 63               | 582 / 805 ms     | 1.26 s / 2.18 s  |
| `GET /api/negotiations` (catalogue) | 55 / 62               | 904 / 522 ms     | 1.64 s / 1.50 s  |
| `POST /api/transfers`               | 55 / 62               | 288 / 267 ms     | 562 / 771 ms     |
| `POST /api/negotiations`            | 55 / 62               | 275 / 257 ms     | 618 / 707 ms     |
| `POST /api/transfers` (no permit)   | 18 / 21               | 78 / 62 ms       | 302 / 163 ms     |
| `GET /api/participants`             | 10 / 10               | 35 / 33 ms       | 185 / 143 ms     |
| poll, outside the threshold         | 189 / 194             | 50 / 37 ms       | 401 / 403 ms     |

- **The transfer itself is not the slow step.** Its POST stays under the SLO.
- **`GET /api/transfers` grows with what the runs leave behind.** The route
  asks the control plane for the newest 200 transfer processes
  (`newestFirstQuery()`). PharmaCo had a handful before these runs; after
  the first it had about 140 and during the second the 200 rows were full,
  each a JSON-LD transfer process. The transfer page reads the same list.
- **The catalogue request was already the slowest call** in the 12:32 run,
  and it is slower while the control plane also runs transfers.
- **The control plane still has headroom:** 72 % of its half core at the
  peak, against 66 % at 12:32. The IdentityHub's 80 % was in the cold run
  only.

The ADR-089 sizes are not what the threshold measures here. What it shows is
two read paths, the transfer list and the catalogue, that need a page size or
a cache before the `contracts` scenario can pass with transfers in it.

## Grafana

The dashboards need a sign-in on <https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red>: the
operator account `admin`, whose password is the Key Vault secret
`grafana-admin-password` in `kv-mvhd-b53a0449` (see
[Dashboards](/docs/operations/dashboards)). They show data only while the
stack is up ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md)), and
keep it: the evening runs were read the next morning. Times are UTC.

The same account answers Grafana's HTTP API, which is how the per-endpoint
numbers above were read, without a browser and without
`az containerapp exec` into `mvhd-observability` (which drops quotes from the
query and is rate-limited after a few calls). With the password in
`GF_PW`:

```bash
curl -s -u "admin:$GF_PW" -G \
  https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/api/datasources/proxy/uid/prometheus/api/v1/query \
  --data-urlencode 'time=2026-11-11T19:01:35Z' \
  --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (name) (increase(k6_http_req_duration_seconds{testid="20261111-1856-contracts-aca"}[6m])))'
```

The DSP chain behind the EDC dashboard answers on
`/api/datasources/proxy/uid/mvhd-audit/audit/chains/dsp/stats?from=<ms>&to=<ms>`.

| Run                                     | Load and stress test                                                                                                                                             | EDC contracts and transfers                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `20261111-1232-contracts-aca` (valid)   | [12:31 to 12:40](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1232-contracts-aca&from=1794400260000&to=1794400800000) | [12:31 to 12:40](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-edc-dsp/edc-contracts-and-transfers?from=1794400260000&to=1794400800000) |
| `20261111-1223-contracts-aca` (invalid) | [12:21 to 12:31](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1223-contracts-aca&from=1794399660000&to=1794400260000) | [12:21 to 12:31](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-edc-dsp/edc-contracts-and-transfers?from=1794399660000&to=1794400260000) |
| `20261111-0807-contracts-aca` (invalid) | [08:05 to 08:15](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-0807-contracts-aca&from=1794384300000&to=1794384900000) | [08:05 to 08:15](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-edc-dsp/edc-contracts-and-transfers?from=1794384300000&to=1794384900000) |
| `20261111-1847-contracts-aca` (cold)    | [18:46 to 18:55](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1847-contracts-aca&from=1794422760000&to=1794423300000) | [18:46 to 18:55](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-edc-dsp/edc-contracts-and-transfers?from=1794422760000&to=1794423300000) |
| `20261111-1856-contracts-aca` (warm)    | [18:55 to 19:04](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-load-test/load-and-stress-test?var-testid=20261111-1856-contracts-aca&from=1794423300000&to=1794423840000) | [18:55 to 19:04](https://grafana.ehds.mabu.red/d/mvhd-edc-dsp/edc-contracts-and-transfers?from=1794423300000&to=1794423840000) |

On **Load and stress test**, the "Load (k6)" row shows the users, requests and
p95, and the "Containers" row the CPU and memory of the connectors. On **EDC
contracts and transfers**, the valid run's negotiations count as requested and
then finalized. In the first invalid run they stay requested until they were
terminated by hand after 12:00; in the second they end terminated within the
run. In the evening runs the "Data transfers" row fills too: started, and
refused for the dataset no permit covers.

## What follows

- The ADR-089 sizes stay. The control plane has the least headroom in CPU, so
  it is the one to watch when the `load` scenario runs with the EDC pages doing
  real work (step 4 of the runs still to do in the
  [load test index](/docs/operations/load-tests#the-runs-still-to-do)).
- Transfers are measured now. The run above started none: the scenario
  transferred only when the POST answered with an agreement, and a live
  negotiation agrees later. Since then `contractJourney()` waits for the
  agreement as the negotiate page does, asking
  `GET /api/negotiations/<id>` after 1, 2, 3, 5 and then every 8 seconds, up
  to `AGREEMENT_TIMEOUT_S` (60 s). On `FINALIZED` it runs
  `POST /api/transfers` on the agreement, to the provider endpoint the
  negotiation recorded, and one time in four the refused transfer for a
  dataset no permit covers. A negotiation that ends `TERMINATED` or is still
  open at the timeout is a failed check (`negotiation agrees within 60 s`)
  and counts in `negotiations_unagreed`; `negotiation_agreed` is the time to
  the poll that saw the agreement. The polls are tagged `kind:poll`, so the
  API p95 and its threshold are the person's calls only.
- On the compose stack (`20261111-1846-contracts-local`, the same 1 to 10
  users) that gave 110 iterations and 623 requests, 0 failed, every check
  passed: 110 negotiations agreed (p50 1.0 s, p95 3.0 s, at the polls'
  resolution), 110 transfers started in the control plane (`201`, p95
  115 ms), 33 refused (`403`). The 140 polls were 22.5 % of the requests;
  the 483 other requests had a p95 of 107 ms. On Azure, where an agreement
  takes about 6 seconds, the polls are about 42 % of the requests; the
  results are in [Transfers under load](#transfers-under-load-the-evening-runs).
- The `contracts` scenario fails its API threshold on Azure since it
  transfers, on `GET /api/transfers` and the catalogue request, not on the
  transfer. Each run adds about 60 transfer processes to PharmaCo's list,
  so later runs read a full 200 rows. Since #1088 both reads do less:

  - **The lists are paged.** `GET /api/transfers` and `GET /api/negotiations`
    take `limit` and `offset` (`ui/src/lib/list-page.ts`): 50 rows unless
    asked, at most 200, a `400` with `{ error }` for anything that is not a
    whole number. The demo and mock rows come on the first page only. The
    transfer page, the negotiate page and the k6 step ask for one page of 50. What a list costs is the control plane compacting each row as
    JSON-LD, so it grows with the rows: on the compose stack, asked
    directly, 200 negotiations were 545 kB and 430 to 570 ms, 50 were
    140 kB and 83 to 108 ms; 200 transfers 160 to 300 ms, 50 about 40 ms.
  - **The catalogue request no longer lists every context first.** The
    participant contexts are kept for a minute
    (`ui/src/lib/edc/context-lookup.ts`), for the catalogue's DID lookup and
    for the transfer POST's lookup of the consumer's DID, which also listed
    them on every live transfer. A DID the kept list does not name is
    looked up again at once, and a catalogue request that fails on a kept
    context id reads the list afresh and tries once more. Requests for the
    same catalogue at the same moment share one DSP request
    (`shareInFlight()` in `ui/src/lib/server-cache.ts`); nothing is kept
    after it answers, so a new offer shows on the next request.
  - **Where the catalogue time goes is not settled.** On the compose stack
    the DSP catalogue request itself takes 25 to 54 ms warm and the context
    list about 20 ms, so neither explains 1.5 s on Azure. There the request
    runs the DCP exchange between the apps (a token from the IdentityHub,
    its presentation, the DID documents) through the Container Apps
    ingress, on a control plane that is also compacting the 200-row lists.
    The next Azure run tells whether the smaller lists free enough of it;
    if the catalogue is still over the SLO, the calls the control plane
    makes to the IdentityHub during one request are the place to look next.

  Measured on the compose stack on 2026-11-12, the branch's UI and the one
  before it side by side on the same stack, against PharmaCo's 200+
  transfers and negotiations. Twenty requests after each other per route:

  | Route, p50 / p90                   | Before #1088   | #1088        |
  | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------ |
  | `GET /api/transfers` (one page)    | 256 / 642 ms   | 59 / 113 ms  |
  | `GET /api/negotiations` (one page) | 542 / 1,173 ms | 147 / 266 ms |
  | `GET /api/negotiations` catalogue  | 74 / 128 ms    | 62 / 96 ms   |

  The `contracts` scenario, back to back (`K6_JSON=1`, then
  `load-tests/p95-by-name.py`):

  | p95                                 | `20261112-base-contracts-local` | `20261112-branch-contracts-local` |
  | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
  | `GET /api/transfers`                | 553 ms (p50 307 ms)             | **302 ms** (p50 111 ms)           |
  | `GET /api/negotiations` (catalogue) | 199 ms                          | 321 ms                            |
  | `POST /api/negotiations`            | 210 ms                          | 540 ms                            |
  | `POST /api/transfers`               | 222 ms                          | 306 ms                            |
  | All `kind:api`                      | 433 ms                          | **364 ms**                        |
  | Answers over 1 s                    | 1 of 470                        | 10 of 435                         |
  | Failed requests                     | 0                               | 0                                 |

  The compose stack shares the laptop with other containers whose load
  comes in bursts, and the runs show it: 9 of the branch run's 10 slow
  answers came within two seconds (09:16:34 to 09:16:36 UTC+1) on every
  route at once, the catalogue and the negotiation POST included, which is
  the host and not a route. A third run (`20261112-branch2-contracts-local`)
  at a load average of 25 was slow on every route, the refused transfer
  that hardly reaches the connector included (p95 813 ms), and is not
  counted. The transfer list is the measure that holds across the runs.

- **On Azure #1088 is not enough.** Run `20261112-1012-contracts-aca`,
  10:12 to 10:18 UTC, the UI at `ccd9ef8f` (#1088 deployed, the Azure E2E
  tests green before it): 51 iterations, 424 requests, 1 failed (0.23 %),
  checks 95.32 %, **API p95 1.50 s**; k6 failed on `checks` and
  `http_req_duration{kind:api}`. Agreements took longer than the evening
  before (p50 11.4 s, p95 19.8 s, against 6.2 to 6.7 s and 14.8 to 19.6 s).
  Per endpoint (Prometheus through Grafana, by `name`, over the run):

  | Endpoint                            | p50    | p95    | Evening p95, 200 rows |
  | ----------------------------------- | ------ | ------ | --------------------- |
  | `GET /api/transfers` (one page)     | 553 ms | 1.44 s | 1.26 s / 2.18 s       |
  | `GET /api/negotiations` (catalogue) | 758 ms | 1.76 s | 1.64 s / 1.50 s       |
  | `POST /api/transfers`               | 351 ms | 825 ms | 562 / 771 ms          |
  | `POST /api/negotiations`            | 327 ms | 738 ms | 618 / 707 ms          |
  | `POST /api/transfers` (no permit)   | 86 ms  | 214 ms | 302 / 163 ms          |
  | poll, outside the threshold         | 64 ms  | 395 ms | 401 / 403 ms          |

  No app was short of CPU: the highest one-minute value was 0.27 vCPU of
  0.5 for the control plane, 0.16 of 0.25 for the IdentityHub and 0.09 of
  0.5 for the UI. Asked one request at a time from a laptop after the run,
  with the hub idle (each answer includes about 118 ms of round trip, what
  `/api/health` takes):

  | Request                        | Five answers                   |
  | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
  | `GET /api/transfers?limit=1`   | 0.24, 0.42, 0.33, 0.26, 0.80 s |
  | `GET /api/transfers?limit=50`  | 0.61, 0.48, 0.55, 0.44, 0.47 s |
  | `GET /api/transfers?limit=200` | 1.26, 2.02, 1.28, 1.24, 1.12 s |
  | Catalogue                      | 0.76, 0.57, 0.65, 0.59, 1.08 s |

  So the page makes the list about three times cheaper on Azure too, but
  one row still takes a few hundred milliseconds, and the catalogue request
  takes half a second to a second with nothing else running. Neither is
  CPU on the apps; both are time spent waiting on the Azure side, in the
  control plane's store or in the calls between the apps. Measuring that
  inside the environment (the control plane's request times against its
  database, and the DCP calls of one catalogue request) comes before any
  further change to the UI.

- After any `contracts` run against Azure, check the control plane's log for
  `Name does not resolve` and the negotiation states before calling it done.

## Reproduce

```bash
scripts/azure/run-load-test.sh contracts      # inside Azure, as a Container Apps job
load-tests/run.sh contracts local             # against the compose stack
```

The run's raw summary is in the job's log (`az containerapp job logs show -n
mvhd-load-test -g rg-mvhd-dev --container k6`) while the execution is kept.

docs.title: The secure processing environment and its confidential containers
docs.summary: How the hub builds the secure processing environment of Art. 73 from confidential containers: the two SPE workspaces on ACI with AMD SEV-SNP, the Trustee the access body runs, how a workspace earns its key, what a federated query goes through, how to run it on a laptop and what is not done yet.
docs.markdown:
# The secure processing environment and its confidential containers

A data user never receives the patients' rows. They ask a question, the
question runs inside a **secure processing environment** (SPE) next to the
data, and only aggregates that pass the output checks come back (Regulation
(EU) 2025/327, [Art. 73](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_73)). This page explains how the hub builds that
environment from confidential containers, so that the claim "the operator
cannot read the data either" rests on hardware rather than on trust. It
covers what runs where, how a workspace gets its key, what a query goes
through, how to run it on a laptop and what is not done yet.

The decisions are [ADR-037](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-037-secure-processing-environment-confidential-computing.md)
(the pattern), [ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md)
(the design), [ADR-069](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-069-two-spe-workspaces-as-aci-confidential-containers.md)
(the Azure deployment) and [ADR-072](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-072-spe-workspaces-start-on-demand.md)
(start on demand). The operator's step-by-step is the runbook
[SPE attestation on Azure](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/spe-attestation-azure.md).

## 1. The idea in one paragraph

Each of the two data holders has a **workspace**: SPE-1 for AlphaKlinik
Berlin, SPE-2 for Limburg Medical Centre. A workspace is a confidential
container group: its memory is encrypted by the CPU ([AMD SEV-SNP](https://docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/amd-memory-encryption.html#secure-nested-paging-snp)), and the
CPU signs a report of exactly what was started in it. The workspace's data
arrives sealed, and the key is held by a **Trustee** that the health data
access body (MedReg DE) runs. Trustee releases the key only when the signed
report proves that the workspace runs the code the data permit was issued
for. **No key, no data**: a changed image, command or environment variable
gives a different policy hash, and the key stays where it is.

## 2. The framework: CNCF Confidential Containers (CoCo)

The SPE is built on [Confidential Containers](https://confidentialcontainers.org/) (CoCo), a
[CNCF incubating project](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/07/22/confidential-containers-becomes-a-cncf-incubating-project/) since July 2026 that runs containers inside
hardware TEEs and releases secrets only to workloads that prove what they
are ([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md), decision 1). CoCo has three parts; the hub uses two
of them today:

| CoCo part                                                                           | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Used here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **[Trustee](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee)**                   | The key broker service ([KBS](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/tree/v0.22.0/kbs)), the attestation service ([AS](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/tree/v0.22.0/attestation-service)) and the reference value provider service ([RVPS](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/tree/v0.22.0/rvps)): it verifies a TEE's evidence and releases secrets against a policy. | Yes, [v0.22.0](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/releases/tag/v0.22.0), run by the access body: ACA app `mvhd-trustee` on Azure, service `trustee` in [`docker-compose.trustee.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docker-compose.trustee.yml#L61) locally.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **[Guest components](https://github.com/confidential-containers/guest-components)** | What runs inside the TEE to collect the evidence and talk to Trustee: the [attesters](https://github.com/confidential-containers/guest-components/tree/v0.22.0/attestation-agent/attester) and [`kbs-client`](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/tree/v0.22.0/tools/kbs-client).                                                                                                                      | Yes: the init container `spe-unlock` uses `kbs-client` with the SEV-SNP attester, patched to ask ACI for the plain report ([`kbs-client.aci.Dockerfile`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/spe-loader/kbs-client.aci.Dockerfile)).                                                                                                                                                   |
| **[Kata Containers](https://katacontainers.io/) runtime**                           | Starts each pod in its own confidential micro-VM, through a Kubernetes [`RuntimeClass`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/runtime-class/) or as [peer pods](https://github.com/confidential-containers/cloud-api-adaptor) on a cloud.                                                                                                                                                                    | Not on Azure: the tenant policy refused AKS, and the peer pods' Azure tests are switched off. ACI's confidential container groups provide the SEV-SNP utility VM instead ([ADR-069](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-069-two-spe-workspaces-as-aci-confidential-containers.md)). On a Mac it is an optional local runtime check ([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md#decision), M2). |

So on Azure the isolation comes from ACI, and the trust decision (which
workload gets a key) from CoCo's Trustee. Moving to Kata on Kubernetes later
changes the runtime and the policy generator ([`genpolicy`](https://github.com/kata-containers/kata-containers/tree/main/src/tools/genpolicy) instead of
[`az confcom`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/confcom)), not Trustee, the permit or its policy hash.

## 3. Terms

| Term                                                                                                                                                               | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Confidential computing**                                                                                                                                         | Running code in a trusted execution environment (TEE) whose memory the host, the hypervisor and the cloud operator cannot read.                                                                                                                                                         |
| **[AMD SEV-SNP](https://docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/amd-memory-encryption.html#secure-nested-paging-snp)**                                                            | The TEE the workspaces use (EPYC 9V74, Genoa). It encrypts the VM's memory and produces an attestation report signed by a key that chains back to AMD. Intel TDX is not used.                                                                                                           |
| **Confidential container**                                                                                                                                         | A container group that runs inside its own SEV-SNP utility VM. On Azure: an [Azure Container Instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-confidential-overview) (ACI) group with `sku: Confidential`.                                    |
| **[ccePolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-confidential-overview#confidential-computing-enforcement-policies)** | The confidential computing enforcement policy of an ACI group: the images by digest, the commands, the environment and the mounts that may run. Generated with [`az confcom acipolicygen`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/confcom#az-confcom-acipolicygen).                |
| **HOST_DATA**                                                                                                                                                      | A field of the SEV-SNP report set at launch. ACI puts the [SHA-256](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) of the ccePolicy there, so the hardware vouches for which policy the group started with.                                                                          |
| **Policy hash**                                                                                                                                                    | That SHA-256, recorded on the permit (`HDABApproval.policyHash`) and in Trustee's resource policy. It binds a permit to one exact workload.                                                                                                                                             |
| **Trustee**                                                                                                                                                        | The [CNCF Confidential Containers](https://confidentialcontainers.org/) key broker: KBS (key broker service), AS (attestation service) and RVPS (reference values). Version [v0.22.0](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/releases/tag/v0.22.0), run by the access body. |
| **Reference values**                                                                                                                                               | What Trustee compares the report against: the launch measurement of Microsoft's utility VM and the minimum TCB (firmware and microcode versions).                                                                                                                                       |
| **Sealed extract**                                                                                                                                                 | A workspace's half of the synthetic patients, format `mvhd-spe-extract/1`: JSON lines, gzipped, encrypted with [AES-256-GCM](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication800-38d.pdf) under a new key per permit.                                                 |

## 4. Where it runs, and what each place proves

The design is the same everywhere; what differs is whether real hardware
signs the evidence. The UI says which, with one of three labels
([`ui/src/lib/spe.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/spe.ts)),
and never claims more than the evidence shows ([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md#decision) decision 5).

| Where                        | What is real                                                                                                                                                                                         | Label                             |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| **Laptop, CI, static demo**  | Trustee, the permit's hash in its policy, key release, the sealed extract, Neo4j loading it, the audit trail. Evidence comes from Trustee's sample attester, because a laptop has no TEE.            | "Simulated attestation"           |
| **Azure, node level (A1)**   | SEV-SNP hardware with a measured boot, but not which container ran. Not deployed.                                                                                                                    | "Attested: SEV-SNP node"          |
| **Azure, per workload (A2)** | ACI confidential containers in westeurope: the per-workload policy is checked by hardware. Ran end to end on 2026-11-02 ([#774](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/774)). | "Attested: confidential workload" |

The seeded `SPESession` nodes in the Trust Center graph
([`neo4j/seed-trust-center.cypher`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/neo4j/seed-trust-center.cypher))
carry `simulated: true`; they illustrate the model and are not evidence.

## 5. The parts on Azure

| Part                      | Azure resource                                                  | What it does                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SPE-1, AlphaKlinik Berlin | ACI group `mvhd-spe-1`, `sku: Confidential`, westeurope         | init container `spe-unlock` attests and gets the key; `neo4j` holds the data; sidecar `spe-ingest` loads it                        |
| SPE-2, Limburg MC         | ACI group `mvhd-spe-2`, same shape                              | the same, with the other half of the synthetic patients                                                                            |
| Trustee (MedReg DE)       | ACA app `mvhd-trustee`, job `mvhd-trustee-admin`                | verifies the SEV-SNP evidence against AMD's chain, the reference values and HOST_DATA, then releases `default/spe-<n>/extract-key` |
| Trustee's state           | file shares `trustee-keys`, `trustee-data`                      | admin key, token key, policies, reference values, extract keys. Never the hub's Key Vault                                          |
| Sealed extracts           | share `spe-extracts`, baked into image `mvhd-spe-loader-spe<n>` | ciphertext only; the extract's digest is part of the policy hash                                                                   |
| Federation and audit      | ACA app `mvhd-neo4j-proxy`                                      | sends the federated questions to the workspaces, applies the output checks, appends their `spe.*` events to the audit chain        |

The group template is
[`scripts/azure/aci/spe-workspace.template.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/aci/spe-workspace.template.json).
Everything else in the hub stays on Azure Container Apps (ACA), which has no
confidential workload profile in an EU region yet. [Azure Attestation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/attestation/overview) and [Key
Vault secure key release](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/concept-skr-attestation) were considered and are deliberately **not** in the
key path: the access body, not the cloud operator, decides who gets a key
([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md#decision) decision 1, [ADR-069](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-069-two-spe-workspaces-as-aci-confidential-containers.md#alternatives-considered) "Alternatives considered").

## 6. The chain of trust

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant HDAB as Access body (MedReg DE)
    participant T as Trustee
    participant W as Workspace (ACI, SEV-SNP)
    participant CPU as AMD SEV-SNP
    HDAB->>T: permit's policy hash, reference values, extract key
    W->>CPU: launch with ccePolicy
    CPU-->>W: report signed by AMD, HOST_DATA = SHA-256(ccePolicy)
    W->>T: spe-unlock sends the report
    T->>T: AMD signature (VCEK), launch measurement, TCB minimum, HOST_DATA = policy hash
    alt every check holds
        T-->>W: extract key
        W->>W: decrypt into memory, load Neo4j, delete plaintext
    else any check fails
        T-->>W: refused (exit code 3)
        W->>W: Neo4j starts empty, the refusal is recorded
    end
```

1. **The permit fixes the workload.** [`21-aci-confidential-spe.sh --policy`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/21-aci-confidential-spe.sh)
   generates the ccePolicy from the template. Its SHA-256 is written to the
   permit (`HDABApproval`) and into Trustee's resource policy
   ([`trustee/policies/resource-azure.rego.tmpl`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/trustee/policies/resource-azure.rego.tmpl)).
2. **The hardware vouches for it.** ACI launches the group in a SEV-SNP
   utility VM and puts the policy's hash into HOST_DATA of the signed report.
3. **Trustee checks four things:** the signature back to AMD ([VCEK](https://kdsintf.amd.com/) from
   AMD's key distribution service), the utility VM's launch measurement
   against a pinned reference value, the TCB against a minimum per component
   ([ADR-073](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-073-the-spe-tcb-is-a-minimum-not-a-list.md),
   [`attestation-ear-cpu.rego`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/trustee/policies/attestation-ear-cpu.rego)),
   and HOST_DATA against the permit's hash.
4. **Only then does the key leave Trustee.** With no reference value pinned,
   the policy refuses: there is no "unlock on first use".

Secrets do not travel in the policy. They reach the group through its secret
volume, so rotating one does not change the hash.

## 7. Inside a workspace

Each group has three containers, built from
[`services/spe-loader`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/spe-loader):

- **`spe-unlock`** (init container): attests with `kbs-client` built with the
  `snp-attester` feature, gets the key, decrypts the extract into the
  `emptyDir` volume `work`.
- **`neo4j`**: [Neo4j 5.26](https://neo4j.com/release-notes/database/neo4j-5/) Community, [1.5 vCPU](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/aci/spe-workspace.template.json#L126) and 4 GiB, store in the
  `emptyDir` volume `neo4j-data`, Bolt with TLS required, HTTP off. Neo4j is
  **a workspace per permit, not a long-lived store** ([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md#decision) decision 3): it
  holds the data only in memory and on ephemeral storage inside the TEE.
- **`spe-ingest`** (sidecar): loads the extract, applies
  [`neo4j/init-schema.cypher`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/neo4j/init-schema.cypher) and the SPE's HealthDCAT-AP registration,
  deletes the plaintext, records the attestation, and stays up.

**The data.** Each workspace gets half of the hub's synthetic patients: the
FHIR records ([Patient](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/patient.html), [Condition](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/condition.html), [Observation](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/observation.html) and the rest), the matching
[OMOP CDM](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html#person) person with its records, and the concepts they are coded by. Sandbox
patients and the Klarbefund app's patients are left out. A patient's
`OptedOut` label travels with the data ([Art. 71](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_71)).

**Stopping is deleting.** The stores live in memory, so stopping or deleting
a group loses every row. Each start attests again and loads again. One trap:
[`az container restart`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/container#az-container-restart) does not re-run the init container, so a restarted
group never asks Trustee again; stop and start it instead
([`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/gotchas.md), 2026-11-01).

**The loader's commands** (`spe-loader <command>`): `policy-hash`,
`trustee-configure`, `record-permit`, `export`, `encrypt`, `extract`,
`unlock`, `ingest` and `load`. Exit code 3 means the key was refused; 2 means
a database or Trustee did not answer.

## 8. What a federated query goes through

1. A data user asks on `/query` or through natural language. The UI calls
   [`/api/federated`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/app/api/federated/route.ts)
   (or [`/api/nlq`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/app/api/nlq/route.ts) with `federated: true`).
2. **Cold start** ([ADR-072](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-072-spe-workspaces-start-on-demand.md)).
   The workspaces are stopped by default to save cost. A federated query by
   `EDC_ADMIN`, `HDAB_AUTHORITY` or `DATA_USER` starts them; until they are up
   the answer is **503** with `state` `starting` or `stopped`,
   `etaSeconds` (240 from stopped) and a [`Retry-After`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-10.2.3) header. Measured: the
   key arrives after about a minute, the data is loaded after about three,
   SPE-2 answers after about four. The job `mvhd-spe-idle-stop` runs every
   15 minutes and stops a workspace idle for 30.
3. **The proxy fans out.** [`services/neo4j-proxy`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/neo4j-proxy) sends the question to both
   workspaces over Bolt with TLS (`POST /federated/query`,
   `GET /federated/stats`).
4. **Output checks before anything leaves.** Groups smaller than k are
   dropped and cells below k become `<k`, with k = 5 ([`MIN_COHORT_SIZE`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/config.ts#L94),
   [`k-anonymity.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/k-anonymity.ts));
   opted-out patients are excluded
   ([`opt-out.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/opt-out.ts)).
5. **Only aggregates return** to the UI, through the proxy.

**The audit trail.** The proxy reads each workspace's events every minute and
appends them to the hub's audit chain `spe` ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)): `spe.attestation`,
`key_release`, `key_refused`, `workspace_loaded`, `workspace_destroyed` and
`optout_synced`.

**Where to see it in the UI**, signed in as `edcadmin`:

- `/admin/attestation`: the attestation of each workspace and its label.
- `/admin/components`: the SPE topology, with a power button per workspace.
- `/admin/audit`: the `spe` chain.
- `/admin/policies`: which permit is bound to which policy hash.
- `/query`: the cold-start notice while the workspaces start.

## 9. Running it on a laptop

Without the overlay below, SPE-1 is simply the hub graph and SPE-2 a second
Neo4j: federation works, but nothing is sealed or attested. To get the real
flow with simulated evidence, start the Trustee overlay on top of the JAD
stack ([`docker-compose.trustee.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docker-compose.trustee.yml)):

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.jad.yml \
  -f docker-compose.trustee.yml --profile federated up -d --build
```

It adds Trustee on <http://localhost:8099>, sets its local policy and
reference values, seals both extracts and records their policy hashes on the
hub, moves both workspaces' stores to `tmpfs`, and runs `spe-loader-spe1` and
`spe-loader-spe2` to attest, unlock and load. Check the result with the
proxy's `GET http://localhost:9090/spe/status` or on `/admin/attestation`.

The tests that guard it, in CI and locally: [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) in [`services/spe-loader`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/spe-loader), and [`opa test`](https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-testing) over [`trustee/policies/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/trustee/policies) through [`scripts/test-trustee-policies.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/test-trustee-policies.sh):

```bash
cd services/spe-loader && npm test        # Vitest: extract, seal, unlock, ingest
./scripts/test-trustee-policies.sh        # opa test over trustee/policies/
```

Both run in [`test.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml)
(SPE Loader Tests, Trustee Policy Tests). The policy tests pin every case of
the resource policy, including HOST_DATA in the place where [Trustee v0.22.0](https://github.com/confidential-containers/trustee/releases/tag/v0.22.0)
puts it.

## 10. Deploying it on Azure

[`scripts/azure/21-aci-confidential-spe.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/21-aci-confidential-spe.sh)
does it in phases, in this order: `--trustee`, `--extracts`, `--policy`,
`--workspaces`, `--wire-proxy`, `--check`. The runbook has the
prerequisites (a [PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-configure) role activated before `az login`, the one-hour session)
and what each phase prints; read it before the first run. Two phases protect
themselves: `--extracts` refuses to re-key while Trustee holds keys unless
`--rekey`, and `--trustee` keeps a resource policy that Trustee already holds.

## 11. What is not done yet

- **The access body does not yet run its own Trustee.** Trustee's shares sit
  in the hub's subscription, so the subscription owner could read them. For
  the sovereignty claim to hold, MedReg DE runs Trustee in a subscription of
  its own ([ADR-069](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-069-two-spe-workspaces-as-aci-confidential-containers.md#decision) decision 3).
- **Trust remains in AMD and in Microsoft's utility VM.** Microsoft's
  endorsement of the utility VM's measurement is compared by the operator,
  but its [COSE](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9052) signature is not verified cryptographically yet.
- **[ADR-073](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-073-the-spe-tcb-is-a-minimum-not-a-list.md) is proposed.** The TCB minimum and its tests are on `main`
  ([#836](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/836)); the ADR says it is not applied on Azure yet.
- **AKS is not an option today.** The tenant policy refused it
  (`RequestDisallowedByPolicy`); an exemption is requested. AKS confidential
  containers were also being [retired by Microsoft](https://github.com/Azure/AKS/issues/3781) ([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md#decision)).
- **Not decided** ([ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md#not-decided-here)): which EU provider hosts the per-workload case
  outside Azure, and Trustee in a subscription of its own.

Issues: [#774](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/774)
(the Azure deployment), [#27](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/27),
[#481](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/481),
[#716](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/716),
[#833](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/833).

## 12. The decisions, in order

| ADR                                                                                               | Decision                                                                              | Status                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| [ADR-037](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-037-secure-processing-environment-confidential-computing.md)                | Confidential containers with remote attestation, not trust in the operator            | Accepted              |
| [ADR-052](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-052-confidential-spe-on-azure-revisited.md)                                 | AKS with Kata and Azure Attestation                                                   | Superseded by ADR-068 |
| [ADR-068](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-068-a-sovereign-confidential-spe-on-confidential-containers-and-trustee.md) | CNCF Confidential Containers, a Trustee the access body runs, Neo4j loaded per permit | Accepted (2026-10-30) |
| [ADR-069](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-069-two-spe-workspaces-as-aci-confidential-containers.md)                   | Two workspaces as ACI confidential containers; the policy hash is HOST_DATA           | Accepted (2026-11-02) |
| [ADR-072](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-072-spe-workspaces-start-on-demand.md)                                      | Stopped by default, started by a federated query, stopped after 30 idle minutes       | Accepted (2026-11-02) |
| [ADR-073](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-073-the-spe-tcb-is-a-minimum-not-a-list.md)                                 | The SEV-SNP TCB is checked against a minimum per component                            | Proposed              |

docs.summary: CodeQL, Semgrep, grype, npm audit, trivy, gitleaks, hadolint, shellcheck, the app's posture tests and the anonymous black-box checks of the live hub; findings F1 to F10 with their status after the fixes, and what an independent test would add.
docs.markdown:
# Security test report, 2026-10-15

A self-conducted security test of the Klarbefund app and the demo hub, by
the project, with the tools the repository can run: static analysis,
dependency and container scanning, secret scanning, configuration tests
and anonymous black-box checks of the live hub. **It is not an independent
penetration test.** What such a test would add is listed at the end. Every
number here is reproducible with the commands given; the raw reports of this
run are not committed (they carry paths), the scripts are.

| Item         | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Commit       | [`64737039`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/commit/64737039) on `feat/186-insurer-report` (the fixes below were made on the same branch)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Date         | 2026-10-15, 18:34 to 18:58 UTC                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Machine      | macOS 26.7.1, [Xcode 26](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes) (Swift 6.4), [syft 1.51.1](https://github.com/anchore/syft/releases/tag/v1.51.1), [grype 0.118.0](https://github.com/anchore/grype/releases/tag/v0.118.0), [trivy 0.74.0](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/tag/v0.74.0), [gitleaks 8.30.1](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/tag/v8.30.1), [semgrep 1.176.0](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep/releases/tag/v1.176.0), [CodeQL CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli) |
| Scope        | `clients/ios` (the app), `ui`, `services/*`, the Dockerfiles, the Kubernetes manifests, the live hub `ehds.mabu.red` from outside                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Not in scope | The EDC connectors and Keycloak internals (the hub's own threat model, [`threat-model.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-hub)), Apple's platform, the model providers behind [ADR-034](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-034-claude-workload-identity-federation.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Method

| Layer                  | Tool, what it checked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Command                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static analysis, Swift | CodeQL, security queries over 31 app and 51 Shared files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [`clients/ios/Scripts/codeql-swift.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/codeql-swift.sh)                                                    |
| Static analysis, TS/JS | CodeQL in CI on every push ([`codeql.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml)); Semgrep with the repository's own rules locally                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | [`scripts/security/scan-repo.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/scan-repo.sh)                                                                |
| Dependencies           | syft bills of materials, grype and npm audit against them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [`scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh), [`scan-repo.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/scan-repo.sh) |
| Filesystem             | trivy: vulnerabilities, secrets, misconfiguration in Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [`scan-repo.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/scan-repo.sh)                                                                                 |
| Secrets                | gitleaks over the tree and the last 200 commits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | [`scan-repo.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/scan-repo.sh)                                                                                 |
| Build configuration    | [`SecurityPostureTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/SecurityPostureTests.swift) (9 tests at the time; 11 since the app lock of [ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)): entitlements, privacy manifest, [ATS](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/preventing-insecure-network-connections), cryptography, [PKCE](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636#section-4.2), [HealthKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit) | `cd clients/ios && swift test --filter SecurityPostureTests`                                                                          |
| Behaviour              | The unit suites: 419 Swift tests, 2488 UI tests, 22 proxy tests on this branch                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `swift test`, `npm test`                                                                                                              |
| Live hub, anonymous    | 46 black-box checks: route gates, redirects, dotfiles, CORS, headers, TLS versions, Keycloak console                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | [`scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh)                                              |

## Results

| Check                                               | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CodeQL, Swift                                       | 0 findings, 0 accepted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Semgrep, local rules                                | 0 findings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| grype over the five bills                           | 0 matches (ui 530 components, proxy 180, epa-ingest 29, claude-federation 20, app 20 Apple frameworks, 0 third-party)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| npm audit, production, four lockfiles               | 0 critical, 0 high, 0 moderate, 0 low                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
