| trivy, vulnerabilities                              | 0 after the fix below (6 before, all in one Python package of the guideline scripts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| trivy, secrets                                      | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| trivy, misconfiguration                             | 0 after the fixes (3 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM and 12 LOW before; the last ten, the missing health checks of F6, closed 2026-10-16)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| gitleaks, tree                                      | 0 after review (2 before, both reviewed and allowlisted with the reason)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| gitleaks, last 200 commits                          | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| hadolint                                            | 5 info, 0 warning, 0 error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| shellcheck, error severity                          | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| SecurityPostureTests                                | 9 of 9 pass                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Unit suites                                         | all pass                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Live hub, black-box (second run, online, 20:37 UTC) | 44 of 46 checks pass: every API route refuses an anonymous caller (401), protected pages redirect, no dotfile served, no CORS reflection, all five security headers, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 refused, metrics closed. Two fails: one expectation of the script (a route that does not exist, fixed) and F10 below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Live hub, black-box                                 | **not run to completion**: the hub was in off-hours mode ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md), stops 18:13 UTC), every API route answered 503 and the script exits 3 by design. Repeat Mon to Fri 05:17 to 18:13 UTC. What the run did establish: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 refused, 1.2 and 1.3 offered (ECDHE, ChaCha20-Poly1305), certificate valid to 2027-02-08; no CORS origin reflected; Keycloak admin console, metrics and health not reachable from the internet (404); the dotfiles a scanner tries are rewritten to the offline page, not served |

## Findings

| #   | Severity       | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Where                                                                                                                                                                                             | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F1  | High           | `docling` 2.131.0 with three published advisories (two high)                                                                                                                                                                       | [`scripts/leitlinien/uv.lock`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/leitlinien/uv.lock)                                                                                                                                  | **Fixed**: `uv lock --upgrade-package docling`, now 2.139.0; grype and trivy report 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| F2  | High (scanner) | Three Dockerfiles without a `USER` instruction ([trivy DS-0002](https://avd.aquasec.com/misconfig/ds-0002))                                                                                                                        | [`load-tests/azure`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/load-tests/azure/Dockerfile), [`jad/keycloak-theme`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/keycloak-theme/Dockerfile), [`scripts/azure/vault-unseal`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/vault-unseal/Dockerfile) | **Fixed**: the k6 and Keycloak images already ran unprivileged, now stated; the vault-unseal sidecar drops to `vault` after its root-only `apk add`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F3  | Low            | gitleaks: IdentityHub superuser key in the compose stack's env file                                                                                                                                                                | [`jad/issuerservice.env`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/issuerservice.env) (tracked)                                                                                                                                  | **Reviewed**: the published development default of the local JAD stack; Azure takes keys from Vault ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)). Allowlisted with the reason in [`.gitleaks.toml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.gitleaks.toml)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| F4  | Info           | gitleaks: a public search key of the AWMF guideline register embedded in a fetch script                                                                                                                                            | [`scripts/leitlinien/fetch_index.py`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/leitlinien/fetch_index.py)                                                                                                                    | **Reviewed**: the register's own public page embeds it; grants nothing a browser lacks. Allowlisted with the reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F5  | Medium         | Kubernetes manifest: image tag `:latest` and a ConfigMap flagged as sensitive content                                                                                                                                              | [`k8s/health-dataspace-ui.yaml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/k8s/health-dataspace-ui.yaml)                                                                                                                              | **Fixed 2026-10-15**: tag pinned to the package version; the flagged ConfigMap keys are a public client id and issuer URL (the secrets already sit in the Secret), recorded as a reviewed false positive in [`.trivyignore`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.trivyignore); trivy reports 0 on the manifest                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| F6  | Closed         | No `HEALTHCHECK` in ten Dockerfiles                                                                                                                                                                                                | `ui`, `services/*`, `scripts/azure/*`, others                                                                                                                                                     | **Fixed 2026-10-16**: every image carries a `HEALTHCHECK` matched to what it serves: the hub's `/api/health`, the proxy's and the explanation service's `/health`, the crawlers' Prometheus endpoint, Keycloak's `/health/ready` and Grafana's `/api/health` through a bash socket (neither image has curl), `vault status` for the unseal sidecar; the two one-shot jobs say `HEALTHCHECK NONE`. Container Apps still takes its probes from the app definition. trivy reports 0 misconfigurations over the repository                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| F7  | Low            | Kubernetes manifest runs with UID and GID below 10000                                                                                                                                                                              | [`k8s/health-dataspace-ui.yaml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/k8s/health-dataspace-ui.yaml)                                                                                                                              | **Fixed 2026-10-15**: runs as 10001                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F8  | Observe        | On the off-hours page the response carried Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy but not HSTS, X-Frame-Options or X-Content-Type-Options, although [`next.config`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/next.config.js#L76-L105) sets all five for every path | `ehds.mabu.red/`, off hours                                                                                                                                                                       | **Closed 2026-10-15 20:37 UTC**: online, all five headers are present on `/`; only the off-hours page lacked them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| F10 | Closed         | Keycloak admin console reachable from the internet: `auth.ehds.mabu.red/admin/master/console/` answers 200 (login still required; found when the black-box checks ran online at 20:37 UTC)                                         | Keycloak ingress                                                                                                                                                                                  | **Fix scripted**: [`scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh) adds a Caddy sidecar that answers 403 for `/admin/*/console/*` and proxies the rest, keeping the admin REST API (which the hub and the provisioning scripts use with a token) reachable; Keycloak's own docs say the `hostname-admin` option does not prevent access to the Administration REST API through the frontend URL ([hostname](https://www.keycloak.org/server/hostname#administration-console-on-a-separate-hostname)) and recommend exposing `/admin/` only internally ([reverse proxy](https://www.keycloak.org/server/reverseproxy#_exposed_path_recommendations)). **Applied and verified 2026-10-15 21:19 UTC**: with Keycloak started briefly behind the guard, discovery 200, the console paths 403, the admin REST API 401 without a token, the token endpoint answering, and [`check-keycloak-health.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/check-keycloak-health.sh) reporting the realm served from a working database; then stopped again. Rollback: the definition saved under `~/.mvhd/keycloak-rollback/` |
| F9  | Closed         | No app lock, no jailbreak detection, no certificate pinning in the app                                                                                                                                                             | `clients/ios`                                                                                                                                                                                     | **Decided 2026-10-15 ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md))**: app lock implemented, on by default; pinning and jailbreak detection declined with reasons                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## What an independent test would add

This report is the project testing itself with deterministic tools. It
does not replace, and the self-assessment does not claim, an independent
penetration test. Such a test, by a BSI-recognised laboratory or a
contracted tester, would add:

1. **A release build on a device**: runtime inspection of the Keychain
   items, the sealed store and the file protection classes with the phone
   locked and unlocked; the cable test repeated by someone else.
2. **Authenticated black-box testing of the hub** as each of the seven
   roles, in office hours: horizontal access between patients ([`refuseForeignRecord`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient/own-record.ts#L19)), the
   app token's scope, rate limits under load, the App Attest verification
   with a replayed or forged attestation.
3. **The [TR-03161 part 1](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2) requirement list**, item by item against the
   official document, which this project assesses only at the level of its
   objective groups ([`docs/klarbefund/self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment)).
4. **Keycloak and EDC configuration review** beyond what the public
   endpoints show.

Until then, the status in the self-assessment reads "tested by the
project, independent test open", and this document is the evidence for
the first half of that sentence.

docs.title: Threat model: the EHDS Integration Hub
docs.summary: STRIDE for the hub on Azure: the data flows and trust boundaries, the four attackers, one exchange with every threat at its step, and each mitigation naming the code, the test or the decision that shows it; what the demo accepts and what real data needs, and how to verify every row.
docs.markdown:
# Threat model: the EHDS Integration Hub

STRIDE, for the hub as it runs on Azure Container Apps: the UI and its API
([Next.js 15](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v15.5.28)), [Keycloak 26.8](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/releases/tag/26.8.0), the neo4j-proxy, the EDC-V connectors with their
IdentityHub and IssuerService, [Neo4j 5.26](https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/5/) and the [PostgreSQL Flexible Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/overview).
Written 2026-10-16; each mitigation names the code, the test or the decision
that shows it. The app that connects to the hub has its own model,
[`threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund). What the project
tested and found is the
[security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report); how the platform
would be run for real data is the
[operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline).

The data on the hub is synthetic: 127 generated patients, fictional
organisations, forged load-test sessions. The threats below are assessed as
if the data were real, because the hub is a reference implementation for a
platform that will hold real data; where a mitigation is enough for the demo
and not for real data, the table says so.

## How to read this model

[STRIDE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/develop/threat-modeling-tool-threats) asks six questions of every data flow: can the sender be spoofed, the
data tampered with, the action repudiated, information disclosed, the service
denied, privilege elevated. The system context in section 1 numbers the data
flows and the trust boundaries they cross; the sequence in section 3 shows one
complete exchange with the id of every threat at the step where it would
happen; the six tables then hold one row per threat with the flow it sits on,
its status, and the mitigation with the evidence. The evidence is a file, a
test, a script or a decision in this repository, so each row can be checked
without asking anyone.

Four attackers are assumed, and every row names at least one implicitly by
its flow:

| Attacker                        | Reaches                                         | Holds                                                        | Wants                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Anyone on the internet          | B1: the hub's pages and API, Keycloak's sign-in | Nothing; or a leaked cookie, token or password               | A patient's record, a session, the admin console, the platform offline                            |
| A signed-in participant         | B1 with a valid session, as its role            | A legitimate account in one role                             | Data outside its role or its permit, another patient's record, a louder voice than its rate limit |
| A peer connector                | B2 through the public control plane             | Its own DID and credentials; forged or stolen ones           | A contract it is not entitled to, data without an agreement, a false identity                     |
| An insider with operator rights | B2 and B3 through `az`, `gh` and the scripts    | Subscription rights, the deploy identity, the admin password | Secrets, a silent change, a cleared audit trail                                                   |

A fifth, the supply chain, has no flow of its own: a compromised dependency or
image arrives through the deploy (F7) and is treated under tampering (T-07).

## 1. System context: data flows and trust boundaries

![The hub's data flows and trust boundaries: the people, the app, a peer connector and the operator outside; the UI and Keycloak behind the internet edge; the proxy, the connectors, the crawler and observability inside the environment; Neo4j, PostgreSQL, Vault and Key Vault behind the data boundary; twenty-one numbered flows](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/hub-trust-boundaries.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/hub-trust-boundaries.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/hub-trust-boundaries.puml),
rendered with [`scripts/render-plantuml.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/render-plantuml.sh).

Three boundaries, and what crossing each one means:

| Boundary              | Who can send a request across it                   | What proves identity                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B1, the internet edge | Anyone                                             | The session cookie ([NextAuth JWT](https://next-auth.js.org/configuration/options#jwt)), a bearer token from Keycloak, or a [DCP](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/) credential |
| B2, the environment   | The hub's own apps and jobs, over internal ingress | The caller header the hub sets (`X-Caller`), the catalog token, the connector's DID                                                                                                                                       |
| B3, data and secrets  | The environment only                               | The managed identity (Key Vault references), the Vault token, the database credentials                                                                                                                                    |

The numbered flows (F1 to F21) are what the STRIDE tables refer to. The ones
that matter most, and why:

| Flow       | What crosses                                         | Why it is the one to watch                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F1         | Every page and API request, with the session cookie  | The only path an anonymous attacker has to the data; every route behind it needs a session ([ADR-044](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-044-every-api-route-needs-a-session.md)) |
| F2, F8     | Sign-in and the token exchange with Keycloak         | A forged or over-scoped token is a forged identity for everything downstream                                                                               |
| F3, F4     | The app's bearer token and its account creation      | A phone is outside anyone's control; App Attest is what keeps account creation to the genuine app                                                          |
| F5         | DSP and DCP between connectors                       | The one flow where a stranger's software talks to ours by design; identity is the DID and the credential, not a login                                      |
| F9         | The hub's call to the proxy, with the caller header  | The proxy trusts the header because only the hub can reach it; the boundary B2 is what makes that trust sound                                              |
| F10, F11   | The management API and the catalog token             | Full control of the connectors; internal ingress and one token in Key Vault are the whole defence                                                          |
| F14, F15   | Reads and writes to the graph, and the audit records | Where the patient data and the evidence live; parameterised queries and the hash chain are the controls                                                    |
| F19 to F21 | Keys and secrets                                     | Vault, its sealed state and Key Vault; nothing here is ever copied into an app                                                                             |

## 2. Assets

| Asset                                                                          | Sensitivity | Where it lives                                  | Notes                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Patient records (FHIR, OMOP)                                                   | High        | Neo4j (B3)                                      | Synthetic today; the model treats them as real                                                                                                                              |
| Who read whose record, the audit chain                                         | High        | Neo4j, hash-chained (B3)                        | Regulatory evidence ([Art. 73(1)(e)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.001)); at least twelve months ([retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md)) |
| Participant signing keys                                                       | High        | Vault, state on the Flexible Server (B3)        | Never leave Vault; [ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)                                                                               |
| Operator secrets: `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, DB and admin passwords, the catalog token | High        | Azure Key Vault, referenced by the apps (B3)    | [ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md); the live `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was rotated after it had been a published default                                   |
| Sessions and tokens                                                            | High        | Cookie in the browser, bearer in the app        | NextAuth JWT; Keycloak access and refresh tokens                                                                                                                            |
| Verifiable credentials and permits                                             | Medium      | IdentityHub (B2)                                | Membership, EHDS participant, purpose, quality label, the permit as a credential                                                                                            |
| Contracts, transfers, tasks                                                    | Medium      | EDC state in PostgreSQL (B3), mirrored to Neo4j | ODRL policies, agreements, `TransferEvent` nodes                                                                                                                            |
| Catalogue metadata                                                             | Low         | Neo4j, the connectors                           | [HealthDCAT-AP](https://healthdcat-ap.github.io/); public by design                                                                                                         |
| The graph schema and the code                                                  | Low         | GitHub, public                                  | The documentation is the schema                                                                                                                                             |

## 3. STRIDE

![One data exchange as a sequence, with the STRIDE id of every threat at the step where it sits: sign-in and request through the hub, then the DSP negotiation and the DCP credential check in the connectors, then the transfer and the audit record](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/hub-exchange-threats.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/hub-exchange-threats.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/hub-exchange-threats.puml).

Status: **closed** means a test or a build setting pins it; **in place** means
the code does it and a test exercises it indirectly; **demo** means enough for
synthetic data and named as open for real data; **open** means nothing does it
yet.

### Spoofing

| ID   | Threat                                 | Flow   | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---- | -------------------------------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| S-01 | A connector impersonates a participant | F5     | In place | [`did:web`](https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-web/) resolution against the IdentityHub's DID document, one per participant; the [DCP](https://eclipse-dataspace-dcp.github.io/decentralized-claims-protocol/v1.0/) presentation carries the membership credential ([ADR-007](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-007-did-web-dsp-negotiation.md), [ADR-009](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-009-issuerservice-credential-fix.md)). Checked by the hub's own `scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh` once a night when main changed ([ADR-074](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-074-e2e-and-compliance-suites-run-nightly-when-main-changed.md)); the Eclipse [DCP TCK](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dcp-tck) has not been run. |
| S-02 | A forged session reaches an API route  | F1     | Closed   | NextAuth JWT signed with `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` from Key Vault; [`requireAuth()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/auth-guard.ts#L22) in every handler, pinned by [`ui/__tests__/unit/api/every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/__tests__/unit/api/every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts) ([ADR-044](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-044-every-api-route-needs-a-session.md)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| S-03 | A replayed credential presentation     | F5     | In place | The EDC-V DCP implementation binds the presentation to the request; the DCP checks of [`compliance.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/compliance.yml) run it nightly. Not re-verified by the hub itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| S-04 | Keycloak realm or console takeover     | F2, F6 | Closed   | The admin console is off the internet ([`guard-keycloak-console.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh), F10 of the [test report](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings)); the admin password lives in Key Vault; the realm is version-controlled and drift-checked ([runbook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/keycloak-realm-drift.md)). MFA on the admin is for the operator (guideline, identity).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| S-05 | A fake Klarbefund creates accounts     | F3     | In place | Account creation answers only a request whose [Apple App Attest](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity) attestation verifies ([ADR-054](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-054-klarbefund-creates-a-sandbox-account-with-app-attest.md)); the challenge is signed and lives five minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

### Tampering

| ID   | Threat                                            | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T-01 | Cypher injection                                  | F14, F15 | Closed   | Parameterised Cypher everywhere; the NLQ engine refuses a query that would read a patient's identity unless the UI says the role may ([`revealsPatientIdentity()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/nlq/engine.ts#L834)); tests in [`services/neo4j-proxy/__tests__/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/neo4j-proxy/__tests__).                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| T-02 | Contract terms changed in transit                 | F5       | In place | TLS at the edge; the agreement is signed by the provider's connector. Mutually authenticated DSP endpoints are a guideline item for real data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| T-03 | A forged credential claim                         | F5       | In place | Credentials are issued and verified by the IssuerService and IdentityHub (EDC-V); the hub shows, it does not re-sign. An HSM for the issuer key is a guideline item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| T-04 | Cross-site request forgery on a mutation          | F1       | In place | `SameSite=Lax` session cookie (NextAuth); the CSP forbids inline scripts; no mutation reads its parameters from a GET.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| T-05 | A state jump in the negotiation                   | F5       | In place | The state machines live in the EDC-V control plane (REQUESTED, AGREED, FINALIZED; transfers REQUESTED to COMPLETED) and are leased in PostgreSQL; the hub mirrors, it does not drive. The hub's dataspace checks run nightly ([ADR-074](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-074-e2e-and-compliance-suites-run-nightly-when-main-changed.md)); they drive the management APIs and are not the Eclipse [DSP 2025-1 TCK](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dsp-tck), which has not been run.                                                            |
| T-06 | The audit trail edited                            | F15      | Closed   | Each record carries the hash of its predecessor, SHA-256 over canonical JSON ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785)); [`verifyChain()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/audit-chain.ts#L206) reports any change, removal or reordering ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md), [`audit-chain.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/audit-chain.ts)). Both chains were intact after every load run.                                                                                      |
| T-07 | A supply-chain change in a dependency or an image | F7       | Closed   | One [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/) bill per part, checked against the lockfiles; [grype](https://github.com/anchore/grype/releases/tag/v0.118.0) and [trivy](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/tag/v0.74.0) weekly and on every pull request that changes a dependency or an image; npm audit in pre-push with time-boxed exceptions; images pinned; [CodeQL](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli). [SBOM](/docs/security/sbom), [`security-scan.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml). |

### Repudiation

| ID   | Threat                                           | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R-01 | A party denies a transfer happened               | F15      | Closed   | `TransferEvent` with sender and receiver DID and timestamp, in the hash-chained `dsp` chain ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)).                                                |
| R-02 | A party denies agreeing to a contract            | F5       | In place | The agreement is signed by the connector and stored in the EDC state; mirrored to the graph with its id.                                                                                                             |
| R-03 | A read of a patient's record is denied or hidden | F14, F15 | Closed   | Every access the proxy serves is an access event in the `query` chain; the patient sees who read their record on their own page; retention at least twelve months ([policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md)).          |
| R-04 | An operator action leaves no trace               | F6, F7   | In place | Keycloak login events kept seven days; deploys are GitHub Actions runs; every live step is a script under [`scripts/azure/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/scripts/azure) and recorded in the gotchas or an ADR. A SIEM is a guideline item. |

### Information disclosure

| ID   | Threat                                                | Flow       | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| I-01 | An anonymous caller reads data                        | F1         | Closed   | Every API route needs a session ([ADR-044](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-044-every-api-route-needs-a-session.md)); the pages that read them are in [`PROTECTED_PATHS`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/middleware.ts#L43) and redirect; 46 black-box checks of the live hub confirm the 401s and redirects ([`check-hub-blackbox.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| I-02 | The connectors' management API reachable from outside | F10        | In place | Internal ingress only; the UI reaches it by its internal name, pinned on every deploy ([#648](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/648)). The catalog crawler sends its token only to listed hosts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| I-03 | Secrets in the page or the repository                 | F1, F7     | Closed   | Server-side environment only; Key Vault references ([ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md)); gitleaks in the hooks and in CI; a test asserts no secret reaches the HTML.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| I-04 | Cross-site scripting exfiltrates a session            | F1         | Closed   | A per-request nonce in the CSP with `strict-dynamic` ([`middleware.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/middleware.ts#L88-L95)), no `unsafe-inline` for scripts; `HttpOnly` session cookie; headers pinned by `next.config.js` and checked black-box. The off-hours page missed some headers once (F8, observe).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| I-05 | A database reachable from the internet                | F14 to F20 | Accepted | Neo4j and Vault have no public ingress. The Flexible Server answers on a public endpoint whose firewall rule `0.0.0.0` admits any Azure service, other customers' subscriptions included ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/network/how-to-networking-servers-deployed-public-access-add-firewall-rules)); the admin password, kept in Key Vault, is the gate. ACA Consumption has no stable egress IP for a narrower rule ([ADR-041](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-041-managed-postgres-on-azure-containerised-locally.md), [`13-postgres-flexible-server.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/13-postgres-flexible-server.sh#L143-L153)). |
| I-06 | Clickjacking                                          | F1         | Closed   | `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, black-box checked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| I-07 | Re-identification from a cohort                       | F9, F12    | In place | [`MIN_COHORT_SIZE`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/config.ts#L94) of 5 in the proxy for federated queries; roles other than the holder and the operator see a pseudonym, the birth year and no residence ([#475](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/475)). Output control by the access body is a process the demo does not run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| I-08 | An expired or revoked credential accepted             | F5         | Demo     | The IdentityHub checks expiry; there is no revocation list in the demo. Status lists and a revocation procedure are guideline items for real data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| I-09 | Logs carry personal data                              | F13        | In place | The proxy logs counts and codes, the caller as a hash; Azure Monitor keeps 30 days; the operational logs are separate from the audit chain ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### Denial of service

| ID   | Threat                                    | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D-01 | One user exhausts the proxy               | F9       | Closed   | Per user: `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` requests and `RATE_LIMIT_HEAVY_MAX` analytical queries per `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`; per participant ten times that for callers that name no user; the audit route has its own. Measured: 83.6 % refused before, 23.2 % after the per-user limit (2026-10-05).                          |
| D-02 | A flood of DSP messages at the connectors | F5       | Demo     | The EDC-V control plane leases its state machines in PostgreSQL and times out; no rate limit at the connector's edge. A WAF and rate limits per hostname are guideline items.                                                                                                                                    |
| D-03 | An unbounded query                        | F14, F15 | Closed   | `LIMIT` on every list route; the graph views capped at the newest 30 access events ([#580](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/580)), which removed the one request that took the UI down at 90 concurrent users; every outbound call has a timeout.                                     |
| D-04 | Load takes the platform down              | F1       | In place | 400 users with no failed request (2026-10-06); the UI scales on an HTTP concurrency rule to six whole-core replicas ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)); health checks on every image; a deploy waits while a load test runs. The latency SLOs break from 200 users; measured next. |
| D-05 | The stack is off                          | F1       | Accepted | Everything stops off hours by decision ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md)) and the UI says so; a 24x7 contract removes the schedule (guideline, availability).                                                                                                                            |

### Elevation of privilege

| ID   | Threat                                             | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| E-01 | A patient reaches an admin route                   | F1       | Closed   | [`requireAuth(["EDC_ADMIN"])`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/auth-guard.ts#L22) on the admin routes, 403 for any other role; the role matrix in [`.claude/rules/api-conventions.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/api-conventions.md#roles-and-access-control); Bruno folder [`09 Access control`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/bruno/MVHDv2/09%20Access%20control) asserts it against a real server. |
| E-02 | A researcher reads a patient's identity            | F1, F9   | Closed   | [`seesPatientIdentity()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient-identity.ts#L33) decides by role; [`refuseForeignRecord()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient/own-record.ts#L19) answers 403 for another patient's record; the NLQ proxy refuses identity reads without the UI's header ([#475](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/475)). Bruno `09 Access control/28` to `/30`.                               |
| E-03 | Roles injected into the token                      | F2, F8   | Closed   | Roles come from the realm's claims only; the UI client has full scope off and exactly the seven EHDS roles in scope ([#648](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/648), [`wire-ui-client-scope.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/wire-ui-client-scope.sh)); [`auth.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/auth.ts) maps nothing else.                                                                                   |
| E-04 | The catalog token used from elsewhere              | F10, F11 | In place | One token in Key Vault, reaching the UI and the crawler as a reference; the crawler sends it only to `DSP_CATALOG_TOKEN_HOSTS`; a wrong token is 401, never a fall back to the session ([ADR-020](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-020-cross-participant-dataset-discovery.md), [ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md)).                                                                                            |
| E-05 | A transfer without an agreement                    | F5, F12  | In place | The data plane hands out an EDR for a finalised agreement only (EDC-V); the hub records the `contractId` with every transfer. No protocol conformance test yet: the hub's dataspace checks are not a DSP peer, and the Eclipse [DSP TCK](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dsp-tck) has not been run.                                                                                                         |
| E-06 | The operator account `edcadmin` on a demo password | F2       | Open     | `EDC_ADMIN` reads a patient's record without a contract negotiation. [`scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh) moves it and every non-demo account to a generated password in Key Vault; to be run against the live realm ([#671](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/671)).                                                                             |

### Summary

| Category               | Threats | Closed | In place |  Demo |  Open | Accepted |
| ---------------------- | ------: | -----: | -------: | ----: | ----: | -------: |
| Spoofing               |       5 |      2 |        3 |     0 |     0 |        0 |
| Tampering              |       7 |      3 |        4 |     0 |     0 |        0 |
| Repudiation            |       4 |      2 |        2 |     0 |     0 |        0 |
| Information disclosure |       9 |      4 |        3 |     1 |     0 |        1 |
| Denial of service      |       5 |      2 |        1 |     1 |     0 |        1 |
| Elevation of privilege |       6 |      3 |        2 |     0 |     1 |        0 |
| **All**                |  **36** | **16** |   **15** | **2** | **1** |    **2** |

Closed and in place differ in how they are proven: a closed row has a test or
a build setting that fails when the mitigation goes; an in-place row relies on
the code doing it and on the suites that exercise it. Turning in-place rows
into closed ones is the ordinary work of this model.

## 4. What the demo accepts, and what real data needs

| Residual risk                                     | Why it is accepted for the demo                                                                                                                    | What closes it                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| No revocation of credentials (I-08)               | Every credential is issued to a fictional participant by the demo                                                                                  | A status list in the IssuerService and a revocation procedure; guideline, identity                                                                     |
| No rate limit at the connectors' edge (D-02)      | The connectors talk to fictional peers only                                                                                                        | A WAF and per-hostname limits; guideline, edge                                                                                                         |
| No mTLS between apps (T-02)                       | One environment, internal ingress                                                                                                                  | Private endpoints and mutually authenticated DSP endpoints; guideline, connectors                                                                      |
| Neo4j has one database user                       | Access is decided in the hub and the proxy, and the data is synthetic                                                                              | Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph with roles and backups; guideline, data                                                                            |
| Operator accounts on demo passwords (E-06)        | Nobody's real data is behind them                                                                                                                  | [`secure-accounts.sh --all-non-demo`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh); [#671](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/671) |
| No independent test                               | The project's own tests are the evidence so far                                                                                                    | A penetration test of the hub; test report, last section; [#655](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/655)                    |
| PostgreSQL reachable from any Azure tenant (I-05) | ACA Consumption has no stable egress IP ([ADR-041](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-041-managed-postgres-on-azure-containerised-locally.md)), and the data is synthetic | A VNet-integrated environment with private access to the Flexible Server; guideline, data                                                              |
| The stack is off outside office hours (D-05)      | A cost decision for a demo                                                                                                                         | A 24x7 service contract; guideline, availability                                                                                                       |

## 5. How this model is kept true

- A new API route needs a session or a superseding ADR; the test
  [`every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/__tests__/unit/api/every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts) fails otherwise.
- A new route that returns patient fields asks [`seesPatientIdentity()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/patient-identity.ts#L33)
  first, and the Bruno collection gets a request that asserts the refusal.
- Every change runs the security scan, CodeQL, the compliance suites and the
  black-box checks; a finding goes into the security test report with a
  status, never only into a commit message.
- The diagrams are PlantUML sources under [`diagrams/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/docs/security/diagrams), rendered by
  [`scripts/render-plantuml.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/render-plantuml.sh); a flow added to the system gets a number here
  and a row in the table that analyses it.

## 6. How to verify this model yourself

Every closed row has a check that can be run on a laptop or read in CI:

```bash
cd ui && npx vitest run __tests__/unit/api/every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts   # S-02, I-01, E-01
cd ui && npx vitest run __tests__/unit/api/patient-route.test.ts                   # E-02, I-07
scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh                                             # I-01, I-04, I-06, S-04 against the live hub
scripts/security/scan-repo.sh                                                      # T-07: grype, npm audit, trivy, gitleaks, semgrep, hadolint, shellcheck
scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh --check                                          # T-07: the bills match the lockfiles
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Azure-Dev "09 Access control"                           # E-01, E-02, E-04 by persona, against a real server
scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh --check                                    # S-04: console 403, admin REST 401, master realm 401
cd services/neo4j-proxy && npm test                                                # T-01, T-06, D-01, D-03
```

The compliance suites ([`compliance.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/compliance.yml): the hub's own dataspace and identity
checks, which are not the Eclipse [DSP](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dsp-tck) and [DCP](https://github.com/eclipse-dataspacetck/dcp-tck) TCKs, and the
EHDS suites) cover the connector rows, S-01, S-03, T-05, E-05, once a night
when main changed ([ADR-074](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-074-e2e-and-compliance-suites-run-nightly-when-main-changed.md)). A row whose check is missing from this list is an in-place row,
and the next step for it is the test that would move it.
