Everything below is the synthetic benchmark; no real report was involved, so the
counts are published as they are in
[`accuracy-benchmark.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json), the file the run wrote.
This is the project checking itself: a reviewer reproduces it with the same
three commands, and a pilot on real reports is still open.

| Step                      | Result                                                |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `swift build`             | Shared, AnalyteParity, ScanReplay and LabFile built   |
| `swift run AnalyteParity` | parity ok: 1589 codings, 71 units                     |
| `swift test`              | 319 tests in 54 suites passed, 0 failures, about 10 s |

One synthetic panel of 8 rows, read with Vision under nine conditions, 72
truth rows in all. `AccuracyBenchmarkTests` asserts zero silent errors under
each condition; the other columns are reported, not asserted.

| Condition          | Found | Exact | Silent errors | Spurious | Unread lines | Reference right |
| ------------------ | ----: | ----: | ------------: | -------: | -----------: | --------------: |
| clean 150 dpi scan |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| skewed 1 degree    |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| skewed 2 degrees   |     7 |     5 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           5 / 7 |
| skewed 5 degrees   |     5 |     0 |             0 |        0 |            2 |           0 / 5 |
| dim room           |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| flash glare        |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| slight motion blur |     7 |     7 |             0 |        0 |            1 |           7 / 7 |
| heavy blur         |     0 |     0 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           0 / 0 |
| low resolution     |     7 |     6 |             0 |        0 |            1 |           7 / 7 |
| **all nine**       |    58 |    50 |         **0** |    **0** |            4 |         51 / 58 |

What the numbers say: a clean, dim, glaring or slightly skewed sheet is read
in full and exactly. As the sheet degrades the app loses rows, first in the
reference-range column, then whole rows, until heavy blur yields nothing at
all. At no point does it show a value, unit or code that is wrong, which is
the property the suite enforces.

One finding from the run itself: the test target did not compile with
Swift 6.4, because `Comparator` had become ambiguous between `Shared` and the
platform SDK. The test now names `Shared.Comparator`, as `OmopExportTests`
already did.

## Open

| Topic                                      | What is missing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Intended purpose (MDR)                     | A written qualification under [MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/b45335c5-1679-4c71-a91c-fc7a4d37f12b_en). The borderline is the trends screen, which colours values against published bands ([ADR-039](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-039-published-reference-ranges.md)); the project's position is that a comparison with a quoted number is not a finding. An external opinion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Operator of the hosted explanation service | Explanations run on the device by default. The person can switch to the hosted service (default [Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/deployment-types#data-zone-standard), EU data zone; Anthropic opt-in, United States) or to their own Azure OpenAI or Anthropic account. Whoever runs the hosted service processes health data and must document that role (records of processing, processor agreements).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Data protection                            | Data-flow diagram and a [data protection impact assessment](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_35) template for an operator.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Security                                   | Threat model, SBOM and a self-conducted security test exist since 2026-10-15 ([`docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund), [`docs/sbom/`](/docs/security/sbom), [`docs/security/security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report)). The app locks with Face ID or the passcode since 2026-10-15 ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)). Open: an independent penetration test and the requirement-level gap list against BSI TR-03161 part 1. CodeQL runs on every iOS change ([`codeql-swift.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql-swift.yml)). |
| Pilot accuracy                             | Truth files and aggregate counts from real reports, as above.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

docs.title: Klarbefund: evidence report for health insurers
docs.summary: The three questions an insurer asks, is the extraction right, is the data safe, is it a medical device, answered with the evidence, plus the white-label and consulting offer.
docs.markdown:
# Klarbefund: evidence report for health insurers

Date 2026-10-15. Prepared by the project for a statutory or private health
insurer, a hospital group or an ePA vendor who asks the same three
questions: _is the extraction right, is the data safe, and is this a
medical device?_ Everything here is produced by tools that anyone can run on
the repository, with the commands given, and every open item is named as
open. The one-page version for a steering meeting is the summary table; the
rest is the evidence behind each line.

**What is on offer.** Klarbefund is a demo environment and an open-source
reference implementation ([Apache 2.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/LICENSE)). It is not a product with a vendor
behind it. What the project offers an insurer is either a **white-label
version** of the app, under the insurer's name and operator responsibility,
or **technical consulting** to integrate the scanner, the coding dictionary
and the FHIR writer into an ePA or EHR app the insurer already runs. Both
paths start from the evidence below.

## Summary

| Question                                  | Answer, with the evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Status                                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Does it read laboratory values correctly? | Synthetic benchmark under nine scan conditions: 0 silent errors, 0 invented values, 50 of 72 rows exact; degraded scans lose rows, they never show a wrong value. 1751 analyte codings, 71 units, LOINC and [UCUM](https://ucum.org/ucum).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | evidenced, pilot on real reports open   |
| Is the data safe?                         | On the device by default, [Face ID](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/localauthentication) or passcode in front of the results, [AES-GCM](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptokit/aes/gcm) per record, key in the [Secure Enclave-backed Keychain](https://support.apple.com/guide/security/keychain-data-protection-secb0694df1a/web), no third-party package, read-only Apple Health. CodeQL 0 findings, 0 known vulnerabilities, 9 posture tests, threat model, SBOM.                                                                                                                                                                                      | self-tested, independent test open      |
| Is it a medical device?                   | Intended purpose: store, display, export and explain what a measurement is; no diagnosis, no verdict. Under [MDCG 2019-11](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/b45335c5-1679-4c71-a91c-fc7a4d37f12b_en) generally not a device; the trends colouring is the borderline the project has written down.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | position written, external opinion open |
| Does it fit the ePA and the EHDS?         | [FHIR R4](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/) with LOINC, UCUM, [SNOMED CT](https://www.snomed.org/), [CVX](https://www2a.cdc.gov/vaccines/iis/iisstandards/vaccines.asp?rpt=cvx) and [ATC](https://atcddd.fhi.no/atc_ddd_index/); the test database now carries results in three of the six [EHDS Art. 14(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#014.001) priority categories: medical test results, imaging reports and, as content of the patient summary, vaccinations and the medication plan; the hub exports the whole record in one Bundle; [Art. 47](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_47) wellness label applies if marketed as interoperable. | yes                                     |
| Is it a DiGA?                             | No, by design: a DiGA must be a CE-marked device ([§ 33a SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__33a.html)). No DiGA certificates are claimed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | n/a                                     |
| Can my team verify this?                  | Yes: every number has a command, the scans and tests run on a Mac with Xcode, and the hub's API collection ([Bruno](https://www.usebruno.com/)) rehearses the integration.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | yes                                     |

## 1. What Klarbefund does

A person photographs a laboratory report or opens the laboratory's PDF.
The app reads it on the device, codes every row with LOINC and UCUM, keeps
the printed reference range, shows trends across reports, and exports the
record as FHIR R4, [OMOP CDM](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54.html), JSON or PDF. Values read from a photograph stay
`preliminary` until the person checks them; only a laboratory's own PDF
text layer yields `final`. With consent the app writes the person's record
into their own account on the EHDS demo hub, and weekly means from Apple
Health beside it. Nothing leaves the phone otherwise.

Details: [`README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/README.md) (person-facing),
[`clients/ios/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/README.md) (developer),
[`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence), [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment).

## 2. Accuracy

The measure is `ExtractionAccuracy`: a field-by-field comparison with a
hand-checked truth, value, unit, code, reference range and date. The number
that matters clinically is **silent errors**, rows the app showed as a value
and got wrong; the benchmark asserts zero under every condition.

| Condition          | Found | Exact | Silent errors | Spurious |
| ------------------ | ----: | ----: | ------------: | -------: |
| clean 150 dpi scan |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| skewed 1 degree    |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| skewed 2 degrees   |     7 |     5 |             0 |        0 |
| skewed 5 degrees   |     5 |     0 |             0 |        0 |
| dim room           |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| flash glare        |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| slight motion blur |     7 |     7 |             0 |        0 |
| heavy blur         |     0 |     0 |             0 |        0 |
| low resolution     |     7 |     6 |             0 |        0 |
| **all nine**       |    58 |    50 |         **0** |    **0** |

Synthetic sheets, 8 rows each, read with Apple [Vision](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/recognizing-text-in-images), 2026-10-15
([`accuracy-benchmark.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json)). A pilot on real
reports, with written consent and only counts leaving the participant's
folder, is designed ([`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence#measuring-accuracy)) and
not yet run; an insurer's own pilot is the natural next step.

## 3. Security and data protection

| Layer                                                                                                                                                    | What was done                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Result, 2026-10-15                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static analysis                                                                                                                                          | CodeQL over the app (82 Swift files); CodeQL and Semgrep over the hub in CI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 0 findings                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Dependencies                                                                                                                                             | [CycloneDX](https://cyclonedx.org/) bills for the app and every hub service ([`docs/sbom/`](/docs/security/sbom)); grype and npm audit against them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | 0 known vulnerabilities; the app has 0 third-party packages                                                                                                                                                 |
| Secrets                                                                                                                                                  | gitleaks over the tree and the last 200 commits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | 0 after review                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Containers, manifests                                                                                                                                    | trivy over Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | 0 after the fixes, as of 2026-10-16 (3 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 12 LOW before)                                                                                                                                       |
| Build configuration                                                                                                                                      | [`SecurityPostureTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/SecurityPostureTests.swift): entitlements, privacy manifest, ATS, cryptography, PKCE, HealthKit read-only, export compliance                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 9 of 9 pass; 11 since the app lock ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)) was added the same day                                            |
| Threat model                                                                                                                                             | STRIDE for the app ([`threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund)) beside the hub's                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | written; residual risks listed                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Live hub, outside                                                                                                                                        | 46 anonymous black-box checks ([`check-hub-blackbox.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh)): route gates, redirects, headers, TLS, Keycloak console                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | 44 of 46 pass in the online run at 20:37 UTC; the two fails were a script expectation (fixed) and [F10](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings), the Keycloak console, closed at 21:19 UTC |
| GDPR                                                                                                                                                     | [Art. 25](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_25) by default, [Art. 5](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_5) minimisation, [Art. 6](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_6)/[9](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_9) consents, [Art. 15](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_15)/[17](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_17)/[20](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng#art_20) rights: met in code; transparency and transfers partly; DPIA and controller role open | see [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment)                                                                                                                                                              |
| BSI [TR-03161](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03161/TR-03161-1.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=2) part 1 | Assessed by objective group: 8 met, 2 partly, 1 open (resilience, declined with reasons in [ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)), 2 n/a                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | input to a laboratory's gap analysis                                                                                                                                                                        |

The full method, findings and fixes are in
[`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report).
It is the project testing itself. An independent penetration test, which
an insurer will rightly ask for, is listed there with what it would add.

## 4. Regulatory position

| Framework                                                                                                            | Position                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Open                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| [MDR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/745/oj/eng) / [IVDR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/746/oj/eng) | Storage, display, export and explanation of what a measurement is; no diagnosis, risk score or treatment advice. Generally not a device under [MDCG 2019-11](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/b45335c5-1679-4c71-a91c-fc7a4d37f12b_en) Rev.1. The trends screen colours values against published, sourced bands; the project's position is that a comparison with a quoted number is not a finding. | written qualification, external opinion |
| DiGA ([§ 139e SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__139e.html))                                          | Not applicable; deliberately not a device                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | none                                    |
| EU AI Act                                                                                                            | Not high-risk while not a device; every answer, on device or hosted, names its provider and model ([Art. 50](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj/eng#art_50))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | none                                    |
| EHDS [2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng)                                                   | [Art. 3](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_3) record access with consent; [Art. 47](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_47) wellness label if marketed as interoperable with EHR systems                                                                                                                                                                                   | label text when marketed                |
| Apple                                                                                                                | [TestFlight](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/test-a-beta-version/invite-external-testers) beta approved for external testers; App Privacy label: health data, not linked, not tracked                                                                                                                                                                                                         | none                                    |

## 5. The test database, and the kinds of result it holds

The demo hub runs on 127 synthetic patients ([Synthea](https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea)) plus hand-seeded
records, in a Neo4j graph that mirrors FHIR R4 and OMOP CDM. On 2026-10-15
it gained the four result types an ePA integrator asks for first ([ADR-059](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-059-the-record-holds-reports-vaccinations-and-the-medication-plan.md)).

| Result type                                                                  | Coding                                                                                               | In the app     | In the test database | How an integrator gets it                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Laboratory, blood and urine                                                  | LOINC, UCUM                                                                                          | yes            | yes                  | [`/api/patient/observations`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/app/api/patient/observations/route.ts), FHIR Bundle |
| Resting ECG, Holter                                                          | LOINC [11524-6](https://tx.fhir.org/r4/CodeSystem/$lookup?system=http://loinc.org&code=11524-6), EC  | yes            | **new**              | `include=all`, DiagnosticReport with Observations                                              |
| Spirometry, CPET, stress test, lactate                                       | LOINC, PF and EC                                                                                     | yes            | planned              |                                                                                                |
| DXA body composition                                                         | LOINC [38269-7](https://tx.fhir.org/r4/CodeSystem/$lookup?system=http://loinc.org&code=38269-7), RAD | yes            | planned              |                                                                                                |
| Continuous glucose monitoring                                                | LOINC [107930-0](https://tx.fhir.org/r4/CodeSystem/$lookup?system=http://loinc.org&code=107930-0)    | yes            | planned              |                                                                                                |
| 24 h blood pressure, device screens                                          | LOINC                                                                                                | yes            | planned              |                                                                                                |
| Wearable weekly means                                                        | LOINC                                                                                                | yes            | yes                  | written by the app ([ADR-057](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-057-klarbefund-sends-weekly-device-means.md))        |
| Imaging reports (X-ray, echo, ultrasound)                                    | LOINC, RAD                                                                                           | no (narrative) | **new**              | `include=all`, DiagnosticReport with conclusion                                                |
| Vaccination record                                                           | CVX                                                                                                  | no             | **new**              | `include=all`, Immunization                                                                    |
| Medication plan ([BMP](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__31a.html)) | ATC, 1-0-1 dosing                                                                                    | no             | **new**              | `include=all`, MedicationStatement                                                             |
| Conditions, medications                                                      | SNOMED CT, [RxNorm](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/rxnorm/index.html)                         | via hub        | yes                  | profile API, [`$everything`](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/patient-operation-everything.html)        |

Candidates after these, by [EHDS Art. 14](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#014.001) category: microbiology, allergy
panels, genetics (laboratory results); pathology, sleep studies, ECG
narratives (reports); patient-reported outcomes and discharge letters
(patient summary, discharge reports). Each is one seed file and one mapper.

Rehearsal: [`bruno/MVHDv2/01 Patient/06 My whole record (Art. 14 categories).bru`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/bruno/MVHDv2/01%20Patient/06%20My%20whole%20record%20%28Art.%2014%20categories%29.bru) pulls the Bundle
with all four result types and fails loudly when one is missing.

## 6. Integration paths

1. **White-label app.** The app as it is, renamed and signed by the insurer,
   with the insurer as operator: privacy notice, DPIA, processor agreement
   for the hosted explanation service ([Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/deployment-types#data-zone-standard), EU data zone, by
   default), and the Apple account. The code stays open source.
2. **Components into an existing ePA or EHR app.** The `Shared` Swift
   package (scanning, the 1751-coding dictionary, provenance, FHIR and OMOP
   writers, consents) has no third-party dependency and is covered by 419
   tests; it drops into an existing iOS app. The same dictionary exists in
   TypeScript ([`services/epa-ingest`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/epa-ingest)) for a server-side path.
3. **Hub-side only.** An insurer's platform reads the record as FHIR R4
   from the hub's API, or runs the ePA ingest CLI against PDFs it already
   holds, without the app.

In every path the insurer owns the data protection roles; the project
supplies the templates and the evidence.

## 7. What is still open

| Item                                            | Who closes it                      |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Independent penetration test, TR-03161 gap list | a BSI-recognised laboratory        |
| Pilot accuracy on real reports                  | the insurer's pilot, with consents |
| Written MDR qualification, external opinion     | regulatory counsel                 |
| DPIA, records of processing, controller role    | the operator                       |
| Profile page sections for the new result types  | the project                        |
| Swift suite in CI (needs workflow rights)       | the repository owner               |

## 8. Verify it yourself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2 && cd MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2
cd clients/ios && swift test                                   # 419 tests, incl. the benchmark and the posture tests
cd ../.. && scripts/security/scan-repo.sh                      # SBOM check, grype, trivy, gitleaks, semgrep, hadolint, npm audit
scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh                         # the live hub from outside, office hours Mon-Fri 05:17-18:13 UTC
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Local "01 Patient"                  # the record as an integrator receives it
```

Documents: [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence), [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment),
[`run-on-mac.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac), [`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report),
[`threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund),
[ADR-059](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-059-the-record-holds-reports-vaccinations-and-the-medication-plan.md).

docs.title: Klarbefund: running the evidence on a Mac
docs.summary: How to reproduce every number in the evidence on a Mac with Xcode.
docs.markdown:
# Klarbefund: running the evidence on a Mac

The Swift package targets macOS 26 and iOS 26, and the scanning and benchmark
tests need Apple's [Vision](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/recognizing-text-in-images) framework, so they run only on a Mac. This is the
checklist for producing the evidence in [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence) and
[`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment) on one.

## Prerequisites

| What                                                                                | Why                                                                                  | Check                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| macOS 26                                                                            | [`Package.swift`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Package.swift) declares `.macOS("26.0")`         | `sw_vers -productVersion`            |
| [Xcode 26](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes), selected | Swift 6 toolchain and the macOS 26 SDK with Vision                                   | `xcode-select -p`, `swift --version` |
| [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) (app only)                        | generates `MeinBefund.xcodeproj` from [`project.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/project.yml) | `brew install xcodegen`              |
| [CodeQL](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/codeql-cli) (optional)            | the static analysis the pre-push hook and CI run                                     | `brew install --cask codeql`         |

Nothing else: the package has no third-party dependencies, so there is nothing
to resolve or download.

## 1. Build and test

```bash
git switch main && git pull --ff-only     # the published state; clone the repository first if you have none
cd clients/ios

swift build                       # Shared, ScanReplay, LabFile, AnalyteParity
swift run AnalyteParity           # the Swift dictionary matches its TypeScript source
KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT=$HOME/Desktop/klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json swift test
```

`swift test` runs the whole suite; the [run of 2026-10-15](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence#run-record) counted 319 tests in 54 suites, and the suite has grown since. The scanning and
benchmark suites render A4 sheets and read them with Vision, serially; on an
Apple-silicon Mac the whole suite took about ten seconds after the build. Two suites measure accuracy:

- [`ExtractionAccuracyTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/ExtractionAccuracyTests.swift): the accuracy measure itself, no Vision needed;
- [`AccuracyBenchmarkTests`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/AccuracyBenchmarkTests.swift): nine scan conditions, zero silent errors required
  under each, counts written to the JSON file named above.

Only that JSON is evidence to publish: synthetic sheets, counts and LOINC codes,
no values. To run one suite: `swift test --filter AccuracyBenchmarkTests`.

## 2. Pilot on real reports (outside the repository)

1. In the app: menu → **Export diagnostics** ([ADR-038](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-038-scan-retained-diagnostics-export.md)), AirDrop the zip to the Mac.
2. Unzip it **outside the repository**, for example `~/Pilot/klarbefund-diagnostics-…`.
3. Next to each `diagnostics.json`, write a `truth.json` from the paper (format
   in [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence#measuring-accuracy)).
4. Run:

   ```bash
   swift run ScanReplay ~/Pilot/klarbefund-diagnostics-2026-10-20 --truth          # per row, no values
   swift run ScanReplay ~/Pilot/klarbefund-diagnostics-2026-10-20 --truth --json   # counts only
   ```

Both tools refuse a path inside [`clients/ios/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios). Get each participant's written
consent before step 1, and delete the export when the counts are taken.

## 3. Optional checks

```bash
Scripts/codeql-swift.sh           # CodeQL on the app, ~15 minutes, exits 1 on a new finding
Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh           # XCUITest on a simulator, demo data only
xcrun simctl launch <udid> red.mabu.meinbefund -MBSelfTest   # 27-check self-test, see clients/ios/README.md
```

The scripts are [`Scripts/codeql-swift.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/codeql-swift.sh) and [`Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh); the self-test is described in the [developer guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-developer-guide#the-self-test) and in [`clients/ios/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/README.md).

## 4. Put the Swift suite into CI

CI today builds only the `Shared` target (`ios-analyte-parity` in
[`.github/workflows/test.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml)); it never runs `swift test`. Add this job after
`ios-analyte-parity` and push it with an account allowed to change workflows:

```yaml
ios-unit-tests:
  name: iOS Unit Tests + Accuracy Benchmark (Swift)
  runs-on: macos-26
  defaults:
    run:
      working-directory: ./clients/ios
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: Swift version
      run: swift --version
    - name: Run unit tests
      env:
        KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json
      run: swift test
    - name: Upload accuracy benchmark
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark
        path: ${{ runner.temp }}/klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json
        if-no-files-found: warn
```

`macos-26` is the [GitHub-hosted macOS 26 runner](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/macos/macos-26-arm64-Readme.md), whose default Xcode is 26.6 as of 2026-11-07; the two actions are [`actions/checkout` v7](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v7.0.0) and [`actions/upload-artifact` v7](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v7.0.0).

The benchmark JSON then becomes a downloadable artifact of every run that
touches `clients/ios/`, which is the reproducible form an outside reviewer can
check.

## 5. What to bring back

- the `swift test` summary line, and any failure in full;
- `klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json`;
- for the pilot, the `--truth --json` output and the number of participants and
  sheets.

docs.title: BSI C5 gap analysis: the EHDS Integration Hub
docs.summary: The hub against the BSI C5:2020 criteria catalogue, measured against the security measures and audits of the secure processing environment in EHDS Art. 73.
docs.markdown:
# BSI C5 gap analysis: the EHDS Integration Hub

**Standard**: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue, [C5:2020](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5) ([BSI page](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Informationen-und-Empfehlungen/Empfehlungen-nach-Angriffszielen/Cloud-Computing/Kriterienkatalog-C5/C5_AktuelleVersion/C5_AktuelleVersion_node.html)). The BSI recommends [C5:2026](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Informationen-und-Empfehlungen/Empfehlungen-nach-Angriffszielen/Cloud-Computing/Kriterienkatalog-C5/C5_2025/C5_2025_node.html) for test periods ending on or after 1 June 2027; this analysis has not been moved to it yet.
**Relevance**: No article of [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng) names C5. [Art. 73(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.001) sets the security measures of the secure processing environment, [Art. 73(3)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.003) requires regular audits of it, including by third parties, and [Art. 73(5)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#073.005) leaves the detailed requirements to implementing acts due by 26 March 2027. C5 is what a public buyer in Germany asks of the cloud underneath ([operational guideline, section 3](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#3-the-bsi-standards-part-by-part)); this analysis uses it as the yardstick for the hub. Earlier versions cited "Art. 50(6)", a number from the 2022 proposal; adopted [Art. 50](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj/eng#art_50) is "Applicability to health data holders" ([numbering](/docs/ehds/article-numbering)).
**Scope**: Demo/MVP assessment. A real C5 report needs an accredited auditor.

Every criterion id links to its page in the C5:2020 PDF, and its title is the catalogue's. Versions up to 2026-03-28 used ids that do not exist in C5:2020 (CCM, IAM, DIP, LOG, INS) and gave OIS, DEV and COS ids titles they do not have; the table at the end lists each change.

---

## Status Legend

| Symbol | Meaning                           |
| ------ | --------------------------------- |
| ✅     | Implemented (demo)                |
| 🟡     | Partially implemented             |
| ⚠️     | Accepted risk for demo            |
| ❌     | Not applicable or not implemented |
| 🔵     | Production roadmap only           |

---

## C5:2020 criteria

### OIS: Organisation of Information Security

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                    | Catalogue title                           | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [OIS-01](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=37) | Information Security Management System    | ⚠️          | No ISMS; the operator needs one ([operational guideline, section 3](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#3-the-bsi-standards-part-by-part))                |
| [OIS-02](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=37) | Information Security Policy               | 🟡          | This document, the [threat model](/docs/security/threat-model-hub) and the [operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline); no policy approved by management |
| [OIS-04](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=39) | Segregation of Duties                     | ⚠️          | One operator; fictional personas only, no real CISO                                                                                            |
| [OIS-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=40) | Risk Management Policy                    | ⚠️          | Not written                                                                                                                                    |
| [OIS-07](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=41) | Application of the Risk Management Policy | 🟡          | STRIDE analyses of the [hub](/docs/security/threat-model-hub) and the [app](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund), without a policy behind them                          |

### AM: Asset Management

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                   | Catalogue title                    | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [AM-01](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=48) | Asset Inventory                    | 🟡          | Assets in the [threat model, section 2](/docs/security/threat-model-hub#2-assets); software components in the [bills of materials](/docs/security/sbom) |
| [AM-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=52) | Asset Classification and Labelling | 🟡          | Each asset has a sensitivity in the [threat model, section 2](/docs/security/threat-model-hub#2-assets); no labelling                                 |

### OPS: Operations

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Catalogue title                                                                | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [OPS-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=63) to [OPS-09](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=65) | Data Backup and Recovery – Concept; – Monitoring; – Regular Testing; – Storage | ⚠️          | PostgreSQL Flexible Server keeps its automatic backups seven days ([`13-postgres-flexible-server.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/13-postgres-flexible-server.sh#L153), [Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/concepts-backup-restore)); no backup of the Neo4j volume; no restore test                                                                |
| [OPS-10](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=65)                                                                                                                                                                 | Logging and Monitoring – Concept                                               | 🟡          | Access and transfer events written by the neo4j-proxy into hash-chained audit records ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)); Keycloak login events kept seven days ([realm](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/keycloak-realm.json#L679-L680)); no SIEM                                                                                                                   |
| [OPS-12](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=67)                                                                                                                                                                 | Logging and Monitoring – Access, Storage and Deletion                          | 🟡          | Retention set in the [audit retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md): 12 months for access events ([`retention.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/src/lib/retention.ts#L8)); a Neo4j administrator can still read and change the records                                                                                                                                                          |
| [OPS-13](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=67)                                                                                                                                                                 | Logging and Monitoring – Identification of Events                              | 🟡          | Azure Monitor alerts when the UI, Keycloak or Neo4j has no replica ([`07-observability.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/07-observability.sh#L31-L48)); no alert on failed sign-ins or unusual access                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [OPS-14](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=68)                                                                                                                                                                 | Logging and Monitoring – Storage of the Logging Data                           | 🟡          | Each audit record carries the hash of its predecessor and [`verifyChain()`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/services/neo4j-proxy/src/audit-chain.ts#L206) reports any change, removal or reordering ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md)); that detects a change, it does not prevent one; no write-once store                                                             |
| [OPS-18](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=70)                                                                                                                                                                 | Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors – Concept                    | 🟡          | [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/SECURITY.md) exists but is still GitHub's unfilled template: it names no reporting address and no response time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [OPS-22](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=72)                                                                                                                                                                 | Testing and Documentation of known Vulnerabilities                             | ✅          | npm audit at high and above before every push ([pre-push hook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml#L287-L292), exceptions time-boxed in [`npm-audit-exceptions.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/npm-audit-exceptions.json)); grype and trivy weekly and on every pull request that changes a lockfile, a Dockerfile or a compose file ([`security-scan.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/security-scan.yml#L14-L37)) |
| [OPS-24](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=74)                                                                                                                                                                 | Separation of Datasets in the Cloud Infrastructure                             | ⚠️          | One resource group, one Neo4j for every participant; the separation a real deployment needs is in the [operational guideline, section 2](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#2-hosting-architecture-from-the-demo-to-an-operable-platform)                                                                                                                                                     |

### IDM: Identity and Access Management

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                    | Catalogue title                                        | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [IDM-01](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=74) | Policy for user accounts and access rights             | 🟡          | The [role matrix](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/api-conventions.md#roles-and-access-control) grants by role; no fine-grained attribute-based access control                                                                                                            |
| [IDM-02](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=76) | Granting and change of user accounts and access rights | ⚠️          | Demo accounts and roles come from a seed file; moving operator accounts to generated passwords in Key Vault is scripted ([#671](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/pull/671)) and not yet run on the live realm                          |
| [IDM-05](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=77) | Regular review of access rights                        | ⚠️          | No review                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [IDM-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=78) | Privileged access rights                               | ⚠️          | The admin role is granted in Keycloak only; the admin console is behind a guard ([`guard-keycloak-console.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh), finding F10 of the [test report](/docs/security/security-test-report#findings)); no PAM system |
| [IDM-09](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=80) | Authentication mechanisms                              | ⚠️          | C5 requires two factors for access to the production environment; the realm configures no one-time password policy and no required action ([`keycloak-realm.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/jad/keycloak-realm.json)), so there is no MFA                                       |

### CRY: Cryptography and Key Management

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                    | Catalogue title                                            | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [CRY-02](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=81) | Encryption of data for transmission (transport encryption) | ✅          | HTTPS at the [Container Apps ingress](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/ingress-overview); checked from outside: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 refused, 1.2 and 1.3 offered, HSTS set ([test report, results](/docs/security/security-test-report#results), [`next.config.js`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/next.config.js#L99-L102)). Plain HTTP on localhost for development                                                                                                                                       |
| [CRY-03](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=82) | Encryption of sensitive data for storage                   | 🟡          | On Azure, the Flexible Server and Azure Files (Neo4j's volume, [ADR-017](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-017-persistent-storage-aca.md)) are encrypted at rest with Microsoft-managed keys ([Postgres](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/concepts-data-encryption), [Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-service-encryption)); C5 asks for keys known only to the customer, so customer-managed keys are open; local Docker volumes are not encrypted |
| [CRY-04](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=83) | Secure key management                                      | 🟡          | Operator secrets are Key Vault references ([ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md)); participant keys in Vault ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)); certificates managed by Container Apps; no rotation schedule, no HSM                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### COS: Communication Security

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                    | Catalogue title                                                  | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [COS-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=86) | Segregation of data traffic in jointly used network environments | ⚠️          | Only the hub and Keycloak have public ingress; the rest is on internal ingress in one Container Apps environment, except the PostgreSQL Flexible Server, which sits outside it on a public endpoint whose firewall admits any Azure service, an accepted risk ([threat model, I-02 and I-05](/docs/security/threat-model-hub#information-disclosure)); no private endpoints |

### DEV: Procurement, Development and Modification of Information Systems

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                    | Catalogue title                                                 | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [DEV-01](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=91) | Policies for the development/procurement of information systems | 🟡          | [`code-style.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/code-style.md), [`testing.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.claude/rules/testing.md) and the [SDLC](/docs/developer/sdlc); not based on a recognised secure development standard                                                                                                                                 |
| [DEV-03](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=92) | Policies for changes to information systems                     | ✅          | Every change is a pull request through the gates in [`quality-gates.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/quality-gates.md) and the [SDLC](/docs/developer/sdlc)                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [DEV-06](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=94) | Testing changes                                                 | ✅          | Unit suites on every push; the security journeys SEC-01 to SEC-10 ([`01-auth-protection.spec.ts`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/ui/__tests__/e2e/security/01-auth-protection.spec.ts)) with the other end-to-end suites once a night when main changed ([ADR-074](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-074-e2e-and-compliance-suites-run-nightly-when-main-changed.md)) |
| [DEV-08](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=95) | Version Control                                                 | ✅          | Git history; images tagged with the commit they were built from; a Container Apps [revision](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/revisions) can be reactivated                                                                                                                                      |
| [DEV-09](https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/CloudComputing/ComplianceControlsCatalogue/2020/C5_2020.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&v=5#page=95) | Approvals for provision in the production environment           | 🟡          | Deploys run on a push to `main`, images tagged with the commit ([`deploy-azure.yml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy-azure.yml#L3-L6)); no separate release approval                                                                                                                                                    |

### SSO: Control and Monitoring of Service Providers and Suppliers

| Criterion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Catalogue title                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Demo Status | Where the hub stands                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
